ArkData.LiteResultSet.getRowsData: Gets a chosen number of rows of data starting from a given position in a query result. Use it to page through or load a batch of records from a database query.
ArkData.LiteResultSet.getString: Reads the value in a chosen column of the current row as text. Use it to read a stored text or number field from a database query result.
ArkData.LiteResultSet.getValue: Gets the value of a chosen column in the current row in its own data type. Use it to read a field from a database query result without converting its type.
ArkData.LiteResultSet.goToNextRow: Moves to the next row of a query result. Use it to step through each record returned by a database query.
ArkData.LiteResultSet.isColumnNull: Checks whether the value in a chosen column of the current row is null. Use it to tell whether a database field is empty before reading it.
ArkData.Preferences.clear: Removes all stored data from this preferences instance. Use it to wipe saved settings or user preferences.
ArkData.Preferences.clearSync: Clears all stored data in a preferences instance. Use it to wipe saved settings or reset an app's stored preferences.
ArkData.Preferences.delete: Deletes one stored key-value pair from a preferences instance. Use it to remove a saved setting you no longer need.
ArkData.Preferences.deleteSync: Deletes one stored key-value pair from a preferences instance right away. Use it to remove a saved setting you no longer need.
ArkData.Preferences.flush: Saves the data held in a preferences instance to its persistent file. Use it to make sure changed settings are kept after the app closes.
ArkData.Preferences.flushSync: Saves the data held in a preferences instance to its persistent file right away. Use it to make sure changed settings are kept after the app closes.
ArkData.Preferences.getAll: Gets all stored key-value pairs from a preferences instance. Use it to read back every saved setting at once.
ArkData.Preferences.getAllSync: Gets all stored key-value pairs at once. Use it to read everything saved in the app's settings store.
ArkData.Preferences.getSync: Gets the stored value for a key, or a default if it is missing. Use it to read a saved setting such as a username or theme choice.
ArkData.Preferences.has: Checks whether a given key exists in the stored settings. Use it to see if a preference like a saved login has been set.
ArkData.Preferences.hasSync: Checks right away whether a given key exists in the stored settings. Use it to see if a preference like a saved login has been set.
ArkData.Preferences.off: Stops listening for changes to stored settings. Use it to stop reacting when a saved preference is updated.
ArkData.Preferences.offChange: Stops an existing watcher from being notified about changes to stored settings. Use it to stop reacting when a saved preference is updated.
ArkData.Preferences.offDataChange: Stops watching for changes to specific stored settings. Use it when you no longer need to be notified that those settings were updated.
ArkData.Preferences.offMultiProcessChang: Stops watching for settings changes made by other processes. Use it to stop being notified when another process updates the shared settings.
ArkData.Preferences.on: Watches for settings changes across processes and runs your callback when any process saves changes. Use it to keep multiple processes in sync when they share the same settings.
ArkData.Preferences.onChange: Watches for changes to the stored settings and runs your callback when they change. Use it to react whenever a saved setting is updated.
ArkData.Preferences.onDataChange: Watches for changes to specific stored settings and runs your callback with the new values. Use it to react when particular settings you care about are updated.
ArkData.Preferences.onMultiProcessChange: Watches for settings changes made by other processes and runs your callback when they happen. Use it to stay informed when another process updates the shared settings.
ArkData.Preferences.put: Writes a value under a key in stored preferences, to be saved later. Use it to remember a setting or small piece of data for next time.
ArkData.Preferences.putSync: Writes a value under a key in stored preferences right away, to be saved later. Use it to remember a setting or small piece of data for next time.
ArkData.Query.and: Combines query conditions so that all of them must match. Use it to narrow a search to items meeting every chosen condition.
ArkData.Query.beginGroup: Starts a grouped set of query conditions with a left parenthesis. Use it to group conditions so they are matched together.
ArkData.Query.deviceId: Sets the device ID as the key prefix for a query. Use it to search only the data belonging to a particular device.
ArkData.Query.endGroup: Closes a grouped set of query conditions with a right parenthesis. Use it to finish a condition group started earlier in a query.
ArkData.Query.equalTo: Finds records whose chosen field matches an exact value. Use it to look up items by a specific name, number, or true/false setting.
ArkData.Query.getSqlLike: Gives back the query statement built so far. Use it to see or reuse the search you have set up.
ArkData.Query.greaterThan: Finds records whose chosen field is larger than a given value. Use it to pick out items above a certain number, like scores or prices.
ArkData.Query.greaterThanOrEqualTo: Finds records whose chosen field is at least a given value. Use it to pick out items at or above a certain number, like dates or amounts.
ArkData.Query.inNumber: Finds records whose chosen field is one of several given numbers. Use it to look up items matching any number in a list, like selected IDs.
ArkData.Query.inString: Finds records whose chosen field is one of several given words. Use it to look up items matching any name in a list, like chosen tags.
ArkData.Query.isNotNull: Finds records where the given field has a value that is not empty. Use it to filter out entries missing that field.
ArkData.Query.isNull: Finds records where the given field is empty. Use it to list entries that have no value set for that field.
ArkData.Query.lessThan: Finds records where the given field is smaller than a value. Use it to filter results below a chosen number or text.
ArkData.Query.lessThanOrEqualTo: Finds records where the given field is smaller than or equal to a value. Use it to filter results up to a chosen number or text.
ArkData.Query.like: Builds a query that finds records whose field is similar to a given string. Use it to search stored data for matching text.
ArkData.Query.limit: Sets how many results to return and where to start. Use it to page through a long list of results.
ArkData.Query.notEqualTo: Finds records where the given field does not equal a value. Use it to exclude entries matching a value you do not want.
ArkData.Query.notInNumber: Finds records whose chosen field is not one of the given numbers. Use it to filter out items by a numeric value, such as excluding certain IDs or ages.
ArkData.Query.notInString: Finds records whose chosen field is not one of the given strings. Use it to filter out items by a text value, such as excluding certain names or categories.
ArkData.Query.or: Combines query conditions so records matching any of them are returned. Use it to search for items that meet one condition or another, like finding entries from either of two groups.
ArkData.Query.orderByAsc: Sorts query results in ascending order by a chosen field. Use it to list items from smallest to largest, such as sorting by price or date.
ArkData.Query.orderByDesc: Sorts query results in descending order by a chosen field. Use it to list items from largest to smallest, such as showing the newest or highest first.
ArkData.Query.prefixKey: Finds records whose key starts with a given prefix. Use it to group or list items that share a common key beginning, like all entries under one category.
ArkData.Query.reset: Clears all conditions set on a query so it starts fresh. Use it to reuse the same query object for a new search without old filters.
ArkData.Query.setSuggestIndex: Sets an index to be preferred when running a query. Use it to make a search faster by pointing it at the best index.
ArkData.Query.unlike: Builds a query that finds records whose field is not similar to a given string. Use it to filter out stored data matching unwanted text.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.and: Adds an AND condition to combine filters in a database query. Use it to require that two or more conditions are all true when searching records.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.beginWrap: Adds a left parenthesis to group conditions in a database query. Use it to control the order in which filters are combined.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.beginsWith: Filters records whose column value starts with the given text. Use it to find entries beginning with a certain word or letter.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.between: Filters records whose column value falls within a range, including both ends. Use it to find entries between a low and high value, such as a date or price range.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.contains: Finds records whose column contains a given piece of text. Use it to search a database for entries matching part of a word or phrase.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.distinct: Filters out duplicate records so each result appears only once. Use it to get a list of unique entries from a database.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.endWrap: Adds a closing right parenthesis to a database search condition. Use it to group search conditions together when building a query.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.endsWith: Finds records whose column ends with a given piece of text. Use it to search a database for entries finishing with certain characters.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.equalTo: Finds records whose column exactly matches a given value. Use it to look up a specific entry in a database.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.glob: Finds records whose column matches a pattern, where * stands for any characters and ? for one. Use it to search a database with wildcard patterns.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.greaterThan: Finds records in a column whose value is greater than a given value. Use it to filter a database query, such as finding items priced above a certain amount.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.greaterThanOrEqual: Finds records in a column whose value is greater than or equal to a given value. Use it to filter a database query, such as finding scores at or above a passing mark.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.groupBy: Groups query results by the columns you name. Use it to combine rows that share the same value, such as totalling sales per store.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.having: Filters grouped data so only groups meeting a condition remain. Use it with grouping to keep only groups that match, such as stores with sales above a target.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.in: Finds records in a column whose value falls within a given set of values. Use it to filter a query, such as finding items in a chosen list of categories.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.inAllDevices: Targets all remote devices on the network when syncing a distributed database. Use it to sync data across every device available on the network.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.inDevices: Sets which remote devices to connect to on the network when syncing a distributed database. Use it to pick the devices you want to share or sync data with.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.inValues: Matches records where a chosen column's value falls within a given set of values. Use it to find rows whose field matches any value in your list.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.indexedBy: Specifies the index column to use when searching a database table. Use it to make lookups on a particular column faster.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.isNotNull: Finds records in a chosen column that are not empty. Use it to list rows that actually have a value in that column.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.isNull: Finds records in a chosen column that are empty. Use it to list rows missing a value in that column.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.lessThan: Finds records in a chosen column that are less than a given value. Use it to list rows below a number, date, or other limit.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.lessThanOrEqualTo: Finds records in a chosen column whose value is less than or equal to a given value. Use it to filter a database search, for example to list items priced at or below a set amount.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.like: Finds records in a chosen column whose value is similar to a given pattern, using % for any characters and _ for one character. Use it to search a database by partial text, such as finding names that start with certain letters.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.limitAs: Limits how many records a database search returns. Use it to cap results, for example to show only the first few matching entries.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notBetween: Finds records in a chosen column that fall outside a given range, excluding the minimum and maximum values. Use it to filter a database search to items outside a price or date range.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notContains: Finds records in a chosen column that do not contain a given value. Use it to filter a database search, for example to list entries missing a certain word.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notEqualTo: Finds records in a chosen column whose value is not equal to a given value. Use it to filter a database search, for example to list items other than a specific one.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notIn: Finds records whose column value is not among the values you list. Use it to filter out rows matching a set of values, like excluding certain IDs from results.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notInValues: Matches records where the specified field's value falls outside the given set of values. Use it to leave out rows whose column matches any value in your list.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.notLike: Finds records whose column value is not similar to a given pattern, using wildcards like % and _. Use it to exclude rows whose text does not match a partial search.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.offsetAs: Sets where in the query results to start returning rows, used together with a limit. Use it to skip the first rows and show the next page of results.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.or: Combines conditions so records matching either one are found. Use it to search for rows that meet any of several conditions.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.orderByAsc: Sorts the found records by a column in ascending order. Use it to list results from smallest to largest, such as by name or date.
ArkData.RdbPredicates.orderByDesc: Sorts database records by a chosen column in descending order. Use it to list items from highest to lowest, such as newest or largest first.
ArkData.RdbStore.attach: Attaches another database file to the database currently in use. Use it to work with data spread across multiple database files at once.
ArkData.RdbStore.backup: Saves a copy of the database under a name you choose. Use it to keep a backup so data can be restored later.
ArkData.RdbStore.batchInsert: Inserts many rows of data into a table at once. Use it to add a large batch of records quickly instead of one by one.
ArkData.RdbStore.batchInsertSync: Inserts many rows of data into a table at once and returns how many were added. Use it to add a large batch of records in one go.
ArkData.RdbStore.batchInsertWithConflict: Inserts many rows into a table at once, choosing how to handle rows that clash with existing ones. Use it to bulk-add records while deciding what happens on duplicates.
Inserts many rows of data into a table at once, resolving conflicts as specified, and returns how many rows were inserted. Use it to save a batch of records to a database in one go.
ArkData.RdbStore.batchInsertWithReturnin: Inserts many rows of data into a table at once and returns the changed fields as a result set. Use it to save a batch of records and see exactly what was written.
Inserts many rows of data into a table at once and returns the changed fields as a result set. Use it to save a batch of records and see exactly what was written.
ArkData.RdbStore.beginTrans: Begins a transaction before running SQL statements and returns the transaction ID. Use it to group several database changes so they all succeed or all fail together.
ArkData.RdbStore.beginTransaction: Starts a transaction before running SQL statements. Use it to group several database changes so they all succeed or all fail together.
ArkData.RdbStore.cleanDeviceDirtyData: Deletes data that was removed during cross-device sync, either all of it or only entries older than a given cursor. Use it to tidy up leftover records after syncing between devices.
ArkData.RdbStore.cleanDirtyData: Cleans up data that was deleted in the cloud, optionally only records before a given position. Use it to remove leftover deleted records from a table.
ArkData.RdbStore.close: Closes the database and all open result sets. Use it to release the database when you are done with it.
ArkData.RdbStore.cloudSync: Syncs the database data to the cloud. Use it to back up or share your data online.
ArkData.RdbStore.cloudSyncEx: Syncs the database data to the cloud using a configuration. Use it to back up or share your data online.
ArkData.RdbStore.commit: Commits the SQL you have executed. Use it to save changes made during a transaction.
ArkData.RdbStore.createTransaction: Creates a transaction instance and begins it. Use it to group database changes so they can be saved or undone together.
ArkData.RdbStore.delete: Deletes data from the database based on conditions. Use it to remove rows that match what you specify.
ArkData.RdbStore.deleteSync: Deletes rows from a database table that match given conditions, and reports how many rows were removed. Use it to remove stored records such as old messages or saved items.
ArkData.RdbStore.deleteWithReturning: Deletes rows matching given conditions and returns the changed data along with the number of rows removed. Use it to delete records and see exactly what was deleted.
ArkData.RdbStore.deleteWithReturningSync: Deletes rows matching given conditions and returns the changed data along with the number of rows removed. Use it to delete records and see exactly what was deleted.
ArkData.RdbStore.detach: Detaches a previously attached database from the current database and reports how many databases remain attached. Use it to close off a linked database when you are done with it.
ArkData.RdbStore.emit: Notifies registered observers that the data at a given address has changed. Use it to tell listeners that stored data was updated so they can refresh.
ArkData.RdbStore.execute: Runs a SQL statement with given parameter values and returns a result value. Use it to run custom database commands such as inserting or updating stored records.
ArkData.RdbStore.executeSql: Runs an SQL statement with given arguments that returns no value. Use it to change stored data, such as adding, updating, or deleting records.
ArkData.RdbStore.executeSync: Runs an SQL statement with given parameters and returns a value right away. Use it to change or query stored data and get the result immediately.
ArkData.RdbStore.getModifyTime: Gets the time rows were last changed, based on their primary keys. Use it to check when a saved record was last updated.
ArkData.RdbStore.insert: Adds one row of data into a table. Use it to save a new record, such as a contact or note, into storage.
ArkData.RdbStore.insertSync: Adds one row of data into a table and returns the new row ID right away. Use it to save a new record and get its ID immediately.
ArkData.RdbStore.lockCloudContainer: Locks the cloud container before a manual cloud sync and reports how long the lock lasts. Use it to hold the cloud data steady while syncing it yourself.
ArkData.RdbStore.lockRow: Locks rows in the database that match a given condition. Use it to stop other changes to selected records while you work on them.
ArkData.RdbStore.obtainDistributedTableN: Gets the distributed table name for a remote device from a local table name, so you can query that device's data. Use it when reading another device's shared database table.
ArkData.RdbStore.off: Stops an observer from receiving data change events from the database. Use it when you no longer want updates about data changes.
ArkData.RdbStore.offAutoSyncProgress: Stops receiving progress updates for automatic database synchronization. Use it when you no longer want sync progress reports.
ArkData.RdbStore.offDataChange: Removes an observer so it no longer receives data change notifications of the given type. Use it to stop watching for database changes.
ArkData.RdbStore.offPerfStat: Stops receiving SQL performance statistics. Use it when you no longer want performance measurements for database statements.
ArkData.RdbStore.offSqliteErrorOccurred: Stops receiving SQL execution error logs. Use it when you no longer want to be notified about database errors.
ArkData.RdbStore.offStatistics: Stops receiving SQL statistics updates. Use it to stop monitoring how long database queries take.
ArkData.RdbStore.on: Listens for changes to data in a shared database. Use it to react when data changes on another device.
ArkData.RdbStore.onAutoSyncProgress: Reports the progress of automatic database synchronization. Use it to show how far syncing data is.
ArkData.RdbStore.onDataChange: Listens for changes to data in a shared database. Use it to react when data changes on another device.
ArkData.RdbStore.onPerfStat: Listens for SQL performance statistics. Use it to monitor how fast database queries run.
ArkData.RdbStore.onSqliteErrorOccurred: Listens for database execution error logs. Use it to catch and review database errors.
ArkData.RdbStore.onStatistics: Subscribes to SQL execution statistics for a database. Use it to monitor how queries perform while managing stored data.
ArkData.RdbStore.query: Queries data from a database using specified conditions. Use it to look up records that match what you are searching for.
ArkData.RdbStore.queryByStep: Queries data in a database step by step using a SQL statement. Use it to read through large result sets one portion at a time.
ArkData.RdbStore.queryLockedRow: Queries locked data in a database based on specified conditions. Use it to find rows currently locked while managing stored data.
ArkData.RdbStore.querySharingResource: Gets the sharing resource for the rows that match your query conditions. Use it to find the shared items you are looking for.
ArkData.RdbStore.querySql: Queries data using a specified SQL statement. Use it to look up records with a custom database query.
ArkData.RdbStore.querySqlSync: Queries data in a database using a SQL statement and returns the result immediately. Use it to look up records without waiting for a callback.
ArkData.RdbStore.querySqlWithoutRowCount: Runs an SQL query on the database and returns the matching rows without counting them, which is faster than a normal query. Use it to fetch stored records quickly when you do not need the total number of results.

Runs an SQL query on the database and returns the matching rows without counting them, doing the work immediately. Use it to fetch stored records quickly when you do not need the total number of results.
ArkData.RdbStore.querySync: Searches the database for rows matching given conditions and returns the matching columns right away. Use it to look up stored records such as contacts or saved items.
ArkData.RdbStore.queryWithoutRowCount: Searches the database for rows matching given conditions and returns them without counting the total. Use it to fetch stored records when you do not need the number of results.
ArkData.RdbStore.queryWithoutRowCountSyn: Searches the database for rows matching given conditions and returns them without counting the total, doing the work immediately. Use it to fetch stored records when you do not need the number of results.
ArkData.RdbStore.rekey: Changes the key used to encrypt the database. Use it to replace or update the password protecting stored data.
ArkData.RdbStore.rekeyEx: Changes the encryption settings of the database. Use it to update the password or encryption parameters protecting stored data.
ArkData.RdbStore.remoteQuery: Queries data on a specified remote device before syncing it. Use it to look up records held on another device before transferring them.
ArkData.RdbStore.restore: Restores a database from a saved database file. Use it to bring back data from a backup copy.
ArkData.RdbStore.retainDeviceData: Removes remote data belonging to distributed tables, optionally keeping data for specified devices. Use it to clear out other devices' copies of shared data.
ArkData.RdbStore.rollBack: Rolls back SQL statements that have already been executed. Use it to undo recent database changes.
ArkData.RdbStore.rollback: Rolls back the SQL statements run in a transaction, identified by its transaction ID. Use it to undo changes made during a transaction.
ArkData.RdbStore.setDistributedTables: Sets which tables are shared across devices. Use it to make chosen data available for syncing between devices.
ArkData.RdbStore.setLocale: Sets the language used for sorting and comparing text in the database. Use it when you need text sorted correctly for a language, such as Chinese.
ArkData.RdbStore.stopCloudSync: Stops syncing the database with the cloud. Use it to pause cloud backup or sync of your app's data.
ArkData.RdbStore.sync: Sends or fetches data between devices, returning each device's sync status. Use it to share or back up your app's data across a user's devices.
ArkData.RdbStore.syncEx: Syncs data between devices and reports detailed results per device. Use it to share or back up your app's data across a user's devices.
ArkData.RdbStore.unlockCloudContainer: Unlocks the cloud container. Use it to release the cloud data after you finish a manual cloud sync.
ArkData.RdbStore.unlockRow: Unlocks rows in the database that match a condition. Use it to release rows you previously locked while editing them.
ArkData.RdbStore.update: Changes existing rows in the database that match a condition, returning how many were updated. Use it to edit saved records, such as updating a contact's details.
ArkData.RdbStore.updateDistributedInfo: Updates the log of a distributed table for the rows matching your conditions and reports how many logs changed. Use it to keep the sync record of shared data up to date.
ArkData.RdbStore.updateSync: Updates rows in a database table that match a given condition, returning how many rows changed. Use it to edit saved records, such as changing a contact's phone number.
ArkData.RdbStore.updateWithReturning: Updates matching rows in a database table and gives back the changed data along with the number of rows changed. Use it to edit saved records and see exactly what was modified.
ArkData.RdbStore.updateWithReturningSync: Updates matching rows in a database table and gives back the changed data along with the number of rows changed. Use it to edit saved records and see exactly what was modified.
ArkData.ResultSet.close: Closes a query result set and frees its memory. Use it after you finish reading search results to avoid memory leaks.
ArkData.ResultSet.getAsset: Reads a file or media value from a column in the current result row. Use it to get a saved photo or attachment from a database record.
ArkData.ResultSet.getAssets: Reads a group of file or media values from a column in the current result row. Use it to get several saved photos or attachments from a database record.
ArkData.ResultSet.getBlob: Gets a column's value from the current row as a byte array, converting numbers or text if needed. Use it to read stored binary data such as an image or file from a database query result.
ArkData.ResultSet.getColumnIndex: Finds a column's position number from its name in a query result. Use it to locate the right column before reading its value.
ArkData.ResultSet.getColumnName: Gets a column's name from its position number in a query result. Use it to see what a column is called when you only know its index.
ArkData.ResultSet.getColumnNames: Lists the names of all columns in a query result, in order. Use it to see what fields are available in the data you queried.
ArkData.ResultSet.getColumnType: Tells you the data type of a column, found by its index or name. Use it to check whether a column holds numbers, text, or binary data before reading it.
ArkData.ResultSet.getColumnTypeSync: Tells you the data type of a column, found by its index or name, returning the answer right away. Use it to check whether a column holds numbers, text, or binary data before reading it.
ArkData.ResultSet.getCurrentRowData: Gets the values of every column in the current row of a query result. Use it to read a full record, such as all details of one saved contact or item.
ArkData.ResultSet.getDouble: Reads a column in the current row as a decimal number, giving 0.0 when the column is empty. Use it to read stored amounts, prices, or measurements from a query result.
ArkData.ResultSet.getFloat32Array: Reads a column in the current row as a list of decimal numbers. Use it to pull numeric data out of a database query result.
ArkData.ResultSet.getLong: Reads a column in the current row as a whole number, giving 0 when the column is empty. Use it to read stored counts, IDs, or other whole-number values from a query result.
ArkData.ResultSet.getRow: Gets the current row of a query result as a set of column values. Use it to read one record, such as a single saved note or entry, from a query result.
ArkData.ResultSet.getRows: Gets up to a chosen number of rows from a query result. Use it to load a batch of records, such as a page of saved items, at once.
ArkData.ResultSet.getRowsData: Gets a chosen number of rows starting from a given position in a query result. Use it to load a batch of records, such as a page of saved items, from a specific point.
ArkData.ResultSet.getSendableRow: Gets the current row's data in a form that can be passed between threads. Use it to move a database row safely to another thread.
ArkData.ResultSet.getString: Reads a column's value from the current row as text. Use it to show a stored value, such as a name or note, as a string.
ArkData.ResultSet.getValue: Reads a column's value from the current row in its own type. Use it to get a stored value such as a number or text without converting it.
ArkData.ResultSet.goTo: Moves the result pointer forward or backward by a given number of rows. Use it to jump to another row when browsing query results.
ArkData.ResultSet.goToFirstRow: Moves to the first row of the result set. Use it to start reading results from the beginning.
ArkData.ResultSet.goToLastRow: Moves to the last row of the result set. Use it to jump to the end of the results.
ArkData.ResultSet.goToNextRow: Moves to the next row in a query result set. Use it to step through rows one by one when reading data from a database.
ArkData.ResultSet.goToPreviousRow: Moves to the previous row in a query result set. Use it to step back through rows when reading data from a database.
ArkData.ResultSet.goToRow: Moves to a specified row in a query result set. Use it to jump directly to a particular row when reading data from a database.
ArkData.ResultSet.isColumnNull: Checks whether the value in a specified column is null. Use it to tell empty values from real data when reading database rows.
ArkData.ShareCenter.changeConfirmation: Changes whether a share invitation is accepted or declined. Use it to update the status of a shared item you were invited to.
ArkData.ShareCenter.changePrivilege: Changes what people you share with are allowed to do with the shared data. Use it to give or take away access for participants in a share.
ArkData.ShareCenter.confirmInvitation: Accepts or declines an invitation to a share using its invitation code. Use it to join a shared item someone invited you to.
ArkData.ShareCenter.exit: Leaves a device-cloud share. Use it to stop sharing an item you previously shared.
ArkData.ShareCenter.queryParticipants: Lists the people taking part in a share. Use it to see who you are sharing an item with.
ArkData.ShareCenter.queryParticipantsByI: Finds the people taking part in a share using its invitation code. Use it to see who is in a shared item before sharing or unsharing.
ArkData.ShareCenter.share: Shares a resource with chosen people. Use it to give others access to a shared item.
ArkData.ShareCenter.unshare: Stops sharing a resource with chosen people. Use it to remove someone's access to a shared item.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.backup: Backs up a distributed key-value store to a file. Use it to save a copy of your stored data so it can be restored later.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.backupEx: Backs up a database using a backup configuration. Use it to save a copy of your stored data with chosen backup settings.

ArkData.SingleKVStore.delete: Deletes one key-value pair from the store by its key. Use it to remove a stored item you no longer need.

ArkData.SingleKVStore.getEntries: Gets the key-value pairs that match a query. Use it to look up stored items, for example to list saved settings or records.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.getResultSet: Gets a result set of the entries matching a query. Use it to browse or step through matching stored data.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.getResultSize: Counts how many entries match a query. Use it to show how many matching items are stored.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.getSecurityLevel: Reports the security level of this store. Use it to check how protected the stored data is before saving sensitive information.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.off: Stops listening for data changes or sync completion events. Use it to stop reacting when stored data changes or finishes syncing.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.offDataChange: Stops listening for changes to data in a single key-value store. Use it when you no longer want to be notified about data updates.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.offSyncComplete: Stops receiving notifications when data syncing between devices finishes. Use it to stop being told when cross-device data sync is done.

ArkData.SingleKVStore.onDataChange: Starts listening for changes to data in a single key-value store. Use it to be notified when data in the store changes.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.onSyncComplete: Starts receiving notifications when data syncing between devices finishes. Use it to know when cross-device data sync is done.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.put: Adds a key-value pair to a single key-value store. Use it to save a value under a key.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.putBatch: Inserts many key-value pairs into the store at once. Use it to save a batch of settings or records together.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.putValuesBuckets: Writes a batch of values into a single key-value database. Use it to save several records at once.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.rekey: Changes the key that encrypts the database. Use it to update the password protecting stored data.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.removeDeviceData: Deletes the data belonging to a specific device. Use it to clear another device's synced data from this store.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.restore: Restores the store from a database file. Use it to bring back saved data from a backup file.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.restoreEx: Restores the database using a backup configuration. Use it to recover data from a chosen backup.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.rollback: Cancels the current transaction and undoes its changes. Use it to discard edits that should not be saved.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.setSyncParam: Sets the default delay before data is synced between devices. Use it to control how long syncing waits before starting.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.setSyncRange: Sets which data labels sync between the local device and remote devices. Use it to limit syncing to chosen groups of data.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.startTransaction: Starts a transaction in the single key-value store. Use it to group several data changes so they all succeed or fail together.
ArkData.SingleKVStore.sync: Starts syncing data to other devices right away. Use it to send your saved data to another device.
ArkData.Storage.clear: Clears all data stored in this storage object. Use it to wipe saved settings or data when resetting.
ArkData.Storage.clearSync: Clears all data stored in this storage object immediately. Use it to wipe saved settings or data when resetting.

ArkData.Storage.deleteSync: Removes the stored value for a given key from the storage object right away. Use it to clear saved settings or data you no longer need.

ArkData.Storage.flushSync: Saves your changes to the storage object and writes them to the file right away. Use it to make sure saved settings or data are kept permanently.
ArkData.Storage.getSync: Reads the value saved under a key, returning a default if it is missing or the wrong type. Use it to look up a saved setting or preference.
ArkData.Storage.has: Checks whether stored data exists under a given key. Use it to test if a saved value is present before reading it.
ArkData.Storage.hasSync: Checks whether a value is saved under a given key. Use it to see if a setting or piece of data already exists before reading it.
ArkData.Storage.off: Stops listening for changes to stored data. Use it when you no longer need to be told that a saved value has changed.
ArkData.Storage.on: Listens for changes to stored data and tells you when a value you follow is updated. Use it to keep a screen or setting in sync after data is saved.
ArkData.Storage.put: Saves a number, text, or true/false value under a key in a storage file. Use it to remember a setting or small piece of data for later.
ArkData.Storage.putSync: Saves a number, text, or true/false value under a key in a storage file right away. Use it to remember a setting or small piece of data for later.
ArkData.TextEmbedding.getEmbedding: Turns text into a list of numbers that represents its meaning, in Chinese or English. Use it to compare or search text by meaning.

ArkData.Transaction.deleteWithReturningS: Deletes rows matching given conditions and gives back the deleted data. Use it to remove stored records and see exactly what was removed.

ArkData.Transaction.insertSync: Adds one row of data into a table and returns its row ID right away. Use it to save a new record, such as a contact or note, inside a database transaction.

ArkData.Transaction.update: Updates rows in a database table that match given conditions and reports how many rows changed. Use it to edit stored records, such as changing a saved contact's details.
ArkData.Transaction.updateSync: Updates rows in a database table that match given conditions and returns how many rows changed right away. Use it to edit stored records, such as changing a saved contact's details.

ArkData.Transaction.updateWithReturningS: Updates matching rows in a database table and returns the affected data immediately. Use it to edit stored records and see the updated results, such as changing a saved contact's details.

ArkData.UnifiedData.addRecord: Adds a data record to a set of data records. Use it to build up a collection of data records.

ArkData.UnifiedRecord.getType: Gets the data type of a record, such as text or image. Use it to tell what kind of content a record holds before working with it.
ArkData.UnifiedRecord.getTypes: Gets all the data types present in a data record. Use it to list every kind of content a shared item contains.
ArkData.UnifiedRecord.getValue: Gets the value stored in a data record, such as its text, image, or HTML content. Use it to read what a shared record actually contains.

ArkData.relationalStore.isVectorSupporte: Checks whether the system supports vector stores. Use it to find out if vector data can be stored in a local database.

ArkData.sharing.queryParticipantsByInvit: Lists the participants based on a sharing invitation code. Use it to see who is taking part in a share you were invited to.

ArkData.sharing.unshare: Stops sharing data with chosen participants using a shared resource ID. Use it to take back access to your data from other people.
