ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawImageRectWithSr: Draws part of an image onto a chosen area of the canvas. Use it to show a cropped piece of a picture, like a sprite from a sprite sheet.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawLine: Draws a straight line from one point to another. Use it to draw lines, borders, or simple shapes on a canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawNestedRoundRect: Draws two rounded rectangles, one inside the other. Use it to draw a rounded frame or border around a rounded shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawOval: Draws an oval inside a given rectangle. Use it to draw circles or ellipses on a canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawPath: Draws a custom path made of outlines that can be open or closed. Use it to draw freeform shapes, icons, or signatures.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawPixelMapMesh: Draws an image stretched over a grid of mesh points. Use it to warp or distort a picture, like a flag waving.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawPoint: Draws a single point at the given x and y coordinates. Use it to plot a dot on a drawing or chart.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawPoints: Draws a group of points, line segments, or polygons on the canvas in the chosen drawing mode. Use it to plot many dots or connect them into lines or shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawRect: Draws a rectangle, filled black by default. Use it to draw a rectangular shape or box on the canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawRegion: Draws a region on the canvas. Use it to draw a defined area or shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawRoundRect: Draws a rounded rectangle. Use it to draw a rectangle with rounded corners, such as a button or card.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawShadow: Draws a spot shadow and outlines an ambient shadow along a given path. Use it to add realistic shadows to shapes or objects.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawSingleCharacter: Draws one character at a given position using a font, falling back to the system typeface if needed. Use it to place a single letter or symbol on a drawing.
Draws one character at a given position using a font and chosen font features. Use it to place a single letter or symbol with specific typographic styling.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawTextBlob: Draws a text blob at a given position; characters unsupported by the blob's typeface are skipped. Use it to render a prepared block of text on a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.drawVertices: Draws a triangle mesh from an array of vertices. Use it to render custom shapes or textured surfaces built from triangles.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.getHeight: Gets the height of the canvas. Use it to find how tall the drawing area is.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.getLocalClipBounds: Gets the bounds of the canvas cropping region. Use it to find the visible area of a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.getSaveCount: Tells you how many saved canvas states are currently on the stack. Use it to check how many times you have saved the drawing state before restoring.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.getTotalMatrix: Gives you the canvas transformation matrix. Use it to find out how the canvas is currently scaled, rotated, or moved.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.getWidth: Gives you the width of the canvas. Use it to find out how wide the drawing area is.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.isClipEmpty: Tells you whether the drawable region is empty after clipping. Use it to check if anything can still be drawn.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.isOpaque: Tells you whether the current layer drawn to the device is opaque. Use it to check if the drawing is fully solid.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.quickRejectPath: Tells you whether a path does not intersect the canvas area. Use it to skip drawing shapes that are off the canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.quickRejectRect: Checks whether a rectangle lies completely outside the canvas area, including its boundaries. Use it to skip drawing shapes that are off-screen and save work.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.resetClip: Clears the current clipping area so the whole canvas can be drawn on again. Use it to undo earlier clipping before drawing something that should not be cut off.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.resetMatrix: Resets the canvas transform back to its default identity matrix. Use it to undo panning, zooming, or rotation before drawing in normal coordinates again.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.restore: Restores the canvas transform and clipping area saved most recently. Use it to undo a saved drawing state after finishing a group of shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.restoreToCount: Restores the canvas transform and clipping area back to a chosen saved depth. Use it to jump back several saved states at once instead of undoing them one by one.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.rotate: Rotates the canvas around a given point so later drawing and clipping appear turned. Use it to draw tilted shapes, dials, or rotated images.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.save: Saves the canvas drawing state, such as its matrix and drawable area, onto a stack so it can be restored later. Use it to temporarily change how you draw and then return to the earlier state.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.saveLayer: Saves the canvas matrix and clipping region and allocates a pixel map for later drawing, which is drawn when you restore. Use it to draw a group of shapes with effects like transparency or blending applied together.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.scale: Applies a scaling matrix to the canvas so later drawing and clipping are scaled in shape and position. Use it to zoom drawings larger or smaller on the canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.setMatrix: Sets a matrix for the canvas so later drawing and clipping are affected in shape and position. Use it to apply a custom transform to everything you draw afterwards.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.skew: Applies a skewing matrix to the canvas so later drawing and clipping are tilted in shape and position. Use it to slant drawings along the X or Y axis.
ArkGraphics2D.Canvas.translate: Applies a translation matrix to the canvas so later drawing and clipping are shifted in shape and position. Use it to move drawings to a different position on the canvas.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createBlendMod: Creates a color filter that blends a chosen color into an image using a blend mode. Use it to tint or recolor graphics, such as giving a picture a colored overlay.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createComposeC: Creates a color filter by applying one color filter and then another on top of it. Use it to stack two color effects, such as a tint followed by a brightness change.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createLighting: Creates a color filter that multiplies colors by one color and then adds another, keeping results in range. Use it to brighten, darken, or tint an image.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createLinearTo: Creates a color filter that applies the sRGB gamma curve to the red, green, and blue channels. Use it to correct colors so they look right on standard screens.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createLumaColo: Creates a color filter that puts brightness into the alpha channel and sets red, green, and blue to zero. Use it to make a brightness-based mask or silhouette.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createMatrixCo: Creates a color filter from a 4 by 5 color matrix. Use it to shift colors precisely, such as adjusting saturation, hue, or contrast.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorFilter.createSRGBGamm: Creates a color filter that applies the sRGB gamma curve to the RGB channels. Use it to convert colors to a linear gamma for correct blending or image processing.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.discriminatePi: Tells whether an image is light or dark. Use it to pick text or icon colors that stay readable over a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getAlphaZeroTr: Measures how much of an image is fully transparent pixels. Use it to check how see-through a picture is before placing it on a background.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getAverageColo: Gets the average color of an image. Use it to pick a representative color from a picture, for example to tint a background.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getComplexityD: Reports how busy or complex an image is. Use it to decide whether a picture suits a simple background or overlay.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getDeepenImmer: Gives a deeper color that blends with the image background. Use it to tint bars or panels so they match the picture behind them.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getHighestSatu: Gets the most saturated color in an image. Use it to find the most vivid color in a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getImmersiveBa: Gives a background color drawn from the image for an immersive look. Use it to fill the area around a picture so it blends in.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getImmersiveFo: Gives a foreground color drawn from the image for text and content. Use it to color labels or icons so they match the picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getLargestProp: Gets the color that covers the largest area of an image. Use it to find the dominant color of a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getMainColor: Gets the main color of an image. Use it to pick the dominant color of a picture, for example for a theme.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getMainColorSy: Gets the main color of an image right away. Use it to pick the dominant color of a picture, for example for a theme.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getMorandiShad: Gets a soft Morandi shadow color from an image's main color. Use it to pick a muted shadow tone that matches a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getReverseColo: Gets a contrasting color for an image, black for very light pictures and white otherwise. Use it to choose readable text or icon color over a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getShadeDegree: Tells how light or dark an image is. Use it to judge a picture's brightness before placing text or icons on it.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.getTopProporti: Finds the most common colors in an image and returns them sorted by how much of the image they cover. Use it to pick a matching color scheme or theme from a photo.
Gets the most common colors in an image and how much of it each covers. Use it to build a color scheme from a photo.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorPicker.isBlackOrWhite: Checks whether a color is black, white, or gray. Use it to tell if a color is plain and neutral, for example when choosing readable text or background colors.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorSpaceManager.getColor: Gets the type of the current color space. Use it to find out which color space is being used when handling images or graphics.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorSpaceManager.getGamma: Gets the gamma value of the color space. Use it to check the brightness curve used when handling images or graphics.
ArkGraphics2D.ColorSpaceManager.getWhite: Gets the x and y coordinates of the color space's white point. Use it to check the reference white used when handling images or graphics.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.off: Stops receiving per-frame change events. Use it to stop updating an animation or drawing when frames change.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.offFrame: Stops listening for per-frame updates. Use it to stop reacting to each screen frame, such as when pausing an animation.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.on: Listens for updates on each screen frame. Use it to run something on every frame, such as animating a moving object.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.onFrame: Listens for updates on each screen frame. Use it to run something on every frame, such as animating a moving object.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.setExpectedFra: Sets the range of frame rates to aim for. Use it to keep a game or animation running smoothly at a chosen speed.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.start: Begins calling back on every screen frame. Use it to start a smooth animation or game loop.
ArkGraphics2D.DisplaySync.stop: Stops calling back on every screen frame. Use it to pause a smooth animation or game loop.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.bezierWarp: Warps a component's shape along bezier curves for a deformation effect. Use it to bend or twist a view into a curved shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.blur: Blurs an image by a given radius, making it look soft or out of focus. Use it to soften a photo or hide details in the background.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.blurBubblesRise: Adds a dreamy blurred effect like bubbles rising through liquid. Use it to give a component a bubbly, underwater look.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.brightness: Adjusts how bright or dark an image looks. Use it to lighten a dark photo or dim a bright one.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.colorGradient: Blends colors across a shape as a gradient filter. Use it to give a component a colorful gradient look.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.contentLight: Adds a light effect from a chosen position and color onto content. Use it to make a component look lit up.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.directionLight: Adds a directional light effect to content using a mask. Use it to give a component a lit, shadowed look.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.displacementDistort: Warps content using a displacement map. Use it to distort or ripple a component's appearance.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.distort: Distorts a component with barrel or pincushion warping. Use it to bend or bulge a component's look.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.edgeLight: Detects edges of content and makes them glow. Use it to add a glowing outline around a component.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.ellipticalGradientB: Blurs an image with an elliptical gradient, strongest at the center and fading outward. Use it to soften or fade parts of a picture around a chosen oval area.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.flyInFlyOutEffect: Makes a component fly in or fly out by stretching it. Use it for entrance and exit animations when a view appears or disappears.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.getEffectPixelMap: Gives you the image with all the added effects applied. Use it to get the finished picture after blurring, brightening, or other edits.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.getPixelMap: Gives you the image that the effects were added to. Use it to get the picture you are editing.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.grayscale: Turns an image into black and white. Use it to make a photo look monochrome.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.hdrBrightnessRatio: Brightens a component by a multiplier, making it glow brighter than normal. Use it to boost the brightness of highlights on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.heatDistortion: Adds a wavy distortion that looks like hot air shimmering. Use it to make a scene feel hot, like desert air or rising heat.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.invert: Inverts the colors of an image, like a photo negative. Use it to flip light and dark colors for a negative effect.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.maskDispersion: Splits colors apart using a mask map to create a dispersion effect. Use it for a colorful, glitchy or prism-like look on an image.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.maskTransition: Fades a component in or out using an alpha mask. Use it for smooth reveal or hide transitions between views.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.pixelStretch: Sets an edge pixel stretch effect on a component. Use it to stretch the pixels along a component's edges.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.radiusGradientBlur: Adds a radius gradient blur effect to a component, with a blurring radius. Use it to blur content more toward the edges.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.setColorMatrix: Applies a custom color matrix to change the colors of an image. Use it to tint, recolor, or adjust the color balance of a picture.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.variableRadiusBlur: Sets a variable radius blur effect using a mask whose alpha controls the blurring degree. Use it to blur content unevenly across a component.
ArkGraphics2D.Filter.waterRipple: Sets a water ripple effect on a component, with ripple progress, wave count, and center position. Use it to show ripples spreading across the screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.countText: Counts how many glyphs a piece of text contains. Use it to measure text length before drawing or laying out words on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.createPathForGlyph: Gets the outline path of a single glyph. Use it to draw or animate the shape of a letter or character.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.enableEmbolden: Turns bold text on or off. Use it to make rendered text appear thicker and heavier.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.enableLinearMetrics: Turns linear font scaling on or off. Use it to keep text spacing consistent when scaling text smoothly.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.enableSubpixel: Turns subpixel font rendering on or off. Use it to make small text look smoother and sharper on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getBounds: Gets the rectangular bounding box around each glyph in an array. Use it to measure where drawn characters will appear on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getEdging: Gets the font edging effect, the smoothing applied to the edges of drawn text. Use it to check how smooth or sharp text edges will look when drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getHinting: Gets the font hinting effect, the adjustment that sharpens text at small sizes. Use it to check how text is tuned for clearer rendering.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getMetrics: Gets the font metrics of the typeface, such as its measurements. Use it to find out how tall or wide text will be when laying out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getScaleX: Gets the horizontal scale ratio of this font. Use it to check how stretched or squeezed text is horizontally when drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getSize: Gets the font size. Use it to find out how large text will be when drawing or laying out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getSkewX: Gets the horizontal skew factor of this font, how slanted it is. Use it to check the slant applied to text when drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getTextPath: Gets the outline path of a piece of text at a given position. Use it to draw text as a shape or outline.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getTextPathWithFallba: Gets the outline path for text, using fallback fonts for characters the main font lacks. Use it to turn text into a shape you can draw or measure.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getTypeface: Gets the typeface used by this font. Use it to check or reuse which font style is being drawn with.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.getWidths: Gets the width of each glyph in an array. Use it to measure how wide characters will be when laying out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isBaselineSnap: Checks whether baselines are set to snap to pixels when the canvas is axis aligned. Use it to see if text baselines will be pixel-aligned.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isEmbeddedBitmaps: Checks whether this font uses embedded bitmaps. Use it to find out if the font draws from bitmap images.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isEmbolden: Checks whether the bold effect is set for this font. Use it to tell if text will be drawn bold.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isForceAutoHinting: Checks whether auto hinting is forcibly used for this font. Use it to find out if text rendering forces auto hinting.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isLinearMetrics: Checks whether linear scaling is used for this font. Use it to find out if the font scales text linearly.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isSubpixel: Checks whether sub-pixel rendering is used for a font. Use it to find out if the font renders text with sub-pixel precision.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.isThemeFontFollowed: Checks whether the font follows the theme font, which it does by default. Use it to find out if the font follows the theme font.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.measureSingleCharacte: Measures the width of a single character, falling back to the system typeface if the current one does not support it. Use it to find how wide one character is when laying out text.

Measures the width of a single character with font features, falling back to the system typeface if the current one does not support it. Use it to find how wide one character is with specific font features.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.measureText: Measures how wide a piece of text is, returning the width as a number. Use it to work out how much space text will take before drawing it.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setBaselineSnap: Sets whether text baselines are snapped to whole pixels when the canvas is axis aligned. Use it to keep text looking crisp and sharp when drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setEdging: Sets the edging effect used when drawing a font. Use it to control how smooth or sharp the edges of text look.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setEmbeddedBitmaps: Sets whether bitmaps stored inside the font are used. Use it to control whether the font draws with its built-in bitmap images.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setForceAutoHinting: Sets whether glyphs are always auto hinted. Use it to force extra shape adjustment so small text stays clear.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setHinting: Sets the hinting effect used for a font. Use it to adjust how glyph shapes are fitted for clearer text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setScaleX: Stretches or squeezes text horizontally by a scale factor. Use it to make text wider or narrower when drawing labels or headings.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setSize: Sets how large the text is drawn. Use it to make text bigger or smaller, such as for titles or captions.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setSkewX: Slants text sideways by a skew factor. Use it to make text look italic or slanted when drawing it.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setThemeFontFollowed: Chooses whether text uses the system theme font when no other typeface is set. Use it to keep text matching the device's theme look.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.setTypeface: Sets the font style, including name, weight, and italic. Use it to pick a bold, italic, or specific font for drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Font.textToGlyphs: Turns a text string into the glyph indexes used for drawing. Use it to get the glyphs needed to render or measure text.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.clearCaches: Clears the stored font cache to free up memory. Use it only when you need to reclaim memory used by fonts.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.getGlobalIn: Gets the shared global font collection. Use it to draw text with fonts anywhere in an app.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.getLocalIns: Gets a font collection for the current widget. Use it to draw text in a widget with its own fonts.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.loadFont: Loads a custom font file so text can be drawn with it. Use it to display text in your own TTF or OTF font.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.loadFontSyn: Loads a custom font file right away so text can be drawn with it. Use it to display text in your own TTF or OTF font.
Loads a custom font file right away, including TTC files, so text can be drawn with it. Use it to display text in your own font.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.loadFontWit: Loads a custom font file (TTF, OTF, or TTC) under a chosen name so text can use it. Use it to add your own font for displaying styled text.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.setParagrap: Turns typesetting paragraph caching on or off, which speeds up repeated text layout but uses extra memory. Use it to make repeated text layout faster or to save memory.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.unloadFont: Removes a previously loaded custom font by its name so it is no longer available. Use it to stop using a custom font you added.
ArkGraphics2D.FontCollection.unloadFontS: Removes a previously loaded custom font by its name immediately, so it is no longer available. Use it to stop using a custom font you added.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createBlendIma: Creates an image filter by blending a background filter and a foreground filter using a blend mode. Use it to combine two image effects into one.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createBlurImag: Creates an image filter that applies a Gaussian blur with given horizontal and vertical strength and edge tiling. Use it to blur an image or picture.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createComposeI: Chains two image filters so the first one's result is fed into the second. Use it to stack effects, such as blurring an image and then shifting its colors.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createFromColo: Creates an image filter that applies a color filter effect. Use it to recolor or tint an image.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createFromImag: Creates an image filter from a given image. Use it to draw or blend one image onto another.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createFromShad: Creates an image filter that renders the contents of a shader. Use it to apply a shader pattern or effect to an image.
ArkGraphics2D.ImageFilter.createOffsetIm: Creates a filter that shifts an image by a horizontal and vertical distance. Use it to move or nudge an image's position.
ArkGraphics2D.Lattice.createImageLattice: Divides an image into a grid of lattices so parts stay fixed while the rest stretch. Use it to resize an image without distorting its corners or borders.
Splits an image into a grid of lattice cells using X and Y coordinates, keeping some cells fixed and stretching others to fit. Use it to resize a picture without distorting its corners and edges.
ArkGraphics2D.LineTypeset.createLine: Creates a text line object for a chosen range of characters so its layout can be measured. Use it to lay out and position a line of text on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.LineTypeset.getLineBreak: Tells how many characters fit from a given position within a set width. Use it to wrap text so each line fits the space available.
ArkGraphics2D.Mask.createPixelMapMask: Creates a mask from a pixel map for use with filters or visual effects. Use it to shape where an effect applies using an image.
ArkGraphics2D.Mask.createRadialGradientM: Creates a radial gradient mask for use with filters or visual effects. Use it to fade an effect in a circular pattern.
ArkGraphics2D.Mask.createRippleMask: Creates a ripple-shaped mask for a filter or visual effect. Use it to make a ripple pattern appear on a component.
ArkGraphics2D.Mask.createUseEffectMask: Creates a mask that controls whether a use effect is applied. Use it to turn a visual effect on or off for a component.
ArkGraphics2D.Mask.createWaveGradientMas: Creates a single-wave gradient mask spreading from a center point. Use it to make a wave-like glow or ripple effect on a component.
ArkGraphics2D.MaskFilter.createBlurMaskF: Creates a mask filter that blurs an image with a Gaussian blur. Use it to soften or blur shapes and pictures.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.getAll: Returns all nine values of the matrix as an array. Use it to read the full transform, such as position, scale, and rotation.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.getValue: Returns one value from the matrix at a given index from 0 to 8. Use it to check a single part of a transform, such as scale or rotation.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.invert: Reverses a matrix so it undoes the original transformation. Use it to undo a rotation, scale, or move applied to a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.isAffine: Checks whether a matrix only moves, turns, or scales things without skewing. Use it to confirm a drawing transform is a simple move, rotation, or zoom.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.isEqual: Checks whether two matrices are the same. Use it to tell if two drawings have the same position, rotation, and scale.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.isIdentity: Checks whether a matrix leaves everything unchanged. Use it to tell if a drawing has no move, rotation, or scale applied.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.mapPoints: Moves a set of points through a matrix to get their new positions. Use it to find where points land after a drawing is moved, turned, or scaled.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.mapRadius: Gives the average radius of the ellipse a circle becomes after a matrix is applied. Use it to find how big a round shape looks after scaling or turning.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.mapRect: Finds the smallest upright rectangle that contains a source rectangle after a matrix transformation. Use it to know where a rotated or skewed shape ends up on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.postConcat: Multiplies the current matrix by another matrix, applying that matrix's transformation after the current one. Use it to combine several transformations, such as moving and rotating a drawing, into one.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.postRotate: Rotates the matrix by a given angle around a chosen point. Use it to spin a drawing or image clockwise or counterclockwise on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.postScale: Scales the matrix by given factors around a chosen point. Use it to make a drawing or image bigger, smaller, or mirrored.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.postSkew: Tilts the matrix along the X and Y axes. Use it to slant a drawing or image for a skewed look.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.postTranslate: Moves the matrix by a given horizontal and vertical distance. Use it to shift a drawing or image to a new position on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.preConcat: Combines the current matrix with another matrix by multiplying them. Use it to stack transformations like move, rotate, or scale in a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.preRotate: Rotates the matrix by a given angle around a chosen point. Use it to turn a drawing or shape clockwise or counterclockwise.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.preScale: Scales the matrix by given factors around a chosen point. Use it to make a drawing bigger or smaller, or to mirror it.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.preSkew: Tilts the matrix along the X or Y axis. Use it to slant a drawing for a skewed or italic look.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.preTranslate: Moves the matrix by a given horizontal and vertical distance. Use it to shift a drawing left, right, up, or down.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.rectStaysRect: Checks whether a rectangle stays a rectangle after the matrix is applied. Use it to tell if a transformation keeps a shape rectangular.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.reset: Resets a matrix back to its identity state, clearing any rotation, scaling, or translation. Use it to start fresh before applying new transformations to a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setConcat: Combines two matrices into one by multiplying them, updating the current matrix with the result. Use it to merge several transformations, such as rotation and scaling, into a single step.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setMatrix: Replaces the current matrix with values from a nine-number array that sets scaling, skew, translation, and perspective. Use it to apply a specific transformation to a drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setPolyToPoly: Builds a transformation that maps up to four source points onto matching destination points. Use it to warp or align a shape so its corners land where you want.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setRectToRect: Builds a transformation that maps one rectangle onto another, with a chosen fit mode. Use it to scale or position an image so it fits a target area.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setRotation: Sets the matrix to rotate by a given angle around a chosen point. Use it to turn a drawing or image clockwise or counterclockwise about a pivot.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setScale: Scales a drawing around a chosen point, and can mirror it if a negative scale is given. Use it to make an image bigger or smaller, or flip it.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setSinCos: Rotates a drawing around a chosen point using sine and cosine values. Use it to turn or spin an image by a set angle.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setSkew: Tilts a drawing along the X or Y axis by given amounts. Use it to slant an image for a skewed look.
ArkGraphics2D.Matrix.setTranslation: Moves a drawing horizontally and vertically by given distances. Use it to shift an image to a new position.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.didExceedMaxLine: Checks whether a paragraph has more lines than its maximum. Use it to tell if text was cut off or overflowed.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.forceReuseRaster: Sets whether to force reuse of a paragraph's rasterization result. Use it to keep text rendering cached instead of updating it.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getActualTextRan: Finds which characters are actually shown on a given line of laid-out text, optionally counting spaces, and leaves out any overflow ellipsis. Use it to tell what text is visible on a line.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getAlphabeticBas: Gives the alphabetic baseline of laid-out text, in pixels. Use it to line up text or other elements along the text baseline.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getCharacterPosi: Finds the character position closest to a given point in the text area. Use it to turn a tap or click location into a text position, such as placing a cursor.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getCharacterRang: Finds which characters correspond to a given range of glyphs. Use it to map drawn glyphs back to the text characters they represent.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getGlyphPosition: Finds the glyph closest to a given point in the text area. Use it to turn a tap or click location into a glyph position in laid-out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getGlyphRangeFor: Finds which glyphs correspond to a given range of characters. Use it to map a selection of text characters to the glyphs that are drawn for them.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getHeight: Gets the total height of the text. Use it to find how tall a block of text is when laying out a page or screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getIdeographicBa: Gets the ideographic baseline of the text. Use it to line up East Asian characters correctly when drawing or positioning text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLineCount: Counts how many lines the text takes up. Use it to know how many lines a paragraph has when arranging a layout.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLineHeight: Gets the height of one line of text by its index. Use it to space lines evenly when drawing a paragraph.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLineMetrics: Gets measurement details for the lines of text. Use it to inspect line positions and sizes when laying out or drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLineWidth: Gets the width of one line of text by its index. Use it to check how wide a line is when fitting text into a layout.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLongestLine: Finds the longest line in the text and gives its length in pixels. Use it to measure how wide the text will be when drawn.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getLongestLineWi: Finds the width of the longest line in the text, counting its indentation, in pixels. Use it to measure the space the text needs when drawn.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getMaxIntrinsicW: Gives the maximum intrinsic width of the paragraph in pixels. Use it to find the widest the text naturally wants to be.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getMaxWidth: Gives the maximum line width of the text in pixels. Use it to measure how wide the text can be when drawn.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getMinIntrinsicW: Gives the minimum intrinsic width of the paragraph in pixels. Use it to find the narrowest the text can be without breaking words.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getParagraphStyl: Gives the style settings of the paragraph, such as its text look. Use it to check how the text is styled before drawing it.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getProcessState: Tells you how far a paragraph's text processing has got. Use it to check whether text is ready to lay out or draw.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getRectsForPlace: Gives the rectangles taken up by all placeholders in the text. Use it to find where placeholder boxes sit when laying out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getRectsForRange: Gives the rectangles the characters in a chosen text range occupy, at a chosen width and height. Use it to highlight or measure a piece of text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getTextDisplaySt: Gets the display status of a paragraph of text. Use it to check how a paragraph is currently shown.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getTextLines: Gives all the lines of text in a paragraph. Use it to work with each line when laying out or drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getVisibleTextRa: Gives the ranges of text actually shown on screen, leaving out text cut off by line limits or ellipsis. Use it to find what text the reader can see.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.getWordBoundary: Gives the range of the word containing the glyph at a given offset. Use it to select or highlight a whole word where the user tapped.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.layout: Calculates the positions of all glyphs within a maximum line width. Use it to arrange text before drawing it on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.layoutSync: Calculates the positions of all glyphs within a maximum line width, finishing before returning. Use it to arrange text before drawing it on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.layoutWithConstr: Arranges text within a given width and height and reports the resulting size and character range. Use it to fit text into a fixed area before drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.paint: Draws the text onto a canvas starting at a chosen corner point. Use it to show laid-out text on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.paintOnPath: Draws text following a curved or shaped path on a canvas. Use it to make text run along a curve or outline.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.updateColor: Changes the color of all the text, and of its decoration if none was set. Use it to recolor text without rebuilding it.
ArkGraphics2D.Paragraph.updateDecoration: Changes the decoration line, such as an underline or strikethrough, for all the text in a paragraph. Use it to add or change underlines and similar lines under text.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.addPlaceh: Inserts a placeholder into the paragraph being built, describing its size, alignment, and baseline. Use it to reserve space for an image or other object inside text.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.addSymbol: Inserts a symbol into the paragraph being built, chosen by its symbol code. Use it to place an icon or symbol character within text.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.addText: Inserts a text string into the paragraph being built. Use it to add the words that make up a paragraph before drawing it.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.build: Creates a paragraph object from the text and content added so far, ready for layout and drawing. Use it to turn built-up text into something you can lay out and render.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.buildLine: Builds a line typesetter from the paragraph content. Use it to lay out and render text line by line.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.popStyle: Restores the previous text style. Use it to undo the last style change when building styled text.
ArkGraphics2D.ParagraphBuilder.pushStyle: Applies a new style to the current text blob, such as font, size, color, weight, spacing, underline, strikethrough, or shadow. Use it to style a piece of text.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addArc: Adds an arc to a path, or an oval when the start angle is a multiple of 90 and the sweep is outside -360 to 360. Use it to draw curved shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addCircle: Adds a circle to a path in the chosen direction, starting at the rightmost point. Use it to draw round shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addOval: Adds the ellipse that fits inside a rectangle to a path, starting from the top, right, bottom, or left point. Use it to draw oval shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addPath: Transforms the points of another path by a matrix and adds the result to this path. Use it to copy or move a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addPolygon: Adds a polygon shape to a path from a list of corner points, optionally closing it back to the start. Use it to draw custom polygon shapes in a drawing or graphic.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addRect: Adds a rectangle to a path, starting at its upper left corner, in a chosen direction. Use it to draw rectangular shapes in a drawing or graphic.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.addRoundRect: Adds a rounded rectangle to a path in a chosen direction. Use it to draw rounded rectangle shapes in a drawing or graphic.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.approximate: Turns a path into a close approximation made of straight line segments, within a given error. Use it to simplify a curved path into straight lines for drawing or measuring.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.arcTo: Adds an arc to a path by defining a rectangle, taking its inscribed ellipse, and drawing the part between a start angle and sweep angle. Use it to draw curved arc shapes in a drawing or graphic.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.buildFromSvgString: Parses an SVG string and builds the path it describes. Use it to draw a shape defined by SVG path data.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.close: Closes a path by adding a line segment from its start point to its last point. Use it to finish an outline so a shape can be filled or drawn as a closed figure.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.conicTo: Draws a conic curve from the path's last point to a target point, shaped by a control point and weight. Use it to draw smooth curved shapes such as rounded outlines or arcs.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.contains: Checks whether a coordinate point lies inside this path. Use it to tell if a tap or touch point falls within a drawn shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.convertToSvgString: Converts the path into an SVG string. Use it to save or share a drawn shape as SVG text.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.cubicTo: Draws a cubic Bezier curve from the path's last point to a target point using two control points. Use it to draw smooth flowing curves such as waves or rounded shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getBounds: Gets the smallest rectangle that encloses this path. Use it to find the size or position of a drawn shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getConicWeightData: Gets the weight values used for the conic curves in a path. Use it to inspect or reuse the shape of curved path segments.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getFillType: Gets the rule used to fill a path. Use it to find out how a shape's inside is decided when drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getLastPoint: Gets the last point of a path. Use it to find where a drawn line or shape ends.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getLength: Measures how long a path is, optionally treating it as closed. Use it to find the distance around a drawn shape or line.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getMatrix: Gets the position and orientation at a given distance along a path. Use it to place or turn something so it follows a path, like a marker moving along a line.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getPathIterator: Gets an iterator for stepping through the drawing operations of a path. Use it to walk through and inspect each segment of a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getPointData: Gets the points that make up a path. Use it to read the coordinates of a drawn shape's corners and curve points.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getPositionAndTangent: Finds the coordinates and tangent direction at a given distance along a path. Use it to place or aim something that travels along a drawn line or curve.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getSegment: Copies part of a path between two distances and adds it to another path. Use it to cut out a piece of a drawn shape or line.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.getVerbData: Lists the drawing commands that make up a path. Use it to inspect how a shape or line was built.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.interpolate: Blends two paths by a weight to make an in-between path. Use it to smoothly morph one drawn shape into another.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isClosed: Tells whether a path forms a closed loop. Use it to check if a drawn shape is sealed shut.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isEmpty: Tells whether a path has no content. Use it to check if a drawn shape or line is blank.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isEqual: Checks whether two paths are equal. Use it to tell if two drawn shapes are exactly the same.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isInterpolate: Checks whether two paths are compatible for interpolation, meaning they can be smoothly morphed into each other. Use it to set up shape morphing animations.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isInverseFillType: Checks whether the path's fill type is an inverse type, which fills everything outside the shape instead of inside. Use it to find out if a shape is drawn as an inverted fill.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.isRect: Checks whether a path forms a rectangle, and can give back that rectangle. Use it to detect when a drawn shape is a plain rectangle.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.lineTo: Draws a straight line from the path's last point to a target point, starting at (0, 0) if the path is empty. Use it to draw straight edges of a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.moveTo: Sets the starting point of a path. Use it to begin drawing a shape at a chosen spot.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.offset: Moves a path by given distances along the X and Y axes and returns the shifted path. Use it to reposition a drawn shape or line on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.op: Combines this path with another path using a chosen operation mode. Use it to merge, intersect, or subtract drawn shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.quadTo: Draws a quadratic Bezier curve from the path's last point to a target point. Use it to draw smooth curved lines or shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rConicTo: Draws a conic curve from the path's last point to a point relative to it. Use it to draw smooth curved lines or shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rCubicTo: Draws a cubic Bezier curve from the path's last point to a point relative to it. Use it to draw smooth curved lines or shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rLineTo: Draws a straight line from the path's last point to a point relative to it. Use it to draw straight edges of shapes or lines.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rMoveTo: Moves the path's start point by an offset from its last point, or from (0,0) if empty. Use it to start a new subpath at a position relative to where you left off when drawing shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rQuadTo: Draws a quadratic Bezier curve from the path's last point to a point given as an offset, using an offset control point. Use it to add smooth curved segments when drawing shapes or outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.reset: Clears all path data, removing every point and line. Use it to start drawing a fresh shape with the same path object.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.rewind: Clears all points and lines from the path but keeps its memory for reuse. Use it to restart a drawing without allocating new memory.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.setFillType: Sets how the inside of a path is decided when filling, such as by winding or even-odd crossing rules. Use it to control which areas get filled when drawing overlapping shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.setLastPoint: Sets the last point of the path to the given coordinates. Use it to adjust where the next line or curve will start from when drawing a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.toggleInverseFillType: Switches a path's fill area to its opposite, so what was filled becomes empty and what was empty becomes filled. Use it to invert which parts of a shape are painted.
ArkGraphics2D.Path.transform: Moves, rotates, scales, or skews all points of a path using a matrix. Use it to reposition or reshape a drawn shape on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createComposePa: Combines two path effects so the first is applied and then the second on top. Use it to stack two line styles, such as dashes with rounded corners, on one shape.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createCornerPat: Rounds off the sharp corners where line segments meet, using a given radius. Use it to soften the hard angles of a drawn shape.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createDashPathE: Turns a path into a dashed or dotted line with set on and off lengths and an offset. Use it to draw dashed borders or dotted outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createDiscreteP: Breaks a path into segments and scatters them irregularly along the path. Use it to give a line a rough, hand-drawn or jittery look.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createPathDashE: Creates a dashed path effect where each dash is shaped by a given path. Use it to draw dashed outlines with custom dash shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.PathEffect.createSumPathEf: Creates an overlay path effect by applying two path effects separately and drawing them on top of each other. Use it to combine two outline styles in one drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.PathIterator.hasNext: Checks whether the path iterator has another operation to read. Use it to loop through the drawing steps of a path.
ArkGraphics2D.PathIterator.next: Reads the next path operation and moves the iterator forward, filling in its coordinate points. Use it to walk through a path step by step.
ArkGraphics2D.PathIterator.peek: Reads the next path operation without moving the iterator forward. Use it to look ahead at the next drawing step of a path.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getAlpha: Gets the alpha (transparency) value of a pen, from 0 to 255. Use it to check how see-through a pen's outline is.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getCapStyle: Gets the cap style of a pen, which is how the ends of an outlined line look. Use it to check whether a drawn line has flat, round, or square ends.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getColor: Gets the color of a pen used to outline a shape. Use it to find out what color an outline will be drawn in.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getColor4f: Gets the pen color as floating point numbers. Use it when you need the outline color with decimal precision.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getColorFilter: Gets the color filter applied to a pen. Use it to check how an outline's colors are being altered.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getFillPath: Turns a path into the outline shape that the pen would draw around it. Use it to get the filled outline of a stroked path.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getHexColor: Gets the pen color as a 32-bit hexadecimal ARGB value. Use it to read the outline color in hex form.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getJoinStyle: Gets the corner join style of a pen, which controls how the corners of an outlined shape look. Use it to check how sharp or rounded the corners of a drawn outline are.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getMiterLimit: Gets the maximum ratio allowed between a sharp corner's length and the line width for a pen. Use it to check how far sharp corners can extend before being cut off when outlining a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.getWidth: Gets the stroke width of a pen, which is how thick the outline of a shape is. Use it to check how thick the line drawn around a shape will be.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.isAntiAlias: Checks whether anti-aliasing is turned on for a pen, which smooths the edges of an outlined shape. Use it to check whether drawn outlines will look smooth or jagged.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.reset: Resets a pen back to its initial state. Use it to clear all pen settings and start drawing outlines with default style again.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setAlpha: Sets the transparency of a pen, from fully transparent to fully opaque. Use it to make the outline of a shape see-through or solid.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setAntiAlias: Turns smoothing on or off for a pen's outline, making drawn edges look smoother. Use it when drawing shapes and you want clean, non-jagged outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setBlendMode: Sets how a pen's outline blends with what is already drawn underneath. Use it to control how drawn lines mix with existing content.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setCapStyle: Sets the shape of the ends of lines drawn with a pen, such as flat or rounded. Use it when drawing lines and you want the line ends to look a certain way.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setColor: Sets the color of a pen used to outline shapes. Use it to choose what color your drawn outlines appear in.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setColor4f: Sets the color and color range of a pen used to outline shapes, with color values given as decimals. Use it when you need precise color control for drawn outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setColorFilter: Sets a color filter on a pen so its outline colors are altered, or clears the filter. Use it to change or tint the colors of drawn outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setDither: Turns dithering on or off for the pen so drawn colors look more realistic. Use it when outlining shapes and you want smoother, more natural color.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setImageFilter: Sets an image filter on the pen, or clears it by passing null. Use it to give the outline of a shape an image-filter look.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setJoinStyle: Sets how the corners where lines of a shape meet are joined. Use it to choose between mitered, rounded, or beveled corners when outlining a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setMaskFilter: Adds a mask filter to the pen, or clears it by passing null. Use it to give the outline of a shape a masked, softened effect.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setMiterLimit: Sets the largest allowed ratio of a sharp corner's length to the line width. Use it to control when sharp corners become beveled instead of pointed when outlining a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setPathEffect: Sets a path effect on the pen, or clears it by passing null. Use it to change how the outline path of a shape is drawn.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setShaderEffect: Sets a shader effect on a pen so outlines are painted with a pattern or gradient instead of a flat colour. Use it to draw shapes with textured or gradient outlines.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setShadowLayer: Sets a shadow layer on a pen, which shows as a shadow when text is drawn. Use it to give drawn text a drop shadow.
ArkGraphics2D.Pen.setStrokeWidth: Sets how thick the pen's outline stroke is, with values below 1 drawn as 1 pixel wide. Use it to make drawn lines and shape outlines thicker or thinner.
ArkGraphics2D.PointUtils.negate: Flips a point's coordinates to their opposite values. Use it to mirror a point's position across the origin.
ArkGraphics2D.PointUtils.offset: Moves a point by given distances along the x and y axes. Use it to shift a point's position on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.centerX: Gets the x coordinate at the horizontal centre of a rectangle. Use it to find the middle of a rectangle, such as to place something centred on it.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.centerY: Finds the Y coordinate of a rectangle's center point. Use it to locate the middle of a shape on screen, for example to place something at the vertical center of a box.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.contains: Checks whether one rectangle completely contains another rectangle. Use it to test if a shape or area fully sits inside another, such as whether a button lies within a panel.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.getHeight: Gets the height of a rectangle. Use it to measure how tall a shape or area is on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.getWidth: Gets the width of a rectangle. Use it to measure how wide a shape or area is on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.inset: Shrinks or grows a rectangle by adding values to its left, top, right, and bottom edges. Use it to make a shape smaller or larger, such as adding padding around a box.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.intersect: Finds where two rectangles overlap and updates the first rectangle to that overlapping area. Use it to get the shared region of two shapes, such as the visible part of a clipped view.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.isEmpty: Checks whether a rectangle has no area, such as when its edges cross or touch. Use it to skip drawing or handling shapes that would not show anything.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.isEqual: Checks whether two rectangles have the same position and size. Use it to tell if two areas on screen match exactly.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.isIntersect: Checks whether two rectangles overlap with real area, not just touching edges or corners. Use it to detect when two on-screen areas collide.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.makeCopy: Creates a separate copy of a rectangle so changes to one do not affect the other. Use it to keep an original rectangle safe while editing a duplicate.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.makeEmpty: Creates a rectangle whose top, bottom, left, and right edges are all zero. Use it as a starting blank rectangle to fill in later.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.makeLtrb: Creates a rectangle from given left, top, right, and bottom edge positions. Use it to define a specific area on screen, such as a button or image region.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.offset: Moves a rectangle left, right, up or down by given amounts. Use it to shift a drawn shape or layout box to a new position.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.offsetTo: Moves a rectangle so its top-left corner sits at a chosen position. Use it to place a shape or layout box at exact coordinates.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.setEmpty: Resets a rectangle's left, right, top and bottom boundaries to zero. Use it to clear a rectangle before reusing it.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.setLtrb: Sets a rectangle's left, top, right and bottom boundary values. Use it to define the exact size and position of a shape or layout box.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.setRect: Copies one rectangle's boundaries onto another rectangle. Use it to make a rectangle match an existing one.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.sort: Swaps a rectangle's boundaries when they are reversed so left is less than right and top is less than bottom. Use it to fix an upside-down or backwards rectangle before drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.RectUtils.union: Combines two rectangles into one that covers both, updating the first rectangle. Use it to merge overlapping areas into a single bounding box.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.getBoundaryPath: Gets the outline of a region as a path. Use it to draw or trace the edge of a shape's drawable area.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.getBounds: Gets the smallest rectangle that encloses a region. Use it to find the bounding box of a shape's drawable area.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isComplex: Checks whether a region is made of more than one rectangle. Use it to tell if a region has a simple or complex shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isEmpty: Checks whether a region has no area. Use it to tell if a shape's drawable area is empty before drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isEqual: Checks whether two regions cover exactly the same area. Use it to compare two shapes' drawable areas.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isPointContained: Checks whether a point lies inside a region. Use it to tell if a tap or touch position falls within a drawn shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isRect: Checks whether a region is exactly one rectangle. Use it to tell if a drawn area is a simple rectangle rather than a complex shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.isRegionContained: Checks whether one region lies entirely inside another. Use it to tell if a drawn shape is fully covered by another area.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.offset: Moves a region by given horizontal and vertical amounts. Use it to shift a drawn shape to a new position.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.op: Combines this region with another using an operation and keeps the result here. Use it to merge, intersect, or subtract drawn shapes.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.quickContains: Checks whether a region is a single rectangle that contains the given rectangle. Use it to quickly test if a rectangular area fits inside a drawn shape.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.quickReject: Checks whether a rectangle does not overlap a region, using the region's bounding rectangle. Use it to quickly skip drawing or hit-testing shapes that are outside a given area.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.quickRejectRegion: Checks whether two regions do not overlap, comparing their outer rectangles. Use it to quickly skip work when two drawn areas are far apart.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.setEmpty: Clears a region so it covers nothing. Use it to reset a drawing area before setting new bounds.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.setPath: Sets a region to match the outline of a path inside a clipping area. Use it to make a drawing area follow a shape's outline.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.setRect: Sets a region to a rectangle given by its left, top, right, and bottom edges. Use it to define a rectangular drawing area.
ArkGraphics2D.Region.setRegion: Copies another region into this one. Use it to reuse an existing drawing area for a new region.
ArkGraphics2D.RoundRect.getCorner: Gets the corner radii of a rounded rectangle at the chosen corner. Use it to find how round a specific corner is when drawing or adjusting a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.RoundRect.offset: Moves a rounded rectangle sideways and up or down by given amounts. Use it to reposition a rounded rectangle on screen.
ArkGraphics2D.RoundRect.setCorner: Sets the radii of one rounded corner of a rounded rectangle. Use it to adjust how round a specific corner looks.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getAdvances: Gets the width of each glyph in a range of text. Use it to measure how wide characters are when laying out text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getFont: Gets the font used for a run of text. Use it to check which font is applied to a piece of text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getGlyphCount: Counts the glyphs in a run of text. Use it to find how many glyphs a piece of text contains.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getGlyphs: Gets the glyph indices for a range of text. Use it to look up which glyphs make up a piece of text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getImageBounds: Gets the visible image boundaries of a text layout unit, excluding leading and trailing spaces. Use it to find the exact area text occupies when drawing or aligning text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getOffsets: Gets each glyph's offset relative to its index in a text run. Use it to place or measure individual characters when drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getPositions: Gets the position of each glyph relative to its line within a range of a text run. Use it to place or measure characters when drawing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getStringIndices: Gets the character indices for glyphs in a range of a text run, as offsets from the whole paragraph. Use it to map glyphs back to characters when selecting or editing text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getStringRange: Gets the range of glyphs produced by a text run, as a start position and length in the paragraph. Use it to locate where a run sits when laying out or selecting text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getTextDirection: Gets the text direction of a text run. Use it to lay out or align text correctly for left-to-right or right-to-left writing.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getTextStyle: Gets the text style used by a run of laid-out text. Use it to check the font, size, or colour of a piece of text.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.getTypographicBounds: Gets the typographic boundaries of a run of text, including spaces at the start and end. Use it to measure how much room a line of text takes up.
ArkGraphics2D.Run.paint: Draws a run of text on a canvas at a given position. Use it to show laid-out text on screen or in an image.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createColorSh: Creates a shader effect filled with a single colour. Use it to paint shapes or text with one solid colour.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createCompose: Creates a shader effect by blending two shaders together. Use it to combine two colour patterns into one for drawing.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createConical: Creates a shader effect with a conical gradient between two circles. Use it to fill shapes or text with a smooth colour sweep.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createImageSh: Fills shapes with a picture instead of a plain colour, repeating or stretching the image as needed. Use it to paint with a photo or texture, such as a tiled background or an image-filled shape.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createLinearG: Fills shapes with a smooth colour blend running in a straight line between two points. Use it to paint a fading background or a colour ramp across a shape.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createRadialG: Fills shapes with a colour blend spreading outward from the centre of a circle. Use it to paint a glowing spot or a round colour fade.
ArkGraphics2D.ShaderEffect.createSweepGr: Fills shapes with colours that sweep around a centre point from a start angle to an end angle. Use it to paint a colour wheel or a circular rainbow effect.
