ArkTS.ParseInfo.getAttributeCount: Counts how many attributes the current start tag has. Use it to check how many settings or properties an element carries while reading XML.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getColumnNumber: Gives the current column number in the text being parsed, counting from 1. Use it to point to exactly where something is on a line.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getDepth: Gives how deeply the current element is nested. Use it to tell how far inside the document structure you are.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getLineNumber: Gives the current line number in the text being parsed, counting from 1. Use it to find which line something is on.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getName: Gives the name of the current element. Use it to find out which tag you are reading.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getNamespace: Gives the namespace of the current element. Use it to tell which group of names a tag belongs to.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getPrefix: Gets the prefix of the current element. Use it to read the namespace prefix while parsing XML.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.getText: Gets the text of the current event. Use it to read the text content while parsing XML.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.isEmptyElementTag: Checks whether the current element is empty. Use it to tell an empty tag from one with content while parsing XML.
ArkTS.ParseInfo.isWhitespace: Checks whether the current event contains only whitespace characters. Use it to skip blank text while parsing XML.
ArkTS.PlainArray.add: Adds a key-value pair to the collection. Use it to store a value under a number key.
ArkTS.PlainArray.clear: Removes all key-value pairs and sets the length to 0. Use it to empty the collection and start over.
ArkTS.PlainArray.clone: Makes a copy of the key-value collection so changes to the copy leave the original untouched. Use it to keep a safe backup of stored pairs before editing.
ArkTS.PlainArray.forEach: Runs a given function once for every value stored in the key-value collection. Use it to go through all stored values and act on each one.
ArkTS.PlainArray.getIndexOfKey: Finds the position of the element that has a given key, or -1 if none matches. Use it to locate where a specific key sits in the collection.
ArkTS.PlainArray.getIndexOfValue: Finds the position of the first element holding a given value, or -1 if none matches. Use it to locate where a particular value first appears.
ArkTS.PlainArray.getKeyAt: Gives the key of the element at a chosen position, or -1 if there is none. Use it to look up which key belongs to a position in the collection.
ArkTS.PlainArray.getValueAt: Gives the value of the element at a chosen position, or undefined if there is none. Use it to read the stored value at a known position.
ArkTS.PlainArray.has: Checks whether a stored key exists in the collection. Use it to test if a particular key is present before looking up its value.
ArkTS.PlainArray.isEmpty: Checks whether the collection holds no entries at all. Use it to tell if there is nothing stored before reading or removing items.
ArkTS.PlainArray.remove: Deletes the entry for a given key and gives back its value. Use it to take an item out of the collection when you know its key.
ArkTS.PlainArray.removeAt: Deletes the entry at a given position and gives back its value. Use it to take out an item when you know where it sits in the collection.
ArkTS.PlainArray.removeRangeFrom: Deletes a run of entries starting at a given position and reports how many were removed. Use it to clear out several stored items at once.
ArkTS.PlainArray.setValueAt: Replaces the value stored at a given position. Use it to update an existing item in the collection without changing its place.
ArkTS.PlainArray.toString: Turns all the key-value pairs in a PlainArray into one string. Use it to display or log the whole collection at once.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.exit: Ends the running application process, with an exit code you provide. Use it to close the app when it should stop, but be careful because unsaved data may be lost.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.getEnvironmentVar: Reads the value of an environment variable by its name. Use it to look up settings the system or app has stored in the environment.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.getSystemConfig: Reads a system configuration value by its parameter name. Use it to check a system setting, such as a limit or option, while the app runs.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.getThreadPriority: Gets the priority of a thread from its thread ID. Use it to check how important a running thread is to the system.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.getUidForName: Looks up the user ID for a given user name in the system user database. Use it to find a user's numeric ID from their name.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.isAppUid: Checks whether a given UID belongs to this application. Use it to tell whether a process ID belongs to your own app.
ArkTS.ProcessManager.kill: Sends a signal to a process to terminate it, but only the current process can be terminated. Use it to stop your own running process.
ArkTS.Queue.add: Adds an element to the end of a first-in-first-out queue. Use it to put items in line for later processing in order.
ArkTS.Queue.forEach: Runs a given function once for each value in a queue. Use it to go through every item in a queue and act on each one.
ArkTS.Queue.getFirst: Gives you the element at the front of a first-in-first-out queue without removing it. Use it to peek at the next item waiting to be handled.
ArkTS.Queue.pop: Removes and returns the first element from a first-in-first-out queue. Use it to take the next item out of a queue for processing.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.compare: Compares one rational number with another and returns 0, 1, or -1. Use it to check whether one fraction is equal to, greater than, or less than another.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.compareTo: Compares one rational number with another and tells you which is larger, smaller, or equal. Use it to sort or order fractions and ratios.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.createRationalFromS: Creates a rational number from a written string such as a fraction. Use it to turn text input into a fraction you can calculate with.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.equals: Checks whether a rational number is equal to another object. Use it to test if two fractions or ratios represent the same value.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.getCommonDivisor: Finds the greatest common divisor of two whole numbers. Use it to simplify fractions or ratios to their smallest form.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.getCommonFactor: Finds the greatest common divisor of two whole numbers. Use it to simplify fractions or ratios to their smallest form.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.getDenominator: Gets the bottom number of a rational number, its denominator. Use it to read or display the denominator of a fraction.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.getNumerator: Gets the top number of a fraction. Use it when you need the numerator of a rational number, for example to show or compare parts of a fraction.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.isFinite: Checks whether a rational number is a normal finite value rather than infinite. Use it to tell whether a fraction has a valid, non-zero denominator.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.isNaN: Checks whether a rational number is not a valid number. Use it to detect a fraction that has no meaningful value.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.isZero: Checks whether a rational number equals zero. Use it to test if a fraction is zero before doing further math.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.parseRationalNumber: Creates a fraction from a numerator and a denominator. Use it to build a rational number from two whole numbers.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.toString: Turns a rational number into text like 3/5. Use it to display a fraction as a readable string.
ArkTS.RationalNumber.valueOf: Gets the integer or floating-point value of a rational number. Use it to turn a fraction into a plain number for calculations or display.
ArkTS.Readable.doInitialize: A method you implement that runs the first time a readable stream is listened to. Use it to set up reading from a source such as a file or network socket.
ArkTS.Readable.doRead: A data-reading method you implement in a subclass to read a given number of bytes. Use it to supply data from a source such as a file or network socket.
ArkTS.Readable.isPaused: Checks whether a readable stream is paused. Use it to tell if reading from a file or network socket has been paused and not yet resumed.
ArkTS.Readable.off: Removes an event callback that was listening for events on a readable stream. Use it to stop reacting to data or other events from a file or network socket.
ArkTS.Readable.on: Registers a callback to listen for events on a readable stream. Use it to react when data arrives from a source such as a file or network socket.
ArkTS.Readable.pause: Pauses a readable stream that is actively flowing, so no more data is delivered until resumed. Use it to temporarily stop reading from a file or network source.
ArkTS.Readable.pipe: Connects a readable stream to a writable stream so data flows automatically from the source to the destination. Use it to send file or network data straight into another stream without handling each chunk.
ArkTS.Readable.push: Adds data into the readable stream's buffer so it can be read out later. Use it to feed content into a stream, such as supplying bytes from a file or network source.
ArkTS.Readable.read: Reads a chosen number of bytes from the stream's buffer, returning the data or nothing when the stream has ended. Use it to pull data out of a file or network stream piece by piece.
ArkTS.Readable.resume: Restarts a readable stream that was explicitly paused, so data flows again. Use it to continue reading from a file or network source after pausing.
ArkTS.Readable.setEncoding: Sets the character encoding used when reading from the stream, only if no data is buffered yet. Use it to read text from a file or network stream in the encoding you need.
ArkTS.Readable.unpipe: Detaches a writable stream that was previously attached to a readable stream. Use it to stop sending data from a source, such as a file or network socket, to a destination.
ArkTS.Scope.clamp: Limits a value to a valid range, returning the lower or upper limit if the value falls outside it. Use it to keep a number within allowed bounds.
ArkTS.Scope.contains: Checks whether a value falls within a valid range. Use it to test if a number is inside allowed limits.
ArkTS.Scope.expand: Combines this range with another range to get the union of both. Use it to widen a valid range so it covers two ranges at once.
ArkTS.Scope.getLower: Gets the lower limit of a valid range. Use it to find the smallest allowed value for a field.
ArkTS.Scope.getUpper: Gets the upper limit of a valid range. Use it to find the largest allowed value for a field.
ArkTS.Scope.intersect: Finds the overlapping range shared by two valid ranges. Use it to get the values that both ranges allow.
ArkTS.Scope.toString: Turns a valid range of a field into a readable text string. Use it to show or log the range a value must fall within.
ArkTS.ScopeComparable.compareTo: Compares two values and tells whether the current one is greater than or equal to the other. Use it to sort or check values against each other.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.clamp: Keeps a value inside a set range, returning the nearest limit if it is too low or too high. Use it to stop a number from going out of bounds.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.contains: Checks whether a value falls inside a set range. Use it to confirm a number is within allowed limits.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.expand: Combines a range with new lower and upper limits to make a wider range. Use it to grow an allowed range to include more values.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.getLower: Gets the lowest allowed value of a range. Use it to find the minimum limit a value can have.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.getUpper: Gets the highest value allowed in a range. Use it to check the top limit of a valid range of values.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.intersect: Finds the overlapping part shared by this range and another range. Use it to combine two valid ranges into the values they have in common.
ArkTS.ScopeHelper.toString: Gives a text version of a range showing its limits. Use it to display or log the range of values.
ArkTS.SequenceRunner.execute: Adds a task to a queue that runs tasks one after another. Use it to run jobs in order, one at a time.
ArkTS.Stack.forEach: Runs a given action once for every item in a last-in-first-out stack. Use it to go through each stacked item and do something with it.
ArkTS.Stack.isEmpty: Checks whether a last-in-first-out stack has no items left. Use it to test if the stack is empty before taking an item.
ArkTS.Stack.locate: Finds the position of the first matching item in a stack. Use it to check where an item sits in a last-in-first-out list.
ArkTS.Stack.peek: Shows the item on top of a stack without removing it. Use it to look at the most recently added item.
ArkTS.Stack.pop: Removes and returns the item on top of a stack. Use it to take back the most recently added item.
ArkTS.Stack.push: Adds an item on top of a stack. Use it to put a new item onto a last-in-first-out list.
ArkTS.StringDecoder.end: Finishes decoding a binary stream and returns any leftover buffered text as a string. Use it to get the last characters after decoding data.
ArkTS.StringDecoder.write: Decodes part of a binary stream into text, holding back incomplete characters for the next call. Use it to turn chunks of bytes into readable text as they arrive.
ArkTS.Task.addDependency: Makes one task wait for other tasks to finish before it runs. Use it to set the order of background jobs, so a step only starts after the steps it needs are done.
ArkTS.Task.isCanceled: Tells you whether a running task has been canceled. Use it to check if a background job was stopped before doing more work.
ArkTS.Task.isDone: Tells you whether a task has finished. Use it to check if a background job is complete.
ArkTS.Task.onEnqueued: Runs your callback when a task is put in line to run. Use it to know when a queued background job has been accepted and is waiting its turn.
ArkTS.Task.onExecutionFailed: Runs your callback when a task fails. Use it to handle a background job that did not succeed.
ArkTS.Task.onExecutionSucceeded: Runs your callback when a task finishes successfully. Use it to react when a background job completes without error.
ArkTS.Task.onReceiveData: Registers a callback so a task can receive and process data sent from a worker thread. Use it to handle results or messages coming back from background work.
ArkTS.Task.onStartExecution: Registers a callback that runs when a task begins executing. Use it to react or update the screen the moment background work starts.
ArkTS.Task.removeDependency: Removes tasks that this task depends on. Use it to let a task run without waiting for other tasks to finish first.
ArkTS.Task.sendData: Sends data to the host thread and triggers the registered callback. Use it to pass results or messages back from background work.
ArkTS.Task.setCloneList: Sets the list of objects that are copied, not shared, when a task runs across threads. Use it to keep the original data unchanged while background work uses a copy.
ArkTS.Task.setTransferList: Sets the list of buffers whose ownership is transferred when a task runs across threads. Use it to hand data over to background work without copying it.
ArkTS.TaskGroup.addTask: Adds a task to a group so it runs together with the other tasks in that group. Use it to run several jobs at once and collect all their results.
ArkTS.TextDecoder.create: Creates a decoder that turns byte arrays into text in formats like UTF-8 or UTF-16. Use it to read text out of raw bytes, such as a downloaded file or network data.
ArkTS.TextDecoder.decode: Turns a byte array into a readable string. Use it to convert raw bytes into text you can display or process.
ArkTS.TextDecoder.decodeToString: Turns a byte array into a readable string. Use it to convert raw bytes into text you can display or process.
ArkTS.TextDecoder.decodeWithStream: Turns a byte array into a readable string, handling data that arrives in chunks. Use it to decode streaming bytes into text as they come in.
ArkTS.TextEncoder.create: Creates an encoder that turns text into byte arrays. Use it to convert a string into bytes for saving or sending.
ArkTS.TextEncoder.encode: Turns a string into a byte array. Use it to convert text to bytes for storage or sending.
ArkTS.TextEncoder.encodeInto: Turns a string into a byte array. Use it to convert text to bytes for storage or sending.
ArkTS.TextEncoder.encodeIntoUint8Array: Encodes a string and writes the bytes into an existing byte array, reporting how many characters were encoded and how many bytes were written. Use it to convert text into bytes in a buffer you already have.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.addEventListener: Adds a listener that runs when a chosen event happens on a background worker thread. Use it to react to messages or events from background work.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.dispatchEvent: Sends an event to a background worker thread. Use it to trigger a listener or action running on background work.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.off: Removes a listener so it no longer runs when a chosen event happens on a background worker thread. Use it to stop reacting to events from background work.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.on: Listens for a chosen event on a worker thread and runs your callback whenever that event happens. Use it to react to messages or events coming from background work.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.once: Listens for a chosen event on a worker thread and runs your callback only the first time, then stops listening. Use it for one-time reactions to a background event.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.postMessage: Sends data from the main thread to a worker thread, either by copying it or by handing over ownership of buffers. Use it to pass work or data to background processing.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.postMessageWithShared: Sends data from the main thread to a worker thread, sharing sendable objects by reference and copying others. Use it to pass work or data to background processing.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.registerGlobalCallObj: Registers an object so its methods can be called from a worker thread. Use it to let background work call back into objects on the main thread.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.removeAllListener: Removes every event listener registered on a worker thread. Use it to stop reacting to all background events at once.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.removeEventListener: Removes an event listener from a worker thread so it no longer reacts to that event. Use it to stop handling worker events you no longer need.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.terminate: Stops a worker thread from receiving any more messages. Use it to shut down background work when it is no longer needed.
ArkTS.ThreadWorker.unregisterGlobalCallO: Unregisters an object previously registered with the worker instance, releasing the strong reference. Use it to clean up a registered object when it is no longer needed.
ArkTS.ThreadWorkerGlobalScope.callGlobal: Calls a method on an object registered in the host thread, synchronously for the worker. Use it to run a host-side method from a worker and get its result.
ArkTS.ThreadWorkerGlobalScope.close: Terminates the worker thread so it stops receiving messages. Use it to end background work from inside the worker.
ArkTS.ThreadWorkerGlobalScope.postMessag: Sends a message from a worker thread to the host thread, copying data or transferring ownership. Use it to pass results or data back to the main thread.
Sends a message from a worker thread to the main thread, placing it at the front of its priority queue. Use it to hand data back to the main thread so it is handled before other queued messages.
Sends a message from a worker thread to the main thread, passing sendable objects by reference and others by copy. Use it to share data back to the main thread without copying large sendable objects.
ArkTS.Transform.doFlush: Processes any remaining data when a transform stream ends. Use it to finish converting or outputting leftover data at the end of a stream.
ArkTS.Transform.doTransform: Converts or processes a chunk of input data and reports when done. Use it to transform data as it flows through a stream, such as changing text encoding.
ArkTS.TreeMap.clear: Removes all key-value pairs from the map. Use it to empty a map and start over.
ArkTS.TreeMap.entries: Returns an iterator of the map's key-value pairs in insertion order. Use it to loop through every key and value stored in the map.
ArkTS.TreeMap.forEach: Runs a given action once for every key currently in the map, skipping deleted keys. Use it to go through all entries in a sorted map and do something with each one.
ArkTS.TreeMap.getFirstKey: Gives the first sorted key in the map, or undefined if the map is empty. Use it to find the smallest key, such as the earliest date or lowest score.
ArkTS.TreeMap.getHigherKey: Gives the least key that is greater than or equal to the key you give, or undefined if there is none. Use it to find the next key at or after a chosen value.
ArkTS.TreeMap.getLastKey: Gives the last sorted key in the map, or undefined if the map is empty. Use it to find the largest key, such as the latest date or highest score.
ArkTS.TreeMap.getLowerKey: Gives the greatest key that is smaller than or equal to the key you give, or undefined if there is none. Use it to find the previous key at or before a chosen value.
ArkTS.TreeMap.hasKey: Tells you whether a given key exists in the map. Use it to check if an entry is already stored before adding or reading it.
ArkTS.TreeMap.hasValue: Checks whether a given value is present in the map. Use it to see if a value is already stored before adding or changing it.
ArkTS.TreeMap.isEmpty: Tells whether the map has no entries at all. Use it to check if anything is stored before reading or looping through the map.
ArkTS.TreeMap.keys: Gives an iterator over all the keys in the map. Use it to walk through every key, for example to list or process each stored item.
ArkTS.TreeMap.remove: Deletes the entry for a given key and returns its value. Use it to take an item out of the map when it is no longer needed.
ArkTS.TreeMap.replace: Changes the value stored under an existing key to a new value. Use it to update an entry that is already in the map.
ArkTS.TreeMap.setAll: Copies every entry from another map into this map. Use it to merge one map's contents into another in a single step.
ArkTS.TreeMap.values: Returns an iterator over all the values stored in the map. Use it to walk through every value in a key-value collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.add: Adds an element to the set if it is not already there, and reports whether it was already present. Use it to collect unique items without duplicates.
ArkTS.TreeSet.clear: Removes every element from the set, leaving it empty. Use it to reset a collection of unique items.
ArkTS.TreeSet.entries: Returns an iterator of [value, value] pairs for each element in the set. Use it to loop over all elements in order.
ArkTS.TreeSet.forEach: Runs a given function once for each value in the set. Use it to process every element in a collection of unique items.
ArkTS.TreeSet.getFirstValue: Gets the first element in the set, or undefined if there is none. Use it to peek at the smallest element in an ordered collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.getHigherValue: Finds the smallest element in the set that is greater than or equal to a given value. Use it to look up the next item at or after a chosen value in a sorted collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.getLastValue: Gets the last element in the set. Use it to read the largest item in a sorted collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.getLowerValue: Finds the greatest element in the set that is smaller than or equal to a given value. Use it to look up the previous item at or before a chosen value in a sorted collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.has: Checks whether the set contains a given value. Use it to test if an item is already in a collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.isEmpty: Checks whether the set has no elements. Use it to test if a collection is empty before working with it.
ArkTS.TreeSet.popFirst: Removes and returns the first element of the set. Use it to take the smallest item out of a sorted collection.
ArkTS.TreeSet.popLast: Removes and returns the last element of the set, or undefined if the set is empty. Use it to take the largest value off a sorted set.
ArkTS.TreeSet.remove: Removes a specified element from the set and reports whether that element was present. Use it to delete a value you no longer need from a sorted set.
ArkTS.TreeSet.values: Returns an iterator over the values in the set. Use it to loop through every value in a sorted set.
ArkTS.URI.addEncodedSegment: Appends an already-encoded path segment to the URI's path and returns a new URI, leaving the original unchanged. Use it to build up a web address path piece by piece.
ArkTS.URI.addQueryValue: Adds a query parameter to the URI and returns a new URI, leaving the original unchanged. Use it to attach search or filter values to a web address.
ArkTS.URI.addSegment: Encodes a path segment, appends it to the URI's path, and returns a new URI, leaving the original unchanged. Use it to build up a web address path piece by piece.
ArkTS.URI.checkHierarchical: Tells whether a URI is hierarchical, meaning it starts with a slash in its scheme-specific part. Use it to check how a web address is structured before working with its path.
ArkTS.URI.checkIsAbsolute: Tells whether a URI is absolute, meaning it has a scheme defined. Use it to check if a web address is complete and self-contained.
ArkTS.URI.checkOpaque: Tells whether a URI is opaque, meaning it does not start with a slash. Use it to check whether a web address has no path structure.
ArkTS.URI.checkRelative: Tells whether a URI is relative. Use it to check if a web address is relative rather than complete.
ArkTS.URI.clearQuery: Removes the query part of a URI and returns a new URI, leaving the original unchanged. Use it to strip parameters from a web address.
ArkTS.URI.createFromParts: Builds a URI from a scheme, scheme-specific part, and fragment. Use it to assemble a web address from its separate pieces.
ArkTS.URI.equals: Checks whether one URI is equivalent to another URI. Use it to compare two web addresses or resource links and see if they point to the same place.
ArkTS.URI.equalsTo: Checks whether one URI is the same as another URI. Use it to compare two web addresses or resource links for equality.
ArkTS.URI.getBooleanQueryValue: Reads a true or false value from a named query parameter in a URI, falling back to a default if the key is missing. Use it to read on/off style settings from a web address.
ArkTS.URI.getLastSegment: Gets the last segment of a URI path. Use it to find the final part of a web address, such as a file or page name.
ArkTS.URI.getQueryNames: Lists all the distinct keys in the query part of a URI. Use it to see which parameters a web address carries.
ArkTS.URI.getQueryValue: Gets the first value for a given key in a URI's query part, decoding it if needed. Use it to read a specific parameter from a web address.
ArkTS.URI.getQueryValues: Gets the decoded values for a given key from a web address's query part. Use it to read parameter values from a link, such as a search term or page number.
ArkTS.URI.getSegment: Gets the decoded path segments of a web address, each without slashes. Use it to break a link into its folder or page parts.
ArkTS.URI.normalize: Cleans up the path of a web address and returns the tidied address. Use it to make links consistent before comparing or storing them.
ArkTS.URI.toString: Turns a web address into an encoded text string. Use it to save or share a link as plain text.
ArkTS.URL.parseURL: Parses a web address string into a usable address, resolving relative links against a base address. Use it to read or work with links entered by a user.
ArkTS.URL.toJSON: Converts a parsed web address into a text string. Use it to store or send a link as plain text.
ArkTS.URL.toString: Turns a parsed web address back into a text string. Use it to get the full address text to display, save, or share.
ArkTS.URLParams.append: Adds a key and value pair onto the end of a web address's query string. Use it to build or extend a link with extra search or filter settings.
ArkTS.URLParams.delete: Removes the key-value pair with the given key from URL query parameters. Use it to strip an unwanted setting out of a web address.
ArkTS.URLParams.entries: Gives an iterator over each key and value pair in a web address's query string. Use it to walk through all the settings in a link one by one.
ArkTS.URLParams.forEach: Runs a given action on every key and value pair in a web address's query string. Use it to process each setting in a link in turn.
ArkTS.URLParams.getAll: Gets every value stored under one key in a web address's query string. Use it to read all the values for a repeated setting in a link.
ArkTS.URLParams.has: Checks whether a key exists in a web address's query string. Use it to test if a link contains a particular setting before reading it.
ArkTS.URLParams.keys: Gets an iterator over the names of all key-value pairs in a URL query string. Use it to list every parameter name in a link or web address.
ArkTS.URLParams.sort: Sorts all key-value pairs in a URL query string by the Unicode order of their keys. Use it to put query parameters in a consistent order.
ArkTS.URLParams.toString: Turns the search parameters into a string, percent-encoding characters when needed. Use it to build a query string for a URL.
ArkTS.URLParams.values: Gets an iterator over the values of all key-value pairs in a URL query string. Use it to list every parameter value in a link or web address.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.append: Adds a new key and value pair as a search parameter. Use it to add a filter or option to a URL query string.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.delete: Removes a named search parameter and its value from the list. Use it to take a filter or option out of a URL query string.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.entries: Gives an iterator over each name and value pair in URL query parameters. Use it to walk through all the settings in a web address one by one.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.forEach: Runs a callback for every key-value pair in a URL query string. Use it to walk through all parameters in a link, like reading every filter in a search address.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.getAll: Returns all values stored under one parameter name as an array. Use it to read every value of a repeated query key, such as all tags in a link.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.has: Checks whether a query string contains a parameter with the given name. Use it to test if a link includes a certain setting, like a page number.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.keys: Gives an iterator over all parameter names in a query string. Use it to list every key in a link's parameters one by one.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.sort: Sorts all key-value pairs in a query string in place. Use it to put link parameters in a stable order, such as for comparing or caching URLs.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.toString: Builds a query string suitable for use in a URL. Use it to turn parameters into the text you append to a link.
ArkTS.URLSearchParams.values: Goes through all the values in a URL query string one by one. Use it to read every value stored in a web address's parameters.
ArkTS.Vector.add: Adds an element to the end of a list. Use it to append items to a growing collection of data.
ArkTS.Vector.clear: Removes all elements from a list, leaving it empty. Use it to reset a collection of data back to nothing.
ArkTS.Vector.clone: Makes a copy of a list that can be changed without affecting the original. Use it to keep a safe duplicate of your data before editing.
ArkTS.Vector.convertToArray: Turns a vector into a plain array. Use it to get an array of the same items when a function needs an array instead of a vector.
ArkTS.Vector.copyToArray: Copies the elements of a list into an array, replacing what was there. Use it to move your stored items into a plain array.
ArkTS.Vector.forEach: Runs a given action on each element in a list, with its position index. Use it to go through every item in a collection and do something with each.
ArkTS.Vector.getCapacity: Tells you how many items the vector can currently hold before it needs to grow. Use it to check available room before adding many items.
ArkTS.Vector.getFirstElement: Gives you the first item in the vector. Use it to read the item at the front of the list.
ArkTS.Vector.getIndexFrom: Finds where an item appears, searching forward from a given position. Use it to locate an item in a list starting partway through.
ArkTS.Vector.getIndexOf: Finds the position of the first matching item in the vector. Use it to look up where an item sits in a list.
ArkTS.Vector.getLastElement: Gives you the last item in the vector. Use it to read the item at the end of the list.
ArkTS.Vector.getLastIndexFrom: Finds where an item appears, searching backward from a given position. Use it to locate the nearest matching item before a point in a list.
ArkTS.Vector.getLastIndexOf: Finds the position of the last matching item in a list. Use it to locate where an item last appears, such as finding the most recent entry in a history list.
ArkTS.Vector.has: Checks whether a list contains a particular item. Use it to test if something is already in a list, like checking whether a name is already saved.
ArkTS.Vector.increaseCapacityTo: Grows the storage space of a list to hold more items. Use it to make room before adding many items so the list does not run out of space.
ArkTS.Vector.insert: Adds an item at a chosen position in a list, shifting later items along. Use it to place a new entry in the middle of an ordered list.
ArkTS.Vector.isEmpty: Checks whether a list has no items in it. Use it to test if a list is empty before showing or processing its contents.
ArkTS.Vector.remove: Deletes the first matching item from a list. Use it to take an item out of a list, such as removing a completed task.
ArkTS.Vector.removeByIndex: Removes the element at a given position and returns it, shifting later elements left. Use it to take an item out of a list by its position.
ArkTS.Vector.removeByRange: Removes all elements in a range, including the start position but not the end position. Use it to delete a block of items from a list at once.
ArkTS.Vector.replaceAllElements: Replaces every element with a new value produced by a callback. Use it to update all items in a list in one pass.
ArkTS.Vector.setLength: Sets a new length for the list. Use it to grow or shrink how many items the list holds.
ArkTS.Vector.sort: Sorts the elements, optionally with a custom comparison. Use it to put a list of items in order.
ArkTS.Vector.subVector: Copies elements in a range, including the start but not the end, into a new list. Use it to take a slice of a list.
ArkTS.Vector.toString: Joins the elements of a vector into one string, separated by commas. Use it to display or print the contents of a list as text.
ArkTS.Vector.trimToCurrentLength: Shrinks a vector's reserved memory down to match its current number of elements. Use it to free unused memory after removing items from a list.
ArkTS.Worker.off: Removes an event listener from a worker so it no longer reacts to that event. Use it to stop handling a background task's events.
ArkTS.Worker.on: Adds an event listener to a worker so it runs when the specified event occurs. Use it to react to messages or events from a background task.
ArkTS.Worker.once: Adds an event listener to a worker that runs only once, then removes itself. Use it to handle a single event from a background task.
ArkTS.Worker.postMessage: Sends data to a worker thread, transferring the given buffers with it. Use it to pass work or data to a background task.
ArkTS.Worker.terminate: Stops a worker thread so it no longer receives messages. Use it to shut down background work when it is no longer needed.
ArkTS.WorkerEventTarget.addEventListener: Adds a listener that runs when a specified event occurs on a worker thread. Use it to react to messages or events sent to a worker.
ArkTS.WorkerEventTarget.dispatchEvent: Sends an event to a worker thread so its listeners run. Use it to trigger event handling in a worker.
ArkTS.WorkerEventTarget.removeAllListene: Removes every event listener from a worker thread. Use it to stop all event handling in a worker at once.
ArkTS.WorkerEventTarget.removeEventListe: Removes a listener for a given event type from a worker thread. Use it to stop reacting to a specific event in a worker.
ArkTS.Writable.cork: Buffers later writes instead of sending them immediately, improving performance for many small writes. Use it when writing lots of data in a row, then release with uncork.
ArkTS.Writable.doInitialize: Sets up a writable stream when it starts, so data can be written to a file, response, or output. Implement it to prepare your own stream for writing.

ArkTS.Writable.end: Finishes writing to a stream, optionally writing one last piece of data first. Use it to close a file or output after you are done saving.
ArkTS.Writable.off: Stops listening for events on a writable stream by removing a previously added callback. Use it when you no longer want to be notified about stream events.
ArkTS.Writable.on: Listens for events on a writable stream by registering a callback. Use it to react when something happens while data is being written.
ArkTS.Writable.setDefaultEncoding: Sets the default encoding used when writing data to a stream. Use it to control how text is encoded before it is written to a file or output.
ArkTS.Writable.uncork: Releases a paused stream and flushes any buffered data to its destination. Use it after corking to resume writing and send the held data on its way.
ArkTS.Writable.write: Writes data into a stream's buffer, reporting whether more room remains. Use it to send text or bytes to a file, output, or another stream.

ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.getOutput: Returns the generated XML as an ArrayBuffer. Use it to retrieve the finished XML document for saving or sending.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setAttributes: Writes an attribute with a name and value onto the current XML element. Use it when building an XML file to add attributes to a tag.

ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setComment: Writes a comment into the XML being generated. Use it to add notes or explanations inside an XML file you are building.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setDeclaratio: Writes the XML declaration with encoding, such as the version and encoding line. Use it at the start when generating an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setDocType: Writes the DOCTYPE declaration into the XML being generated. Use it to declare the document type when building an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setNamespace: Writes a namespace with a prefix and URI for the current element tag. Use it to define namespaces when generating an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.setText: Writes text content into an XML element while building an XML file. Use it to add the text that goes inside an element you are creating.
ArkTS.XmlDynamicSerializer.startElement: Writes an opening tag for a named element while building an XML file. Use it to begin a new element before adding its content.
ArkTS.XmlPullParser.parse: Starts reading and parsing an existing XML file. Use it to process XML data from a file.
ArkTS.XmlPullParser.parseXml: Parses XML information from a given source. Use it to read and interpret XML content.
ArkTS.XmlSAXHandler.characters: A callback triggered when text content is encountered while handling XML. Use it to capture the text inside XML elements as they are read.
ArkTS.XmlSAXHandler.endDocument: A callback triggered when the end of an XML document is reached. Use it to run finishing steps after all XML content has been handled.
ArkTS.XmlSAXHandler.endElement: Handles the end of an element while reading XML. Use it to know when a tag closes as you process a document.
ArkTS.XmlSAXHandler.startDocument: Handles the start of an XML document. Use it to begin processing when reading an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlSAXHandler.startElement: Handles the start of an element while reading XML, including its name and attributes. Use it to read each tag and its attributes as you process a document.
ArkTS.XmlSAXParser.parse: Parses XML in a streaming manner using a handler. Use it to read and process an XML document piece by piece.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.addEmptyElement: Adds an empty element to the XML being generated. Use it to write a self-closing tag when building an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.endElement: Writes the end tag of the current element. Use it to close a tag when building an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setAttributes: Adds an attribute with a name and value to the current element while building an XML file. Use it to give an element extra details such as an id or label.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setCDATA: Adds text inside a CDATA tag so it is treated as raw data in the XML file being built. Use it to include content that should not be parsed as markup.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setComment: Adds a comment to the XML file being generated. Use it to leave notes or explanations inside the document.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setDeclaration: Writes the XML file declaration, including the encoding, at the start of the generated file. Use it to begin an XML document properly.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setDocType: Sets the document type declaration for the XML file being generated. Use it to state the document type of the XML you are building.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setNamespace: Sets a namespace, with a prefix, for an element tag and its child elements in the XML file being built. Use it to group elements under a named namespace.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.setText: Sets the text content of an XML tag. Use it to write the value inside an element when building an XML file.
ArkTS.XmlSerializer.startElement: Writes the opening tag for an element with the given name. Use it to begin an element while generating an XML file.

ArkTS.buffer.from: Creates a new buffer from an array or shared memory. Use it to turn binary data into a buffer for storage or processing.
ArkTS.buffer.isBuffer: Checks whether an object is a buffer. Use it to confirm a value holds binary data before working with it.
ArkTS.buffer.isEncoding: Checks whether an encoding format is supported. Use it to confirm text encoding is valid before converting data.
ArkTS.buffer.transcode: Converts a buffer from one encoding format to another. Use it to change text encoding, such as from UTF-8 to another format.

ArkTS.fastbuffer.allocUninitializedFromP: Creates a new binary buffer of a given size from a shared pool, without filling it with initial data. Use it to set aside a block of bytes when you will write the contents yourself.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.byteLength: Tells you how many bytes a string or binary data takes up when encoded. Use it to find the real byte size of text before storing or sending it.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.compare: Compares two binary buffers and reports which one comes first when sorted. Use it to sort or check whether two blocks of binary data are equal.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.concat: Joins several binary buffers together into one new buffer. Use it to combine pieces of binary data into a single block.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.from: Creates a new FastBuffer from an array of bytes or other binary data. Use it to hold raw binary data for reading or processing.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.isBuffer: Checks whether an object is a FastBuffer and returns true or false. Use it to tell binary data apart from other objects.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.isEncoding: Checks whether a character encoding name is supported and returns true or false. Use it to validate an encoding before converting text to bytes.
ArkTS.fastbuffer.transcode: Re-encodes binary data from one character encoding to another. Use it to convert text bytes between encodings.
ArkTS.json.has: Checks whether a parsed JSON object contains a given key. Use it to see if a field exists in JSON data.
ArkTS.json.parse: Parses a JSON string into an object, array, or value. Use it to read data from JSON text.
ArkTS.json.remove: Removes a key from an object, typically after parsing JSON text. Use it to delete an unwanted field from parsed data.
ArkTS.json.stringify: Converts an object or array into JSON text. Use it to turn data into a JSON string for saving or sending.
ArkTS.process.abort: Aborts a process and generates a core file, causing it to exit immediately. Use it to force a process to stop right away.
ArkTS.process.chdir: Changes the current working directory to the given path. Use it to make file operations happen in a different folder.
ArkTS.process.cwd: Returns the current working directory. Use it to find out which folder the program is currently working in.
ArkTS.process.exit: Terminates the process, exiting the application. Use it to end the app with a chosen exit code.
ArkTS.process.getEnvironmentVar: Obtains the value of an environment variable by name. Use it to read a stored environment setting.
ArkTS.process.getPastCpuTime: Obtains the CPU time in milliseconds from process start to now. Use it to measure how much CPU time the process has used.
ArkTS.process.getStartRealtime: Tells how long the system has been running, excluding sleep time, when the process started, in milliseconds. Use it to measure uptime or how long since the process began.
ArkTS.process.getSystemConfig: Reads a system configuration value by its parameter name. Use it to look up a system setting your app needs.
ArkTS.process.getThreadPriority: Gets the priority of a thread from its thread ID. Use it to check how important a thread is scheduled to be.
ArkTS.process.getUidForName: Looks up the user ID that belongs to a given user name in the system user database. Use it to find a user's ID from their name.
ArkTS.process.is64Bit: Checks whether the process is running in a 64-bit environment. Use it to tell if the app is running as 64-bit.
ArkTS.process.isAppUid: Checks whether a given user ID belongs to this application. Use it to tell if a user ID is your own app's.
ArkTS.process.isIsolatedProcess: Checks whether the current process is isolated. Use it to find out if the app is running in a restricted, isolated process.
ArkTS.process.kill: Sends a signal to a chosen process to terminate it. Use it to stop or end another running process.
ArkTS.process.off: Removes a previously registered event handler so it no longer runs. Use it to stop listening for an event you no longer need.
ArkTS.process.on: Registers a handler that runs when a chosen event happens. Use it to react to events while your app is running.
ArkTS.process.runCmd: Starts a new child process to run a shell command and returns an object for it. Use it to run command-line tasks from your app.
ArkTS.process.uptime: Gets how long the current system has been running, in seconds. Use it to check system uptime.
ArkTS.taskpool.cancel: Cancels a task in the task pool so a queued task will not run. Use it to stop a background job you no longer need.
ArkTS.taskpool.execute: Queues a task to run on a worker thread and returns its result. Use it to run heavy work in the background without blocking the app.
ArkTS.taskpool.executeDelayed: Runs a task after a set delay and returns its result. Use it to schedule background work to start later.
ArkTS.taskpool.executePeriodically: Runs a task over and over at a set time interval, in milliseconds. Use it for work that must repeat on a schedule, such as polling or refreshing data in the background.
ArkTS.taskpool.getTask: Finds a task instance by its task ID, or by task ID and task name. Use it to look up a task you started so you can check or manage it.
ArkTS.taskpool.getTaskPoolInfo: Gets the thread and task information of the task pool. Use it to see how busy the pool is and what tasks are running.
ArkTS.taskpool.isConcurrent: Checks whether a function is a concurrent function. Use it to confirm a function can run in the background before scheduling it.
ArkTS.taskpool.terminateTask: Stops a long-running continuous task in the task pool. Use it to end a background task once its work is done and free the thread.
ArkTS.types.isAnyArrayBuffer: Checks whether a value is an ArrayBuffer or SharedArrayBuffer. Use it to confirm a value is binary buffer data before working with it.
ArkTS.types.isArgumentsObject: Checks whether a value is an arguments object. Use it to confirm a value is an arguments object before treating it as one.
ArkTS.types.isArrayBuffer: Checks whether a value is an ArrayBuffer. Use it to confirm a value holds raw binary data before working with it.
ArkTS.types.isArrayBufferView: Checks whether a value is an ArrayBufferView. Use it to confirm a value is a typed view over binary data before reading it.
ArkTS.types.isAsyncFunction: Checks whether a value is an asynchronous function. Use it to confirm a value is an async function before calling it.

ArkTS.types.isBigUint64Array: Checks whether a value is a BigUint64Array. Use it to confirm a value's type before working with it, avoiding type errors.
ArkTS.types.isBooleanObject: Checks whether a value is a Boolean. Use it to confirm a value is a Boolean before using it as one.
ArkTS.types.isBoxedPrimitive: Checks whether a value is a boxed Boolean, Number, String, or Symbol. Use it to confirm a value's type before working with it, avoiding type errors.
ArkTS.types.isDataView: Checks whether a value is a DataView. Use it to confirm a value is a DataView before reading or writing binary data.
ArkTS.types.isDate: Checks whether a value is a Date. Use it to confirm a value is a date before showing or formatting a date.
ArkTS.types.isExternal: Checks whether a value is a native external type. Use it to confirm a value comes from native code before handling it.
ArkTS.types.isFloat32Array: Checks whether a value is a Float32Array. Use it to confirm a value is a 32-bit float array before processing numeric data.
ArkTS.types.isFloat64Array: Checks whether a value is a Float64Array. Use it to confirm a value is a 64-bit float array before processing numeric data.
ArkTS.types.isGeneratorFunction: Checks whether a value is a generator function. Use it to confirm a value can be run as a generator before calling it.
ArkTS.types.isGeneratorObject: Checks whether a value is a generator object. Use it to confirm a value is a generator before stepping through its values.
ArkTS.types.isInt16Array: Checks whether a value is an Int16Array. Use it to confirm a value holds 16-bit integer data before reading it.
ArkTS.types.isInt32Array: Checks whether a value is an Int32Array. Use it to confirm a value holds 32-bit integer data before reading it.
ArkTS.types.isInt8Array: Checks whether a value is an Int8Array. Use it to confirm a value holds 8-bit integer data before reading it.
ArkTS.types.isMap: Checks whether a value is a Map. Use it to confirm a value stores key-value pairs before looking up entries.
ArkTS.types.isMapIterator: Checks whether a value is a Map iterator. Use it to confirm something is a Map iterator before looping through it.
ArkTS.types.isModuleNamespaceObject: Checks whether a value is a module namespace object. Use it to confirm a value is a module namespace object before using it.
ArkTS.types.isNativeError: Checks whether a value is an Error. Use it to confirm a value is an error before handling or showing it.
ArkTS.types.isNumberObject: Checks whether a value is a Number object. Use it to confirm a value is a number object before doing number work.
ArkTS.types.isPromise: Checks whether a value is a promise. Use it to confirm a value is a promise before waiting on it.
ArkTS.types.isProxy: Checks whether a value is a proxy. Use it to confirm a value is a proxy before working with it.
ArkTS.types.isRegExp: Checks whether a value is a regular expression object. Use it to confirm a value is a regular expression before matching or replacing text.
ArkTS.types.isSet: Checks whether a value is a Set. Use it to confirm a value is a Set before adding or reading unique items.
ArkTS.types.isSetIterator: Checks whether a value is a Set iterator. Use it to confirm a value is a Set iterator before stepping through Set items.
ArkTS.types.isSharedArrayBuffer: Checks whether a value is a SharedArrayBuffer. Use it to confirm a value is a shared buffer before reading or writing shared data.
ArkTS.types.isStringObject: Checks whether a value is a string object. Use it to confirm a value is a string object before treating it as text.
ArkTS.types.isSymbolObject: Checks whether a value is a symbol object. Use it to confirm a value is a symbol object before using it as a unique key.
ArkTS.types.isTypedArray: Checks whether a value is a TypedArray. Use it to confirm a value is a typed array before working with binary data.
ArkTS.types.isUint16Array: Checks whether a value is a Uint16Array. Use it to confirm a value is an unsigned 16-bit integer array before processing it.

ArkTS.types.isUint8Array: Checks whether a value is a Uint8Array. Use it to confirm a value is an unsigned 8-bit integer array before processing it.
ArkTS.types.isUint8ClampedArray: Checks whether a value is a Uint8ClampedArray. Use it to confirm a value is a clamped 8-bit integer array before processing it.
