ArkUI.LazyWaterFlowLayoutAttribute.onVis: Runs when the first or last visible item in the layout changes, and once at startup. Use it to react to scrolling, such as loading more items or tracking what is on screen.
ArkUI.LazyWaterFlowLayoutAttribute.rowsG: Sets the spacing between rows in a waterflow layout. Use it to add breathing room between rows of items like cards or images.
ArkUI.LazyWaterFlowLayoutAttribute.stick: Sets whether the header and footer stay fixed while the content scrolls. Use it to keep a header or footer visible in a scrolling waterflow list.
ArkUI.LevelOrder.clamp: Creates a dialog box level with the given display order, limiting values to the allowed range. Use it to control how far forward or back a dialog box appears.
ArkUI.LevelOrder.getOrder: Gets the display order of a dialog box. Use it to check how far forward or back a dialog box is set to appear.
ArkUI.LiveViewInfo.getLongTermTaskId: Gets the long-term task ID for a live view. Use it to identify a running image generation task.
ArkUI.LiveViewInfo.getWant: Gets the Want object for a live view. Use it to find the details of the task behind a live view.
ArkUI.LiveViewInfo.isLiveViewNeeded: Checks whether a live view is needed. Use it to decide whether to show a live preview during AI image generation.
ArkUI.LuminanceSampler.offBackgroundLumi: Stops listening for background luminance color picking changes. Use it to stop adapting your app's colors when the background brightness changes.
ArkUI.LuminanceSampler.onBackgroundLumin: Starts listening for background luminance color picking changes and reports the current background brightness. Use it to adapt your app's colors when the background brightness changes.
ArkUI.LuminanceSampler.setBackgroundLumi: Sets the parameters for background luminance color picking, including the brightness and dark thresholds. Use it to tune when your app reacts to background brightness changes.
ArkUI.Magnifier.bind: Attaches the magnifier to a component by its ID so its content can be enlarged. Use it to let someone zoom in and see details of a specific component.
ArkUI.Magnifier.show: Shows the magnifier centered on a point within the bound component. Use it to enlarge and inspect details at a chosen spot on a component.
ArkUI.Magnifier.unbind: Detaches the magnifier from the current component. Use it to stop enlarging a component's content.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.combine: Combines two matrices into one new matrix, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to merge two transformations, such as a rotation and a scale, into a single effect.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.copy: Makes a copy of this matrix. Use it to keep the original transformation while trying out changes on a duplicate.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.invert: Inverts this matrix, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to undo a transformation, such as reversing a rotation or scale.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.rotate: Rotates this matrix around the x, y, and z axes, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to turn a shape or image.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.scale: Scales this matrix along the x, y, and z axes, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to make a shape or image bigger or smaller.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.setPolyToPoly: Maps the corner points of one polygon onto another. Use it to stretch or skew a shape so it fits a different outline.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.skew: Skews a matrix along the x and y axes, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to slant or tilt a shape or image.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.transformPoint: Applies the current matrix transformation to a coordinate point and returns the transformed point. Use it to find where a point moves after a transform.
ArkUI.Matrix4Transit.translate: Moves a matrix along the x, y, and z axes, changing the matrix it is called on. Use it to shift a shape or image to a new position.
ArkUI.MeasureText.measureText: Measures the single-line display width of text, returning the width of the longest line for multi-line text. Use it to find how wide text will be before drawing it.
ArkUI.MeasureText.measureTextSize: Measures the width and height of the given text. Use it to find how much space text will take up before laying it out.
ArkUI.MeasureUtils.getParagraphs: Converts a styled string into an array of paragraph objects based on text layout options. Use it to break styled text into paragraphs for layout.
ArkUI.MeasureUtils.measureText: Measures the display width of given text, returning the width of the longest line for multi-line text. Use it to check how wide a piece of text will appear before laying it out.
ArkUI.MeasureUtils.measureTextSize: Measures the width and height of a single line of text. Use it to find out how much space text will take up before placing it on screen.
ArkUI.MediaQuery.matchMedia: Queries a media item and returns a list object for it. Use it to check whether the current screen or device matches a media condition.
ArkUI.MediaQuery.matchMediaSync: Sets media query criteria and returns a listening handle for them. Use it to watch for changes in screen or device conditions.
ArkUI.MediaQueryList.addListener: Adds a listening function that runs when the media query result changes. Use it to react when the screen or device conditions change.
ArkUI.MediaQueryList.removeListener: Removes a listening function so it no longer runs when the media query result changes. Use it to stop reacting to screen or device condition changes.
ArkUI.MediaQueryListener.off: Stops a media query listener so its callback no longer runs when media attributes change. Use it to stop reacting to screen size or orientation changes.
ArkUI.MediaQueryListener.on: Registers a media query listener whose callback runs when media attributes change. Use it to react when the screen size or orientation changes.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.addComponentContent: Adds a component content node as an overlay, centered on the page by default. Use it to show a floating popup or overlay on top of the page.
Creates an overlay node with a chosen display order so you control how overlays stack. Use it to show floating popups layered above or below each other.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.hideAllComponentCon: Hides all overlay component content nodes at once. Use it to dismiss every floating popup or overlay on the page.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.hideComponentConten: Hides one specified overlay component content node. Use it to dismiss a particular floating popup or overlay.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.openOrderOverlay: Opens an overlay with the given content and options, centered on the page by default. Use it to show a floating panel or pop-up layer above the current screen.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.removeComponentCont: Removes a specified node from the overlay manager. Use it to take down an overlay you previously added.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.showAllComponentCon: Shows all overlay content nodes managed by the overlay manager. Use it to bring back every overlay that was hidden.
ArkUI.OverlayManager.showComponentConten: Shows a specified overlay content node. Use it to make a hidden overlay visible again.
ArkUI.PathShape.commands: Sets the drawing commands that define a path shape. Use it to describe the outline used for clipping or masking a shape.
ArkUI.PersistenceV2.globalConnect: Stores key-value data on the application disk and returns the existing value or a newly created default. Use it to keep app state saved so it survives restarts.
ArkUI.PersistenceV2.notifyOnError: Registers a callback that runs when saving data for persistence fails. Use it to detect and handle problems when your app tries to keep its state saved.
ArkUI.PersistenceV2.save: Saves the data for a given key or type so it is kept persistently. Use it to store app state so it survives after the app is closed and reopened.
ArkUI.PiPController.getPiPSettingSwitch: Checks whether the auto-start picture-in-picture switch is turned on in Settings. Use it to find out if picture-in-picture can start automatically.
ArkUI.PiPController.getPiPWindowInfo: Gets information about the current picture-in-picture window. Use it to find out details of the small floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.isPiPActive: Checks whether the picture-in-picture window is currently active and visible. Use it to tell if the small floating video window is showing.
ArkUI.PiPController.isPiPSupported: Tells you whether picture-in-picture is supported. Use it to check before showing a video in a small floating window.
ArkUI.PiPController.off: Stops listening for picture-in-picture action events. Use it to stop reacting to changes in the small floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.offActiveStatusChang: Stops listening for changes to whether picture-in-picture is active. Use it to stop being told when a floating video window turns on or off.
ArkUI.PiPController.offControlEvent: Stops listening for control events from a picture-in-picture window. Use it to stop receiving button presses on a floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.offControlPanelActio: Stops listening for picture-in-picture lifecycle events. Use it to stop being told about the life of a floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.offPipWindowSizeChan: Stops listening for picture-in-picture window size changes. Use it to stop being told when a floating video window is resized.
ArkUI.PiPController.offStateChange: Stops listening for picture-in-picture lifecycle state changes. Use it to stop being told when a floating video window changes state.
ArkUI.PiPController.on: Starts listening for picture-in-picture events, such as when the floating video window turns active or is resized. Use it to react while a video plays in a small floating window.
ArkUI.PiPController.onActiveStatusChange: Watches whether picture-in-picture is currently active and tells you when that changes. Use it to know when a floating video window opens or closes.
ArkUI.PiPController.onControlEvent: Listens for control events from a picture-in-picture window. Use it to react when someone taps controls on the floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.onControlPanelAction: Listens for actions taken on the picture-in-picture control panel. Use it to respond when someone presses a button on the floating window's controls.
ArkUI.PiPController.onPipWindowSizeChang: Watches the size of the picture-in-picture window and tells you when it changes. Use it to adjust content when the floating video window is resized.
ArkUI.PiPController.onStateChange: Listens for changes in the picture-in-picture control state. Use it to track when the floating video window's state changes.
ArkUI.PiPController.setAutoStartEnabled: Chooses whether the floating picture-in-picture window opens by itself when the app goes to the background. Use it to make a video keep playing in a small window when you leave the app.
ArkUI.PiPController.setPiPControlEnabled: Turns a control shown on the picture-in-picture window on or off. Use it to enable or disable buttons like play, pause, or mute in a small floating video window.
ArkUI.PiPController.startPiP: Starts a picture-in-picture window. Use it to show a small floating window, such as a video that keeps playing while you use other apps.
ArkUI.PiPController.stopPiP: Stops a picture-in-picture window. Use it to close the small floating window when you are done watching.
ArkUI.PiPController.updateContentNode: Replaces the content shown in a picture-in-picture window. Use it to switch what is displayed in the small floating window.
ArkUI.PiPController.updateContentSize: Updates the size of the media shown in a picture-in-picture window. Use it to keep the small floating window's shape right when the video size changes.
ArkUI.PiPController.updatePiPControlStat: Updates the status of a control shown on the picture-in-picture window. Use it to show whether a button like play, pause, or mute is on or off in the small floating window.
ArkUI.PiPWindow.create: Creates a controller for picture-in-picture, letting you add a custom UI node and start or stop a floating mini window. Use it to keep a video or call playing in a small window while using other apps.
ArkUI.PiPWindow.isPiPEnabled: Checks whether the current device supports picture-in-picture. Use it to decide whether to offer a floating mini window for video or calls.
ArkUI.PictureDrawableDescriptor.setHdrCo: Sets the HDR composition for a picture. Use it to control how high dynamic range images are combined when displayed.
ArkUI.Prompt.showActionMenu: Shows a menu of actions for the user to choose from. Use it to offer choices such as save, share, or delete.
ArkUI.Prompt.showDialog: Shows a dialog box. Use it to ask the user to confirm something or enter information.
ArkUI.Prompt.showToast: Shows a short notification text. Use it to briefly tell the user something, like a saved or failed message.
ArkUI.PromptAction.closeCustomDialog: Closes a custom dialog box using the ID returned when it was opened. Use it to dismiss a custom popup after the user is done with it.
ArkUI.PromptAction.closeMenu: Closes the menu shown for the given content. Use it to dismiss an action menu after the user picks an option or taps away.
ArkUI.PromptAction.closePopup: Closes the popup shown for the given content. Use it to dismiss a popup after the user finishes with it.
ArkUI.PromptAction.closeToast: Closes the specified toast using the ID returned when it was shown. Use it to hide a brief message before it disappears on its own.
ArkUI.PromptAction.getBottomOrder: Returns the order of the dialog box currently at the bottom layer. Use it to decide the stacking order for dialog boxes you show next.
ArkUI.PromptAction.getTopOrder: Returns the order of the dialog box currently at the top layer. Use it to decide the stacking order for dialog boxes you show next.
ArkUI.PromptAction.openCustomDialog: Shows a custom dialog box and returns its ID so you can close it later. Use it to pop up your own dialog, such as a confirmation or sign-in prompt.
ArkUI.PromptAction.openCustomDialogWithC: Shows a custom dialog box whose content follows your own styling, with a controller to manage it afterwards. Use it to display a custom popup you can later control.
ArkUI.PromptAction.openMenu: Opens a menu with your chosen content attached to a target component. Use it to show a context or options menu when someone taps something.
ArkUI.PromptAction.openPopup: Creates and shows a popup with your chosen content attached to a target component. Use it to display a small popup near a button or item.
ArkUI.PromptAction.openToast: Shows a brief toast message and returns its ID so you can close it. Use it to flash a short notice like "saved" on screen.
ArkUI.PromptAction.presentCustomDialog: Shows a custom dialog box and returns its ID, optionally with a controller to manage it. Use it to present your own dialog, such as a confirmation prompt.
ArkUI.PromptAction.showActionMenu: Shows an action menu with the given settings. Use it to offer someone a list of choices to pick from.
ArkUI.PromptAction.showDialog: Creates and displays a dialog box. Use it to ask someone a question or show a message that needs a response.
ArkUI.PromptAction.showToast: Creates and displays a toast. Use it to briefly show a short message on screen, like a quick confirmation.
ArkUI.PromptAction.updateCustomDialog: Updates a custom dialog box's alignment, offset, auto-cancel, or mask color. Use it to change how an open custom dialog looks or behaves.
ArkUI.PromptAction.updateMenu: Updates the style of a menu. Use it to change how an open menu looks while it is showing.
ArkUI.PromptAction.updatePopup: Updates the style of a popup. Use it to change how an open popup looks while it is showing.
ArkUI.RectShape.radius: Sets how round the corners of a rectangle are, either one value for all corners or four values for each corner. Use it to round off the corners of a shape used to clip or mask content.
ArkUI.RectShape.radiusHeight: Sets the vertical radius of a rectangle's rounded corners. Use it to control how tall the corner curves are on a shape that clips or masks content.
ArkUI.RectShape.radiusWidth: Sets the horizontal radius of a rectangle's rounded corners. Use it to control how wide the corner curves are on a shape that clips or masks content.
ArkUI.Router.back: Returns to the previous page or to a page with a given URL. Use it to go back after navigating forward.
ArkUI.Router.clear: Removes all earlier pages from the page history, keeping only the page currently shown. Use it to stop someone from going back to previous screens.
ArkUI.Router.disableAlertBeforeBackPage: Turns off the confirmation dialog that appears before going back to the previous page. Use it when you no longer want users asked to confirm leaving a page.
ArkUI.Router.enableAlertBeforeBackPage: Shows a confirmation dialog before going back to the previous page. Use it to ask users to confirm before they leave a page.
ArkUI.Router.getLength: Tells you how many pages are currently in the page stack. Use it to check how many pages deep the user has navigated.
ArkUI.Router.getParams: Gets the parameters that were passed in when navigating to the current page. Use it to read data handed over from the previous page.
ArkUI.Router.getStackSize: Tells you how many pages are currently in the page stack. Use it to check how many pages deep the user has navigated.
ArkUI.Router.getState: Gets state information about the current page. Use it to find out where the user is in the page stack.
ArkUI.Router.getStateByIndex: Gets the status information of a page at a given position in the stack. Use it to look up details about a specific page in the navigation history.
ArkUI.Router.getStateByUrl: Gets the status information of a page by its web address. Use it to look up details about a page in the navigation history by its address.
ArkUI.Router.hideAlertBeforeBackPage: Turns off the confirmation dialog that appears before going back to the previous page. Use it to let the user go back without being asked to confirm.
ArkUI.Router.push: Opens a specified page in the app. Use it to go to another screen, like tapping a button to open a settings or details page.
ArkUI.Router.pushNamedRoute: Opens a page by its named route, with a choice of routing mode. Use it to go to another screen in the app by name.
ArkUI.Router.pushUrl: Opens a specified page in the app, with a choice of routing mode. Use it to go to another screen, like opening a details page.
ArkUI.Router.replace: Replaces the current page with another page and removes the current one. Use it to swap screens so the user cannot go back to the old one.
ArkUI.Router.replaceNamedRoute: Replaces the current page with another page by its named route and removes the current one. Use it to swap screens by name so the old one is gone.
ArkUI.Router.replaceUrl: Replaces the current page with another page and removes the current one, with a choice of routing mode. Use it to swap screens so the old one is gone.
ArkUI.Router.showAlertBeforeBackPage: Shows a confirm dialog box before going back to the previous page. Use it to ask the user to confirm leaving a page, such as when unsaved changes might be lost.
ArkUI.Screen.setDensityDpi: Sets the pixel density of the screen. Use it to adjust how large content appears on the display.
ArkUI.Screen.setOrientation: Sets the screen orientation, but only if it matches the app's rotation policy. Use it to lock or rotate the display to a chosen orientation.
ArkUI.Screen.setScreenActiveMode: Sets the active display mode of the screen by its mode index. Use it to switch the screen's resolution or refresh rate.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.bindSe: Binds a custom menu that appears when text is selected. Use it to offer actions like copy or share on the selected text.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.caretC: Sets the color of the caret shown in selected text. Use it to make the text cursor match your app's theme.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.copyOp: Sets whether selected text can be copied and where it can be copied to. Use it to allow or restrict copying text in your app.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.editMe: Sets a custom menu for selected text, including its text, icon, and action. Use it to add your own options to the text selection menu.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.enable: Turns haptic feedback on or off. Use it to make the device vibrate when the user selects text.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.onCopy: Runs when selected text is copied. Use it to react to a user copying text.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.onText: Runs when the text selection changes. Use it to track which text a user has selected.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.onWill: Runs just before the copy menu copies text. Use it to react before a user copies text.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.select: Sets the background color of selected text. Use it to highlight the text a user has selected.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerAttribute.textJo: Sets how aggregated text is joined together. Use it to control how copied or selected text is combined.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerController.clear: Clears the current text selection and closes the selection menu. Use it to deselect text and dismiss the menu.
ArkUI.SelectionContainerController.close: Closes the custom or default selection menu of a selection container. Use it to dismiss the menu that appears when text is selected.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.delay: Sets how long an animation waits before it starts playing, in milliseconds. Use it to delay when an animation begins.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.direction: Sets the playback direction of an animation, such as forward or reverse. Use it to control which way an animation plays.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.duration: Sets how long an animation lasts, in milliseconds. Use it to make an animation play faster or slower.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.easing: Sets the interpolation curve that controls the speed changes of an animation. Use it to make an animation ease in, ease out, or move at a steady pace.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.fill: Sets the fill mode that decides how an animated element looks before the animation starts and after it ends. Use it to keep an element in its final state once the animation finishes.
ArkUI.SimpleAnimatorOptions.iterations: Sets how many times an animation plays. Use it to repeat an animation, or to loop it forever with -1.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.clearMonito: Removes all monitoring callbacks registered for the current UI context. Use it to stop receiving smart gesture monitoring updates.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.clearSelect: Clears the currently selected node for smart gestures. Use it to deselect the component that was highlighted for gesture selection.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.enableSmart: Turns the tap and slide operations of smart gestures on or off. Use it to allow or block tap and slide gesture handling.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.registerMon: Registers a callback that receives the system's default handling of a smart gesture before it is processed, so the app can intervene. Use it to customize how smart gestures are handled.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.requestSele: Requests that a specified component become the current smart gesture selected node, showing a selection prompt box. Use it to highlight a component for smart gesture selection.
ArkUI.SmartGestureController.unregisterM: Removes a previously registered smart gesture monitoring callback. Use it to stop receiving monitoring updates for smart gestures.
ArkUI.SpringLoadingContext.abort: Stops further hover detection during a drag. Use it to end drag hover handling and clean up state yourself.
ArkUI.SpringLoadingContext.updateConfigu: Changes the hover detection settings while a drag hover is in its beginning state. Use it to adjust how a drag hover responds before detection continues.
ArkUI.SwiperContentTransitionProxy.finis: Tells the swiper that its custom page transition animation has finished playing. Use it to signal the end of a custom swipe animation.
ArkUI.TextGenerationModel.cancelTextGene: Cancels an AI text generation task for the given session. Use it to stop text that is being generated.
ArkUI.TextGenerationModel.onComplain: Reports a complaint about the result of an AI-generated text task. Use it when a user complains about generated text.
ArkUI.TextGenerationModel.requestTextGen: Requests an AI text generation task and receives the generated text. Use it to have text written for you.
ArkUI.TextMenuController.disableMenuItem: Turns off chosen system service items in the text selection menu. Use it to hide specific menu entries when text is selected.
ArkUI.TextMenuController.disableSystemSe: Turns off all system service items in the text selection menu. Use it to hide system menu entries when text is selected.
ArkUI.TextMenuController.setMenuOptions: Sets options for the text selection menu. Use it to control how the menu appears when text is selected.
ArkUI.ThemeControl.setDefaultTheme: Sets the default theme for the whole app or for the current page and pages opened later. Use it to apply a custom look to your app or page.
ArkUI.TransitionContext.completeTransiti: Completes a transition animation after animateTo has run. Use it to finish a screen transition animation.
ArkUI.TransitionController.animationForH: Customizes the animation played when a window is hidden. Use it to control how a window disappears from view.
ArkUI.TransitionController.animationForS: Customizes the animation played when a window is shown. Use it to control how a window appears on screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.addLocalInputEventMonito: Registers a monitor that watches input events within the current UI context and returns an identifier you save to cancel it later. Use it to detect taps, keys, or other input in one part of the screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.animateTo: Adds transition animations for state changes made inside the given closure. Use it to make a button, panel, or other element animate smoothly when it changes.
ArkUI.UIContext.animateToImmediately: Triggers an explicit animation right away using the given animation settings and closure. Use it to make a state change animate immediately without missing its end callback.
ArkUI.UIContext.bindTabsToNestedScrollab: Binds tabs to nested scrollable containers so the tab bar hides automatically as you scroll. Use it to give a page with nested scrolling a tab bar that slides away.
ArkUI.UIContext.bindTabsToScrollable: Binds tabs to a scrollable container so the tab bar hides automatically as you scroll. Use it to give a scrolling page a tab bar that slides away.
ArkUI.UIContext.clearResourceCache: Clears the cached resources loaded from app resource files. Use it to free cached resources, though pages may load resources more slowly afterward.
ArkUI.UIContext.closeBindSheet: Closes the sheet shown for the given sheet content. Use it to dismiss a pop-up sheet when the user is done with it.
ArkUI.UIContext.createAnimator: Creates an object for running animations. Use it to play an animation.
ArkUI.UIContext.createUIContextWithoutWi: Creates a UI instance that does not depend on a window and returns its context. Use it to set up UI without a window.
ArkUI.UIContext.destroyUIContextWithoutW: Destroys the UI instance created without a window. Use it to clean up that UI instance.
ArkUI.UIContext.dispatchKeyEvent: Sends a keyboard event to a specific UI element. Use it to simulate typing or key presses.
ArkUI.UIContext.enableEventPassthrough: Turns passing of raw input events through to lower layers on or off. Use it to let touches pass through to what is behind.
ArkUI.UIContext.enableSwipeBack: Turns swipe-to-go-back on or off. Use it to control whether swiping back navigates to the previous screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.fp2px: Converts a font-size value in fp units to pixels. Use it to turn a font size into screen pixels for layout or drawing.
ArkUI.UIContext.freezeUINode: Freezes or unfreezes a specific component so it stops being marked dirty and triggering layout updates. Use it to hold a component's layout steady while other parts of the screen change.
ArkUI.UIContext.getAllUIContexts: Gets all currently valid UI context instances, or an empty array if none exist. Use it to find every active UI context in the app.
ArkUI.UIContext.getAtomicServiceBar: Gets the atomic service bar. Use it to access the bar shown for an atomic service.
ArkUI.UIContext.getAttachedFrameNodeById: Gets the frame node attached to the current window by its id. Use it to look up a specific node in the window.
ArkUI.UIContext.getCallingScopeUIContext: Gets the UI context of the current calling scope, or undefined if the scope is unclear. Use it to find which UI context is in effect.
ArkUI.UIContext.getComponentSnapshot: Gets the component snapshot helper. Use it to capture a picture of a component.
ArkUI.UIContext.getComponentUtils: Gets a helper object for working with UI components. Use it when you need to inspect or measure parts of the screen layout.
ArkUI.UIContext.getContextMenuController: Gets a controller for context menus. Use it to show or manage the menu that pops up on a long press.
ArkUI.UIContext.getCursorController: Gets a controller for the text cursor. Use it to manage where the cursor sits while typing.
ArkUI.UIContext.getDialogPresenter: Gets an object for showing dialogs. Use it to pop up a dialog box on screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.getDragController: Gets a controller for drag operations. Use it to start or manage dragging items on screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.getFilteredInspectorTree: Gets the component tree and its attributes as a text string, for testing only. Use it to inspect what is on screen while testing an app.
Gets the attributes of a component and its child components as a JSON string, for testing. Use it to inspect a component's details and its children during testing.
ArkUI.UIContext.getFocusController: Gets the focus controller. Use it to manage which element has focus.
ArkUI.UIContext.getFont: Gets a font object. Use it to work with text fonts.
ArkUI.UIContext.getFrameNodeById: Gets a frame node by its id. Use it to find a component's node by id.
ArkUI.UIContext.getFrameNodeByUniqueId: Gets a frame node by its unique id. Use it to find a component's node by unique id.
ArkUI.UIContext.getHostContext: Gets the context of the current ability. Use it to access the ability's context.
ArkUI.UIContext.getId: Gets the unique ID of a UI instance object. Use it to tell different UI instances apart when managing several at once.
ArkUI.UIContext.getKeyboardAvoidMode: Gets the avoidance mode of the virtual keyboard. Use it to find out how the on-screen keyboard moves content out of its way.
ArkUI.UIContext.getLastFocusedUIContext: Gets the UI instance that most recently became focused. Use it to find which screen or window the user was last working in.
ArkUI.UIContext.getLastForegroundUIConte: Gets the UI instance that most recently came to the foreground. Use it to find which screen or window the user last had open on top.
ArkUI.UIContext.getLuminanceSampler: Gets the luminance sampler for a specified node, or nothing if the node is not found. Use it to read brightness information from a node on screen.
ArkUI.UIContext.getMagnifier: Gets a magnifier object that controls showing and hiding a magnifier. Use it to magnify part of the screen for easier reading.
ArkUI.UIContext.getMaxFontScale: Gets the largest font scale currently allowed. Use it to check how big text can be shown when supporting larger fonts.
ArkUI.UIContext.getMeasureUtils: Gets a tool for measuring text. Use it to find out how tall and wide a piece of text will be before placing it.
ArkUI.UIContext.getMediaQuery: Gets the media query object for the current UI context. Use it to check screen size or orientation so a layout can adapt.
ArkUI.UIContext.getNavigationInfoByUniqu: Gets the navigation information for a frame node by its unique ID. Use it to find out where a page sits in the navigation stack.
ArkUI.UIContext.getOverlayManager: Obtains the overlay manager object. Use it to show or hide floating overlays on top of the page.
ArkUI.UIContext.getOverlayManagerOptions: Gets the overlay manager options object. Use it to read the current settings that control how overlays are shown.

ArkUI.Window.onDisplayIdChange: Listens for the event that this window has moved to a different display. Use it to react when a window is dragged onto another screen.
ArkUI.Window.onFrameMetricsMeasured: Watches for changes in the window's frame measurements, reporting them when the screen content is redrawn. Use it to track layout shifts during page transitions or animations.
ArkUI.Window.onFreeWindowModeChange: Tells you when the window switches in or out of free window mode. Use it to react when a user moves a window into floating mode.
ArkUI.Window.onKeyboardDidHide: Notifies you after the on-screen keyboard has finished hiding. Use it to restore the layout once typing is done.
ArkUI.Window.onKeyboardDidShow: Notifies you after the on-screen keyboard has appeared. Use it to adjust the layout when the keyboard pops up for typing.
ArkUI.Window.onKeyboardHeightChange: Reports when the on-screen keyboard's height changes while it overlaps this window. Use it to keep content from being covered as the keyboard grows or shrinks.
ArkUI.Window.onKeyboardWillHide: Notifies you just before the on-screen keyboard hides. Use it to prepare the layout for the keyboard going away.
ArkUI.Window.onKeyboardWillShow: Tells you when the on-screen keyboard is about to appear in a window. Use it to adjust your layout before the keyboard shows up while typing.
ArkUI.Window.onMainWindowFullScreenAcros: Listens for changes to whether the main window is full-screen across multiple displays. Use it to react when the main window enters or leaves full-screen mode across displays.
ArkUI.Window.onNoInteractionDetected: Alerts you when no touching or physical keyboard input happens in a window for a set time. Use it to dim the screen or lock things after the user stops interacting.
ArkUI.Window.onOcclusionStateChanged: Tells you when a window's visibility changes because other windows cover it. Use it to pause or resume what is shown when a window is hidden or revealed.
ArkUI.Window.onRectChangeInGlobalDisplay: Tells you when a window moves or resizes on the screen. Use it to reposition or resize content when the window changes.
ArkUI.Window.onRotationChange: Tells you when the screen or window rotates. Use it to rearrange your layout when the device is turned sideways.
ArkUI.Window.onScreenshot: Tells you when a screenshot of the window is taken. Use it to react when the user captures the screen.
ArkUI.Window.onScreenshotAppEvent: Lets you know when a screenshot is taken. Use it to react to screenshots, such as showing a notification or saving the image.
ArkUI.Window.onSubWindowClose: Tells you when a child window is closed by the user clicking the system close button. Use it to clean up or update your app when a child window is dismissed that way.
ArkUI.Window.onSystemDensityChange: Tells you when the screen's display scale changes. Use it to adjust sizes or convert between virtual and physical pixels.
ArkUI.Window.onTouchOutside: Tells you when the user touches outside the window. Use it to close a popup or menu when the user taps elsewhere.
ArkUI.Window.onUiExtensionSecureLimitCha: Tells you when the secure limit of a UI extension in the window changes. Use it to update your app's behavior when security restrictions change.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowEvent: Tells you when the window's lifecycle changes. Use it to respond to window state changes like opening, closing, or resizing.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowHighlightChange: Watches whether the window's highlight state changes. Use it to react when a window becomes highlighted or loses its highlight.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowPostureModeChange: Watches for the window switching to a chosen posture mode. Use it to react when the device folds or unfolds into that posture.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowRectChange: Watches for changes to the window's position and size. Use it to react when the window is moved or resized.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowSizeChange: Watches for changes to the window's size. Use it to react when the window is resized.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowStatusChange: Watches for changes in the window's status, such as maximizing or recovering. Use it to react when the window switches between display states.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowStatusDidChange: Watches for window status changes after the window's position and size have been updated. Use it to react once the window has finished switching display states.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowTitleButtonRectChan: Watches for changes to the rectangle holding the minimize, maximize, and close buttons on a window's title bar. Use it to keep custom title bar layouts aligned when those buttons move or resize.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowVisibilityChange: Watches for changes to whether a window is visible. Use it to react when a window is shown or hidden, such as pausing or resuming what the window displays.
ArkUI.Window.onWindowWillClose: Watches for the moment a main or child window is about to be closed by the user clicking the close button in the system title bar. Use it to run cleanup or ask for confirmation before the window closes.
ArkUI.Window.opacity: Sets how see-through a window is, from fully transparent to fully opaque. Use it to fade a window in or out during a custom show or hide animation.
ArkUI.Window.raiseAboveTarget: Puts a child window above another child window. Use it to bring one child window in front of another.
ArkUI.Window.raiseMainWindowAboveTarget: Moves the main window above another main window in the same application, with child windows following. Use it to bring one main window in front of another.
ArkUI.Window.raiseToAppTop: Brings a child window to the top among child windows of the same type and parent in the app. Use it to bring a floating panel or popup window in front of its siblings.
ArkUI.Window.recover: Restores the main window from full-screen, maximized, or split-screen mode back to a floating window at its previous size and position. Use it to let someone return a full-screen window to a floating one.
ArkUI.Window.requestFocus: Asks this window to gain or lose focus. Use it to make a window take focus or give it up, for example when switching between windows.
ArkUI.Window.resetAspectRatio: Clears the saved aspect ratio of the window content layout, valid only for the main window. Use it to let a window go back to its default proportions after a fixed ratio was set.
ArkUI.Window.resetSize: Changes the size of a window from its top-left corner. Use it to make an app window bigger or smaller.
ArkUI.Window.resize: Changes the size of a window from its top-left corner. Use it to make an app window bigger or smaller.
ArkUI.Window.resizeAsync: Changes the size of a window from its top-left corner and reports the final result. Use it to make an app window bigger or smaller.
ArkUI.Window.restore: Brings a minimized main window back to the foreground at its previous size and position. Use it to reopen an app window that was minimized.
ArkUI.Window.restoreMainWindow: Brings the main window back to the foreground, or raises it if already there. Use it to return to the main app window from a floating window.
ArkUI.Window.rotate: Sets the rotation parameters for a window, used when customizing the animation played while a system window is shown or hidden.
ArkUI.Window.scale: Sets the scale parameters for a window, used when customizing the animation played while a system window is shown or hidden.
ArkUI.Window.setAspectRatio: Sets the width-to-height ratio of a window's content area. Use it to keep an app window in a fixed shape, such as a square or widescreen view.
ArkUI.Window.setBackdropBlur: Blurs the background area behind a window; make the window background transparent first so the blur shows through.
ArkUI.Window.setBackdropBlurStyle: Sets the blur style for the background behind a window.
ArkUI.Window.setBackgroundColor: Sets the background color of a window using a hexadecimal color code. Use it to give an app window a custom background color.
ArkUI.Window.setBlur: Blurs the window itself, with the radius controlling how strong the blur is.
ArkUI.Window.setBrightness: Sets the screen brightness for a window, from 0.0 (darkest) to 1.0 (brightest), or -1.0 to restore the system brightness. Use it to brighten or dim the screen while your app is shown.
ArkUI.Window.setColorSpace: Sets the color space used by a window. Use it to control how colors are displayed in your app window.
ArkUI.Window.setContentAspectRatio: Sets the aspect ratio of the window content area, excluding borders and title bars. Use it to keep your app's content at a fixed width-to-height ratio.
ArkUI.Window.setCornerRadius: Sets how rounded the corners of a window are.
ArkUI.Window.setDecorButtonStyle: Sets the button style of the window decoration bar. Use it to customize the look of the window's title bar buttons.
ArkUI.Window.setDefaultDensityEnabled: Sets whether the window uses the screen's default density, so its layout stays the same when the system display size changes. Use it to keep a window's layout fixed regardless of display size settings.
ArkUI.Window.setDialogBackGestureEnabled: Sets whether a modal window responds to the back gesture. Use it to let users swipe back to close a dialog.
ArkUI.Window.setDimBehind: Dims the window that is not on top, making it darker behind the active one. Use it to darken background windows so the front window stands out.
ArkUI.Window.setDragKeyFramePolicy: Sets the keyframe policy used when the main window is dragged. Use it to control how smoothly the main window moves while being dragged.
ArkUI.Window.setExclusivelyHighlighted: Makes a window take the highlight exclusively when it gains focus, so other windows in its chain lose theirs. Use it to keep only one window highlighted at a time.
ArkUI.Window.setFloatNavigationAvoidArea: Turns the float navigation avoid area on or off for a window. Use it to keep content clear of the floating navigation bar.
ArkUI.Window.setFocusable: Sets whether a window can gain focus when operated. Use it to stop a window from taking keyboard input or focus.
ArkUI.Window.setFollowParentMultiScreenP: Lets a child window span and show on multiple screens while its parent is dragged or resized. Use it to keep a child window visible across screens as the parent moves.
ArkUI.Window.setFollowParentWindowLayout: Makes a child or dialog window keep the same position and size as the main window. Use it so a pop-up or child window stays aligned with the main window.
ArkUI.Window.setForbidSplitMove: Sets whether the main window is forbidden to move while in split-screen mode. Use it to keep a window pinned in place during split-screen use.
ArkUI.Window.setFullScreen: Turns full-screen mode on or off for a window, letting content overlap the status bar and navigation bar. Use it to show content edge to edge, like a video or game.
ArkUI.Window.setGestureBackEnabled: Turns the side-swipe back gesture on or off for the main window. Use it to allow or block swiping from the edge to go back.
ArkUI.Window.setHandwritingFlag: Adds or removes a handwriting flag so the window responds to stylus events instead of touch events. Use it for handwriting or stylus input on a window.
ArkUI.Window.setImmersiveModeEnabledStat: Turns immersive layout on or off for the main window without changing its mode or size. Use it to let content extend under the status bar and navigation bar.
ArkUI.Window.setKeepScreenOn: Keeps the screen on or lets it turn off as usual. Use it while watching a video or reading so the screen does not dim.
ArkUI.Window.setLayoutFullScreen: Sets whether a window's layout is immersive, letting content overlap the status bar and navigation bar. Use it to lay out content edge to edge.
ArkUI.Window.setMainWindowRaiseByClickEn: Sets whether clicking the main window raises it and its child windows to the front. Use it to control whether clicking a window brings it forward.
ArkUI.Window.setOutsideTouchable: Sets whether the area outside a child window can be touched. Use it to let people tap outside a pop-up to interact with what is behind it.
ArkUI.Window.setParentWindow: Gives a child window a new parent window, such as a main window or another child window. Use it to move a pop-up or panel under a different window.
ArkUI.Window.setPreferredOrientation: Sets the preferred display orientation for a window, such as landscape or portrait. Use it to keep a screen the right way up for reading or watching.
ArkUI.Window.setPreferredOrientationWith: Sets the preferred display orientation for the main window and reports the result. Use it to rotate the screen to suit what someone is viewing.
ArkUI.Window.setPrivacyMode: Sets whether a window is in privacy mode, so it cannot be captured or recorded. Use it to hide sensitive content from screenshots or screen recording.
ArkUI.Window.setRaiseByClickEnabled: Sets whether clicking a child window brings it to the front among its siblings. Use it to control whether a tapped pop-up jumps above other windows.
ArkUI.Window.setReceiveDragEventEnabled: Turns on or off whether the current window can receive drag events. Use it to let a window accept or ignore items dragged onto it.
ArkUI.Window.setRelativePositionToParent: Keeps a first-level child window at a fixed position relative to the main window in freeform mode. Use it so a floating panel stays anchored beside the main window as it moves.
ArkUI.Window.setResizeByDragEnabled: Turns on or off resizing a decorated main or child window by dragging its edge. Use it to let someone resize a window by dragging.
ArkUI.Window.setRotationLocked: Locks or unlocks a system window's screen rotation, so its orientation stays fixed or follows the device. Use it to keep a window from rotating with the device.
ArkUI.Window.setSeparationTouchEnabled: Turns on or off the event separation state, so each finger tap goes to the window it hits. Use it to control how multi-finger taps are sent to windows.
ArkUI.Window.setShadow: Sets the shadow around the window borders, including its radius, color, and offset. Use it to give a window a shadowed border look.
ArkUI.Window.setSingleFrameComposerEnabl: Turns the single-frame composer on or off to cut the screen display delay of the rendering node. Use it for apps needing extremely low interaction latency.
ArkUI.Window.setSnapshotSkip: Sets whether this window is ignored during screen capture, recording, or casting. Use it to keep a window out of screenshots, recordings, or casts.
ArkUI.Window.setSpecificSystemBarEnabled: Shows or hides the status bar and three-button navigation bar of the main window, optionally with animation. Use it to hide the status bar for a full-screen view.
ArkUI.Window.setStatusBarColor: Sets the text color of the status bar in the main window. Use it to make the status bar clock and icons readable against your app's background.
ArkUI.Window.setSubWindowModal: Makes a child window modal so its parent window stops responding to touches until the child is closed or made non-modal. Use it to block interaction with the window behind a popup or dialog.
ArkUI.Window.setSubWindowZLevel: Sets the stacking level of a child window so it can be shown above or below other child windows. Use it to bring a floating panel to the front or push it behind others.
ArkUI.Window.setSupportedWindowModes: Sets which window modes an app window supports, such as full screen, split screen, or floating. Use it to control how your app window can be displayed on screen.
ArkUI.Window.setSystemAvoidAreaEnabled: Lets a floating, modal, or system window report the areas it should avoid, such as the status bar. Use it so your window can find out where system bars overlap it.
ArkUI.Window.setSystemBarEnable: Shows or hides the status bar and three-button navigation bar in the main window's full-screen mode. Use it to give an app a clean full-screen look.
ArkUI.Window.setSystemBarProperties: Sets the look of the status bar and navigation bar of the main window, such as their colors. Use it to match the system bars to your app's theme.
ArkUI.Window.setTitleAndDockHoverShown: Chooses whether the window title bar and dock bar appear when the cursor hovers over the hot zone in full-screen mode. Use it to control what shows when hovering in a full-screen window.
ArkUI.Window.setTitleButtonVisible: Shows or hides the maximize, minimize, and split-screen buttons on the main window title bar. Use it to control which title bar buttons appear.
ArkUI.Window.setTopmost: Pins the main window above all other windows. Use it to keep your window on top of everything else.
ArkUI.Window.setTouchable: Sets whether the window responds to touch. Use it to turn touch input on or off for a window.
ArkUI.Window.setTouchableAreas: Sets which areas of the window respond to touch, letting touches outside them pass through. Use it to make only part of a window touchable.
ArkUI.Window.setUIContent: Loads a page from a given path into the window. Use it to show a chosen page inside a window.
ArkUI.Window.setWakeUpScreen: Wakes up the screen. Use it to turn the screen on.
ArkUI.Window.setWaterMarkFlag: Turns a watermark flag on or off for a window. Use it to show or hide a watermark on a window.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowBackgroundColor: Sets the background color of the window. Use it to give a window the color you want behind its content.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowBrightness: Sets the brightness of the main window while it is in the foreground and focused. Use it to make the screen brighter or dimmer for the focused window.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowColorSpace: Sets the color space used by the window. Use it to control how colors are shown in a window.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowContainerColor: Sets the background color of the whole window, separately for when it is focused and when it is not. Use it to give a window a different look when active versus inactive.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowContainerModalColo: Sets the background color of the window container for when it is focused and when it is not. Use it to give a window a different background color when active versus inactive.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowCornerRadius: Sets how round the corners of a child or floating window are. Use it to round off a floating window's corners, or set 0 for square corners.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowDecorHeight: Sets the height of the window's title bar. Use it to make the title bar taller or shorter on a window that has one.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowDecorVisible: Shows or hides the window's title bar. Use it to hide the title bar for a cleaner, more immersive window.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowDelayRaiseOnDrag: Sets whether a window waits to come to the front until the mouse button is released during drag-and-drop. Use it to keep a dragged window from jumping in front too early.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowFocusable: Sets whether a window can receive focus. Use it to make a window clickable and typeable, or to stop it taking focus.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowGrayScale: Sets a grayscale effect on the window. Use it to make a window appear in shades of gray.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowKeepScreenOn: Keeps the screen always on while true, and lets it turn off again when false. Use it during navigation, video playback, drawing, or gaming so the screen does not sleep.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowLayoutFullScreen: Makes the window layout immersive so components can overlap the status bar and navigation bar, or non-immersive so they avoid them. Use it to draw edge-to-edge behind the system bars.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowLimits: Sets the minimum and maximum size limits for a window. Use it to control how small or large a window can be resized.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowMask: Sets a pixel mask that gives a window an irregular shape, where 0 pixels are transparent and 1 pixels are opaque. Use it to make a child or floating window with a custom outline.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowMaskWithAlpha: Sets a window's shape using per-pixel alpha values from fully transparent to fully opaque. Use it to give a window smooth, partially transparent edges.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowMode: Sets the display mode of the main window. Use it to switch a window between modes such as full screen or floating.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowPrivacyMode: Turns privacy mode on or off so the window cannot be captured or recorded, and shows a mask in the multitasking view. Use it to hide sensitive content from screenshots and screen recording.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowShadowEnabled: Turns the shadow around the main window on or off. Use it to remove or restore the window's drop shadow.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowShadowRadius: Sets how soft or blurry the shadow around a child or floating window looks. Use it to make a floating window's shadow softer or sharper, or set it to zero to remove the shadow.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowSystemBarEnable: Shows or hides the status bar and the three-button navigation bar in the main window. Use it to hide the status bar and navigation buttons for a full-screen view.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowSystemBarPropertie: Changes the look of the status bar and navigation bar of the main window. Use it to restyle the status bar and navigation bar colors.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTitle: Sets the title shown on a window. Use it to give a window a name in its title bar.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTitleButtonVisible: Shows or hides the maximize, minimize, and close buttons on the main window's title bar. Use it to remove or restore the window's title bar buttons.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTitleMoveEnabled: Turns on or off the ability to move a window by dragging its title bar and to maximize it with a double-click. Use it to control whether users can drag the title bar to move or double-click to maximize a window.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTopmost: Pins the main window above all other windows of the app, or unpins it. Use it with a custom shortcut key to keep the main window always on top.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTouchable: Sets whether a window responds to touch. Use it to make a window touchable or to block touches on it.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowTransitionAnimatio: Adds a transition animation for a window in a specific scene, currently only when the window is destroyed. Use it to animate a window as it closes.
ArkUI.Window.setWindowType: Sets the type of a window. Use it to change what kind of window this is.
ArkUI.Window.show: Shows the window. Use it to make a hidden window visible.
ArkUI.Window.showWindow: Shows a window, or brings an already visible main window to the top of the stack. Use it to display a window or bring the app's main window to the front.
ArkUI.Window.showWithAnimation: Shows a window and plays an animation while it appears. Use it to make a window appear with a smooth animation.
ArkUI.Window.snapshot: Takes a picture of the window's current contents. Use it to capture what is on screen, such as for a screenshot; if privacy mode is on, the picture comes out blank.
ArkUI.Window.snapshotIgnorePrivacy: Takes a picture of the window's current contents even when privacy mode is on. Use it to capture a screenshot that would otherwise be blank.
ArkUI.Window.snapshotSync: Takes a picture of the window's current contents and gives it back right away. Use it to grab a screenshot of the window on the spot.
ArkUI.Window.startMoving: Moves a window by dragging it, setting where the cursor sits inside the window first. Use it to drag a window around the screen.
ArkUI.Window.startMovingWithOptions: Starts moving a window so it follows the cursor, when called on a touch-down event. Use it to let someone drag a window around the screen.
ArkUI.Window.stopMoving: Stops a window that is being dragged. Use it to end dragging a window around the screen.
ArkUI.Window.translate: Sets the translation parameters for a window, in pixels. Use it to move a window as part of a custom animation when a system window is shown or hidden.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onAppTra: Called when the device switches from one application to another. Use it to play a custom animation during the app switch.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onCloseW: Called when a window is closing. Use it to play a custom animation as a window closes.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onMinimi: Called when a window is being minimized. Use it to play a custom animation as a window shrinks down.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onScreen: Called when the screen is unlocked. Use it to play a custom animation when the user unlocks the screen.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onStartA: Called when an application is started from the launcher. Use it to play a custom animation when an app opens from the home screen.
Runs the window animation shown when an app is launched from somewhere other than the recent apps list. Use it to animate the opening of an app started from outside the recent tasks view.
Runs the window animation shown when an app is launched from the recent apps list. Use it to animate the opening of an app started from the recent tasks view.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationController.onWindow: Updates the window animation targets, giving the fullscreen window target and all floating window targets. Use it to keep track of which windows should be animated.
ArkUI.WindowAnimationFinishedCallback.on: Signals that a window animation has finished. Use it to run follow-up work once the window animation is done.
ArkUI.WindowExtensionAbility.onConnect: Called when a window extension is first connected to an ability, providing the connection information. Use it to set up a window extension when something connects to it.
ArkUI.WindowExtensionAbility.onDisconnec: Called when all abilities connected to a window extension have disconnected, providing the disconnection information. Use it to clean up a window extension once nothing is connected to it.
ArkUI.WindowExtensionAbility.onWindowRea: Tells the extension when its window has been created, handing over the window instance. Use it to start setting up the window as soon as it exists.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.createSubWindowWithOpt: Creates a smaller window inside this one, with options for its name and behaviour. Use it to open an extra window, such as a floating panel, on top of the current one.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.getWindowAvoidArea: Finds the parts of the screen where a window cannot be shown, such as the status bar, notch, gesture area, or keyboard. Use it to keep content clear of those blocked areas.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.hideNonSecureWindows: Turns hiding of non-secure windows on or off. Use it to keep sensitive content from showing in unsafe windows.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.occupyEvents: Makes a component take over certain events so the surrounding host app does not react to them inside that component's area. Use it to stop the host from handling touches or keys within an embedded component.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.off: Stops listening for changes to an embedded component's position and size. Use it when you no longer need updates about the component moving or resizing.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.offAvoidAreaChange: Stops listening for changes to the area where a window cannot be displayed. Use it when you no longer need updates about blocked screen areas like the status bar or keyboard.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.offRectChange: Stops listening for changes to an embedded component's position and size. Use it when you no longer need updates about the component's rectangle changing.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.offWindowSizeChange: Stops listening for size changes of an embedded component. Use it when you no longer need updates about the component getting bigger or smaller.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.on: Subscribes to position and size change events of an embedded component or extension window. Use it to react when that window moves or resizes.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.onAvoidAreaChange: Subscribes to changes in the area where a window cannot be displayed. Use it to adjust layout when part of the window becomes covered or blocked.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.onRectChange: Listens for changes in the position and size of an embedded component. Use it to react when an embedded window moves or resizes.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.onWindowSizeChange: Subscribes to size change events of an embedded component or extension window. Use it to react when that window's size changes.
ArkUI.WindowProxy.setWaterMarkFlag: Adds or removes a watermark on the window. Use it to mark window content with a watermark, or to clear that mark.
ArkUI.WindowStage.createSubWindow: Creates a subwindow of the stage by name. Use it to open an additional window alongside the main one.
ArkUI.WindowStage.createSubWindowWithOpt: Creates a subwindow of the stage with specified options. Use it to open an additional window with custom settings.
ArkUI.WindowStage.disableWindowDecor: Turns off the window's title bar and border decorations, so the main window can go full screen. Use it for a clean, full-screen look without window decor.
ArkUI.WindowStage.getMainWindow: Gets the main window of the stage. Use it to access and manage the app's primary window.
ArkUI.WindowStage.getMainWindowSync: Gets the main window of the stage. Use it to access the main window for showing your app's content.
ArkUI.WindowStage.getSubWindow: Gets the sub windows of the stage. Use it to find and manage extra windows your app has opened.
ArkUI.WindowStage.isWindowRectAutoSave: Tells whether the window supports automatically saving its rectangle. Use it to check if window position and size are remembered automatically.
ArkUI.WindowStage.loadContent: Loads a page into the main window of the stage. Use it at app startup to show your first screen.
ArkUI.WindowStage.loadContentByName: Loads a named route page into this window. Use it at app startup to show a specific named page.
ArkUI.WindowStage.off: Stops listening for window stage lifecycle or close events. Use it to stop reacting when the window stage changes or closes.
ArkUI.WindowStage.offWindowStageClose: Stops listening for the main window's close button being clicked. Use it to stop reacting when someone closes the app's main window.
ArkUI.WindowStage.offWindowStageEvent: Stops listening for window stage lifecycle changes. Use it to stop reacting when a window is shown, hidden, or resized.
ArkUI.WindowStage.offWindowStageLifecycl: Stops listening for changes in the window stage's lifecycle. Use it to stop reacting when the window stage is shown, hidden, or otherwise changes state.
ArkUI.WindowStage.on: Starts listening for window stage lifecycle changes, including when the window stage is closed. Use it to react when the app's window stage opens, closes, or changes state.
ArkUI.WindowStage.onWindowStageClose: Listens for the close button in the main window's three-button navigation bar being clicked. Use it to react when someone taps the close button to shut the main window.
ArkUI.WindowStage.onWindowStageEvent: Starts listening for changes in the window stage's lifecycle. Use it to react when the window stage is shown, hidden, or otherwise changes state.
ArkUI.WindowStage.onWindowStageLifecycle: Starts listening for changes in the window stage's lifecycle. Use it to react when the window stage is shown, hidden, or otherwise changes state.
ArkUI.WindowStage.releaseUIContent: Releases the content shown in this window. Use it to clear the window's displayed content when closing or resetting a screen.
ArkUI.WindowStage.removeImageForRecent: Removes the image shown for the app in the multitasking view and on dock hover. Use it to clear a custom recent-app picture.
ArkUI.WindowStage.removeStartingWindow: Removes the starting window that appears while an app is launching. Use it to dismiss the launch splash screen once the app is ready.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setCustomDensity: Sets a custom display size scale factor for the app's main window. Use it to make the app's interface appear larger or smaller.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setDefaultDensityEnabl: Chooses whether the main window uses the system's default display density. Use it to keep the app's sizing consistent with the system or follow system size changes.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setImageForRecent: Sets the image shown for the app in the multitasking view and on dock hover. Use it to show a chosen picture when switching apps.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setShowOnLockScreen: Sets whether the app's window is shown on the lock screen. Use it to keep an app visible on the lock screen, such as a music player or navigation.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setSupportedWindowMode: Sets which window modes the main window supports, such as full screen or split screen. Use it to control how the app's window can be displayed.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setWindowModal: Turns the window stage's application modality on or off. Use it to make the window block interaction with other windows while it is open.
ArkUI.WindowStage.setWindowRectAutoSave: Turns on automatic saving of a window's size and position, and can mark the window so its rectangle is saved. Use it to keep a window opening in the same place and size next time.

ArkUI.componentSnapshot.getSync: Gets a snapshot image of an already loaded component by its ID, waiting until it is ready. Use it to capture a picture of a component on screen.
ArkUI.componentUtils.getItemsInShapePath: Gets the image objects located within a selected area. Use it to find which images fall inside a drawn shape or region.
ArkUI.componentUtils.getRectangleById: Gets the size, position, rotation, and scaling of a component by its ID. Use it to find where a component is and how big it is on screen.
ArkUI.curves.cubicBezier: Creates a cubic Bezier curve for smooth animation timing. Use it to make movement or fades ease in and out instead of starting and stopping abruptly.
ArkUI.curves.cubicBezierCurve: Creates a cubic Bezier curve with x-coordinates automatically kept between 0 and 1. Use it to shape smooth, natural-feeling animation motion.
ArkUI.curves.customCurve: Creates a custom curve from your own interpolation rule. Use it to give an animation a motion pattern you define yourself.
ArkUI.curves.init: Creates an interpolation curve from a chosen curve type. Use it to set how an animation speeds up or slows down.
ArkUI.curves.initCurve: Creates an interpolation curve from a chosen curve type. Use it to set how an animation speeds up or slows down.
ArkUI.curves.interpolatingSpring: Creates a spring curve that animates from 0 to 1 with bouncing motion. Use it to make elements spring, bounce, or settle naturally.
ArkUI.curves.responsiveSpringMotion: Creates a responsive spring animation curve for smooth, natural motion. Use it to make an element spring back or follow a drag with a lively feel.
ArkUI.curves.spring: Builds a spring curve object from velocity, mass, stiffness, and damping. Use it to give an animation a bouncy, elastic feel.
ArkUI.curves.springCurve: Creates a spring curve whose shape follows the spring settings while the animation duration is set separately. Use it to make motion bounce or settle like a spring.
ArkUI.curves.springMotion: Creates a spring animation curve that replaces earlier spring animations on the same property and inherits their velocity. Use it to make an element spring smoothly to a new position.
ArkUI.curves.steps: Creates a step curve that jumps in a set number of steps. Use it to make an animation move in discrete jumps instead of smoothly.
ArkUI.curves.stepsCurve: Creates a step curve that changes in a set number of steps. Use it to make an animation advance in distinct jumps.
ArkUI.curves.trailOptimizedInterpolating: Creates a spring animation curve that runs from 0 to 1, with duration set by the curve itself. Use it for smooth springy motion in animations.
ArkUI.curves.trailOptimizedResponsiveSpr: Creates a responsive spring animation curve, a special case of spring motion with default settings. Use it for smooth springy motion in animations.
ArkUI.curves.trailOptimizedSpringMotion: Creates a spring animation curve where each new animation replaces the previous one and inherits its velocity. Use it for smooth springy motion in animations.

ArkUI.display.destroyVirtualScreen: Removes a virtual screen that was created earlier. Use it to clean up an extra display surface when it is no longer needed.
ArkUI.display.getAllDisplay: Gets a list of all connected displays. Use it to find out how many screens are available and their details.
ArkUI.display.getAllDisplayPhysicalResol: Gets every display mode the device supports together with the physical resolution of each mode. Use it to pick the best resolution for a screen.
ArkUI.display.getAllDisplays: Gets every connected display screen. Use it to find all screens, for example to place a window on a second monitor.
ArkUI.display.getBrightnessInfo: Gets the screen brightness information of a display, including HDR headroom values. Use it to check how bright a screen is or to read brightness details for a display.
ArkUI.display.getCurrentFoldCreaseRegion: Gets the crease region of a foldable device in its current display mode. Use it to find where the fold line sits on a folding phone screen.
ArkUI.display.getDefaultDisplay: Gets the default display object for the device. Use it to find out about the main screen your app is shown on.
ArkUI.display.getDefaultDisplaySync: Gets the display object of the screen where the application is running, returning the main screen if abilities are on different screens. Use it to find out about the screen your app is on.
ArkUI.display.getDisplayByIdSync: Gets a display object for a given display ID. Use it to look up details about a specific screen by its ID.
ArkUI.display.getFoldDisplayMode: Gets the display mode of a foldable device. Use it to tell whether a folding phone is open, closed, or half-folded.
ArkUI.display.getFoldStatus: Tells you whether a foldable device is folded, unfolded, or half-open. Use it to adjust the layout when someone folds or unfolds their phone.
ArkUI.display.getPrimaryDisplaySync: Gives you the main screen of the device, such as the built-in screen or the primary external monitor. Use it to place content on the screen the person is looking at.
ArkUI.display.hasPrivateWindow: Checks whether a display currently shows a visible privacy window whose content cannot be captured or recorded. Use it to know if screen capture or recording would expose private content.
ArkUI.display.isCaptured: Checks whether the screen is being captured, cast, or recorded by any of the listed apps. Use it to warn someone that their screen is being shared or recorded.
ArkUI.display.isFoldable: Checks whether the device can fold. Use it to decide whether to show fold-aware layouts.
ArkUI.display.makeUnique: Puts a screen into independent display mode. Use it to show separate content on a second screen.
ArkUI.display.off: Stops listening for privacy mode changes on a display, which happens when a private window is in front and cannot be captured or recorded. Use it to stop reacting when private content appears or disappears.
ArkUI.display.offAdd: Stops listening for new displays being added. Use it to stop being notified when a display is connected.
ArkUI.display.offBrightnessInfoChange: Stops listening for screen brightness changes. Use it to stop being notified when the display brightness changes.
ArkUI.display.offCaptureStatusChange: Stops listening for screen capture, casting, or recording status changes. Use it to stop being notified when the screen is being captured, cast, or recorded.
ArkUI.display.offChange: Stops listening for display changes. Use it to stop being notified when the display changes.
ArkUI.display.offFoldAngleChange: Stops listening for fold angle changes. Use it to stop being notified when a foldable device's hinge angle changes.
ArkUI.display.offFoldDisplayModeChange: Stops listening for fold display mode changes. Use it to stop being notified when a foldable device's display mode changes.
ArkUI.display.offFoldStatusChange: Stops listening for changes in the fold status of a foldable device. Use it to stop being notified when the device is folded or unfolded.
ArkUI.display.offPrivateModeChange: Stops listening for changes to the display's private mode. Use it to stop reacting when privacy mode is turned on or off.
ArkUI.display.offRemove: Stops listening for display removal events. Use it to stop being notified when a display is disconnected.
ArkUI.display.on: Listens for changes to the display's privacy mode. Use it to be notified when the screen's privacy mode is turned on or off.
ArkUI.display.onAdd: Listens for display addition events. Use it to be notified when a new display is connected.
ArkUI.display.onBrightnessInfoChange: Listens for changes in the display's brightness information. Use it to be notified when the screen brightness changes.
ArkUI.display.onCaptureStatusChange: Listens for changes in the device's capture, casting, or recording status. Use it to be notified when screen capture, casting, or recording starts or stops.
ArkUI.display.onChange: Tells you when the display changes, such as when a screen is added or removed. Use it to react when a monitor or screen is plugged in or unplugged.
ArkUI.display.onChangeWithAttribute: Watches for changes to specific display attributes you choose. Use it to be notified when a screen property you care about changes.
ArkUI.display.onFoldAngleChange: Tells you when the fold angle of a foldable device changes. Use it to react as a foldable phone is opened or closed.
ArkUI.display.onFoldDisplayModeChange: Tells you when the display mode of a foldable device changes. Use it to adjust your app when a foldable switches between folded and unfolded modes.
ArkUI.display.onFoldStatusChange: Tells you when the fold status of a foldable device changes. Use it to react when a foldable phone is folded, unfolded, or half-opened.
ArkUI.display.onPrivateModeChange: Starts listening for changes to the display's private mode. Use it to react when privacy mode is turned on or off, for example to update screen capture behavior.
ArkUI.display.onRemove: Tells you when a display is removed. Use it to react when a screen or monitor is disconnected.
ArkUI.display.removeVirtualScreenBlockli: Removes windows from the list of windows that are hidden during casting. Use it to make an app's main window visible again when casting or screen sharing.

ArkUI.display.setFoldDisplayMode: Changes the display mode of a foldable device, such as switching between folded and unfolded screens. Use it to control how a foldable phone shows content when its shape changes.
ArkUI.display.setFoldStatusLocked: Locks or unlocks the current fold status of a foldable device. Use it to keep a foldable phone from switching screens when it is folded or unfolded.
ArkUI.display.setVirtualScreenSurface: Binds a surface to a virtual screen so its content can be shown there. Use it to display output on a virtual screen you created.

ArkUI.dragInteraction.offDragStateChange: Stops listening for changes in dragging state. Use it to stop reacting when a drag begins or finishes.

ArkUI.dragInteraction.onDragStateChange: Listens for changes in dragging state. Use it to react while an item is being dragged.

ArkUI.floatingBall.isFloatingBallEnabled: Checks whether the device supports floating balls. Use it to decide whether to offer a floating ball feature.
ArkUI.font.getFontByName: Gets information about a system font from its name. Use it to look up details of an installed font.

ArkUI.mediaquery.matchMediaSync: Sets a media query condition and returns a listener for it. Use it to apply different styles for different screen types or sizes.

ArkUI.prompt.showToast: Shows a short notification text on the screen. Use it to briefly tell the user something, like a quick status message.

ArkUI.promptAction.closeToast: Closes a toast notification that is currently showing. Use it to hide a brief message before it disappears on its own.

ArkUI.promptAction.openToast: Shows a toast notification and returns an ID for it. Use it to briefly display a message to the user, such as a quick confirmation.
ArkUI.promptAction.showActionMenu: Shows a menu of actions for the user to choose from. Use it when you want to offer choices like save, share, or delete.
ArkUI.promptAction.showDialog: Shows a dialog box with the settings you give. Use it to ask the user to confirm something or enter information.
ArkUI.promptAction.showToast: Shows a short toast message on the screen. Use it to briefly tell the user something, like that a save finished.

ArkUI.router.getStateByUrl: Gets state information about a page by its URL. Use it to look up details of a page from its address.
ArkUI.router.hideAlertBeforeBackPage: Turns off the confirm dialog that appears before going back to the previous page. Use it when you no longer want a pop-up asking to confirm leaving the page.
ArkUI.router.push: Opens a specified page inside the app. Use it to move the user to another screen, such as tapping a button to go to a details page.
ArkUI.router.pushNamedRoute: Opens a page by its named route. Use it to move the user to another screen when pages are identified by name.
ArkUI.router.pushUrl: Opens a specified page inside the app. Use it to move the user to another screen, such as tapping a button to go to a details page.

ArkUI.router.showAlertBeforeBackPage: Shows a confirm dialog before going back to the previous page. Use it to ask the user to confirm leaving a page.

ArkUI.screen.isScreenRotationLocked: Checks whether automatic screen rotation is locked. Use it to find out if the screen will stay upright or follow the device's orientation.
ArkUI.screen.makeExpand: Sets screens into extended mode. Use it to join displays so content can span across them.
ArkUI.screen.makeMirror: Puts a screen into mirror mode so secondary screens copy the main screen. Use it to show the same picture on several displays at once.

ArkUI.screen.makeUnique: Sets screens to independent display mode so each shows its own content. Use it to stop screens from mirroring and give each its own picture.

ArkUI.screen.onChange: Listens for changes to the screen state. Use it to react when a display's state changes.

ArkUI.screen.setVirtualScreenSurface: Sets a surface for a virtual screen. Use it to attach a drawing surface to a virtual display.

ArkUI.screen.stopMirror: Stops mirror mode for secondary screens. Use it to end screen mirroring so a secondary display no longer copies the main screen.
ArkUI.screenshot.capture: Takes a full-screen screenshot and returns it as an image. Use it to capture what is on the screen, such as for saving or sharing.
ArkUI.screenshot.pick: Obtains a screenshot of the main display. Use it to grab the current screen image for saving or sharing.
ArkUI.screenshot.save: Takes a screenshot of the screen and returns it as a picture. Use it to capture what is currently shown on the screen.

ArkUI.uiAppearance.getFontWeightScale: Gets the current font weight scale factor of the system. Use it to adjust text thickness to match the user's font weight setting.
ArkUI.uiAppearance.setDarkMode: Sets the system color mode to dark or light. Use it to switch the whole device between dark and light appearance.
ArkUI.uiAppearance.setFontScale: Sets the system font size scale factor. Use it to make text across the system larger or smaller.
ArkUI.uiAppearance.setFontWeightScale: Sets the system font weight scale factor. Use it to make text across the system thicker or thinner.
