ArkUI.window.getSnapshot: Takes a picture of a chosen window, the same size as that window. Use it to capture what a window currently shows on screen.
ArkUI.window.getTopNavDestinationName: Gets the name of the page currently on top inside a window's navigation. Use it to find out which screen or page the user is looking at.
ArkUI.window.getTopWindow: Gets the top window of the current app. Use it to work with the window currently on top.

ArkUI.window.moveMainWindowToTargetDispl: Moves a main window onto a different display. Use it to send an app's window to another screen.
ArkUI.window.notifyScreenshotEvent: Tells the system that a screenshot was taken. Use it to react when someone captures the screen.

CameraKit.VideoSession.on: Listens for errors that happen while setting up or running a camera session. Use it to be told when something goes wrong during video recording.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onApertureInfoCha: Starts listening for changes in the camera aperture setting while recording video. Use it to keep the aperture value up to date on screen.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onAutoDeviceSwitc: Listens for changes in the automatic camera switching status. Use it to be told when the camera automatically switches between lenses while recording.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onControlCenterEf: Listens for changes to the control center effect status. Use it to be told when an effect applied from the control center changes while recording.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onEffectSuggestio: Starts listening for suggestions about which camera effect to use while recording video. Use it to show or apply a suggested effect.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onError: Watches for errors while recording video. Use it to notice and handle problems during a video recording.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onExposureInfoCha: Reports updated exposure information after exposure settings change. Use it to keep track of brightness while recording video.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onFocusStateChang: Reports when the focus state changes. Use it to know when the camera has focused while recording video.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onFocusTrackingIn: Starts listening for focus tracking information while recording video. Use it to follow a moving subject and keep it in focus.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onIsoInfoChange: Reports the latest sensitivity (ISO) value when it changes. Use it to track how light-sensitive the camera is while recording video.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onLcdFlashStatus: Starts listening for updates about the screen flash used as a light while recording video. Use it to know when the screen flash is on or off.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onLightStatusChan: Watches the camera light status and reports changes. Use it to react when the camera light turns on or off.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onMacroStatusChan: Reports when the camera macro status changes. Use it to know when close-up macro mode turns on or off while recording video.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onSmoothZoomInfoA: Reports zoom information during smooth zooming. Use it to follow the zoom level while recording video.
CameraKit.VideoSession.onSystemPressureL: Watches for changes in the device's system pressure level during a video session. Use it to react when the phone gets too hot or busy while recording.
CameraKit.VideoSession.preconfig: Sets up the video session ahead of time with a chosen resolution type and aspect ratio. Use it to prepare the camera for recording before you start.
CameraKit.VideoSession.setQualityPriorit: Chooses whether video recording favors higher quality or other priorities. Use it to decide how good your recorded video should look.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.getColorTint: Reads the current color tint setting for white balance. Use it to check how warm or cool the colors look before adjusting them.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.getWhiteBalance: Reads the current white balance value in kelvin. Use it to check how warm or cool the camera's colour setting is.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.getWhiteBalanceGa: Reads the current red, green and blue white balance gain values. Use it to check the colour balance the camera is applying.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.getWhiteBalanceMo: Tells you which white balance mode the camera is using. Use it to check whether white balance is automatic or set manually.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.setColorTint: Changes the color tint for white balance. Use it to make the picture look warmer or cooler.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.setWhiteBalance: Sets the white balance value in kelvin. Use it to make photos or video look warmer or cooler under different lighting.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.setWhiteBalanceGa: Sets the red, green and blue white balance gain values. Use it to fine-tune the colour balance of the camera image.
CameraKit.WhiteBalance.setWhiteBalanceMo: Sets the camera's white balance mode so colours look right under different lighting. Check first whether the device supports that mode.
CameraKit.WhiteBalanceQuery.getColorTint: Tells you the range of color tint values you can set for white balance. Use it to find the limits before adjusting the tint.
CameraKit.WhiteBalanceQuery.getWhiteBala: Gives the range of white balance values available in manual white balance mode, in Kelvin. Use it to see how warm or cool you can make the picture.
CameraKit.WhiteBalanceQuery.isWhiteBalan: Checks whether the camera supports RGB gain for white balance. Use it to find out if you can fine-tune colour balance with gains.
Checks whether the camera supports a given white balance mode. Use it before choosing a white balance setting for your shot.
CameraKit.Zoom.getZoomCenterPoint: Gets the point the camera zooms in on. Use it to find where the zoom is centred in the picture.
CameraKit.Zoom.getZoomRatio: Tells you the zoom ratio the camera is currently using. Use it to show how far in or out the camera is zoomed.
CameraKit.Zoom.prepareZoom: Tells the camera to get ready for zooming, such as powering on the sensor. Use it before zooming in or out.
CameraKit.Zoom.setSmoothZoom: Zooms the camera in or out smoothly to a chosen ratio. Use it to zoom in on a subject without a sudden jump.
CameraKit.Zoom.setZoomCenterPoint: Sets the point that the camera zooms in on. Use it to zoom toward a chosen spot in the picture, such as a face or object.
CameraKit.Zoom.setZoomRatio: Sets the camera zoom to a chosen ratio. Use it to zoom in or out for a photo or video.
CameraKit.Zoom.unprepareZoom: Tells the camera to stop being ready for zooming. Use it to release zoom preparation when zooming is no longer needed.
CameraKit.ZoomQuery.getRAWCaptureZoomRat: Tells you the zoom ratios the camera supports when shooting in RAW format. Use it to know how far you can zoom for RAW photos.
CameraKit.ZoomQuery.getZoomPointInfos: Gets the list of equivalent focal length information for the current camera mode. Use it to see the zoom levels available for taking a photo or video.
CameraKit.ZoomQuery.getZoomRatioRange: Tells you the smallest and largest zoom ratios the camera supports. Use it to know how far you can zoom in or out.
CameraKit.ZoomQuery.isZoomCenterPointSup: Checks whether the camera supports choosing a zoom center point. Use it to find out if you can zoom toward a chosen spot in the picture.
CameraKit.camera.getCameraManager: Gives you the camera manager for the app. Use it to start working with the camera, such as opening it or taking photos.
CameraKit.cameraPicker.pick: Opens the system camera in photo or video mode so the user can capture media. Use it to take a photo or record a video from your app.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.connec: Connects a Bluetooth audio device for A2DP streaming. Use it to start playing sound through wireless headphones or speakers.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.disabl: Turns off the absolute volume switch for a connected device. Use it to stop a Bluetooth audio device's volume from being controlled together with the phone.
Restricts a device from playing music for a set time after it connects. Use it to stop a Bluetooth audio device from automatically playing a song right after connecting.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.discon: Disconnects a Bluetooth audio device from A2DP streaming. Use it to stop playing sound through wireless headphones or speakers.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.enable: Turns on the absolute volume switch for a connected audio device. Use it to let the phone's volume control directly change the volume of Bluetooth headphones or speakers.
Allows a connected device to automatically start playing music. Use it so a paired speaker or car stereo begins playing a song as soon as it connects.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.getAut: Gets how long automatic playback stays disabled for a connected device, in milliseconds. Use it to check how long a speaker or car stereo will wait before auto-playing music again.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.getCur: Gets the audio codec information currently used with a connected device. Use it to see which audio format is being used when playing a song on Bluetooth headphones or speakers.
Gets the full set of audio codec capabilities agreed between the connected device and this device. Use it to check all audio formats available for playing music on Bluetooth headphones or speakers.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.getPla: Checks whether a Bluetooth audio device is currently playing. Use it to see if music is playing on connected wireless headphones or speakers.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.isAbso: Checks whether the absolute volume switch is on for a connected device. Use it to see if the phone's volume control directly changes the volume of Bluetooth headphones or speakers.
Checks whether a connected Bluetooth audio device supports absolute volume. Use it to find out if you can control the volume of a paired speaker or headphones directly.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.off: Stops listening for changes in the Bluetooth audio connection state. Use it to stop being notified when wireless headphones or speakers connect or disconnect.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.on: Listens for changes in the Bluetooth audio connection state. Use it to know when wireless headphones or speakers connect or disconnect.
ConnectivityKit.A2dpSourceProfile.setCur: Sets the audio codec information for a connected Bluetooth device. Use it to choose how audio is encoded when playing a song to a paired speaker or headphones.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.createGattClientDevi: Creates a Bluetooth Gatt client instance for a remote device address. Use it to connect to and talk to a nearby Bluetooth device such as a fitness tracker or smart sensor.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.createGattServer: Creates a Bluetooth Gatt server instance. Use it to offer Bluetooth services so other devices can connect and exchange data with your device.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.getConnectedBLEDevic: Gets the addresses of Bluetooth devices that are currently connected. Use it to see which Bluetooth devices are linked right now.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.off: Stops listening for Bluetooth scan results. Use it to stop receiving nearby Bluetooth device findings after a scan.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.on: Starts listening for Bluetooth scan results. Use it to receive nearby Bluetooth devices found while scanning.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.startBLEScan: Starts scanning for Bluetooth devices, optionally filtered. Use it to find nearby Bluetooth devices such as headphones or beacons.
ConnectivityKit.BLE.stopBLEScan: Stops scanning for nearby Bluetooth Low Energy devices. Use it to end a search for BLE devices such as fitness trackers or beacons.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.getConnected: Gets the addresses of devices currently connected through a Bluetooth profile. Use it to list which paired devices are connected right now.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.getConnectio: Gets the addresses of devices currently connected through a Bluetooth profile. Use it to list which paired devices are connected right now.
Tells you the connection state of a Bluetooth profile for a given device. Use it to check whether a device is connected, connecting, or disconnected.
Gets the connection strategy for a Bluetooth profile with a device. Use it to check how a device is set to connect, such as automatically or manually.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.getDeviceSta: Tells you the Bluetooth profile state of a given device. Use it to check whether a device is connected, connecting, or disconnected.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.off: Stops listening for changes in a Bluetooth profile's connection state. Use it to stop being notified when a device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.offConnectio: Stops listening for changes in a profile's connection state. Use it to stop being notified when a paired device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.on: Listens for changes in a profile's connection state. Use it to be notified when a paired device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.onConnection: Listens for changes in a profile's connection state. Use it to be notified when a paired device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.BaseProfile.setConnectio: Sets the connection strategy for a Bluetooth profile with a device. Use it to control whether a device connects automatically or manually.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.off: Stops listening for Bluetooth Low Energy scan results. Use it to stop being notified about nearby Bluetooth devices found while scanning.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.offBLEDeviceF: Stops listening for Bluetooth Low Energy scan results. Use it to stop being notified about nearby Bluetooth devices found while scanning.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.on: Listens for Bluetooth Low Energy scan results. Use it to be notified about nearby Bluetooth devices found while scanning.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.onBLEDeviceFi: Listens for nearby Bluetooth low-energy devices found during a scan and reports each result. Use it to detect nearby Bluetooth gadgets like trackers, sensors, or headphones.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.startScan: Begins scanning for nearby Bluetooth low-energy devices, optionally filtered to only the ones you want. Use it to search for nearby Bluetooth devices such as trackers, sensors, or headphones.
ConnectivityKit.BleScanner.stopScan: Stops scanning for nearby Bluetooth Low Energy devices. Use it to end a search for BLE devices such as fitness trackers or beacons.
ConnectivityKit.Bluetooth.startBLEScan: Starts a scan for nearby Bluetooth low-energy devices. Use it to look for nearby Bluetooth gadgets like trackers, sensors, or headphones.
ConnectivityKit.Bluetooth.stopBLEScan: Stops an ongoing scan for nearby Bluetooth low-energy devices. Use it to end the search for nearby Bluetooth gadgets once you have found what you need.
ConnectivityKit.Bluetooth.subscribeBLEFo: Subscribes to be notified when a nearby Bluetooth low-energy device is found. Use it to keep getting alerts about nearby Bluetooth gadgets as they appear.
ConnectivityKit.Bluetooth.unsubscribeBLE: Stops the subscription that reports nearby Bluetooth low-energy devices. Use it to stop being alerted about nearby Bluetooth gadgets.
ConnectivityKit.CdsmClient.getCdsmInfo: Gets information about the set of coordinated devices. Use it to see which devices are working together.
ConnectivityKit.CdsmClient.offCdsmInfoCh: Stops listening for changes to the coordinated devices set information. Use it when you no longer need updates about which devices are coordinated.
ConnectivityKit.CdsmClient.onCdsmInfoCha: Starts listening for changes to the coordinated devices set information. Use it to keep track of which devices are working together.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.close: Closes a channel to the secure element. Use it to end a secure card session when you are done.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.getSelectRespons: Returns the data from the application select command, including the status word. Use it to check the result of selecting an applet on a secure element.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.getSession: Gets the session that opened this channel. Use it to find which session a secure element channel belongs to.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.isBasicChannel: Checks whether a channel to a secure element is the basic channel. Use it to tell the basic channel apart from a logical channel before sending commands.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.isClosed: Checks whether a channel to a secure element has been closed. Use it to confirm a channel is no longer open before reusing or reopening it.
ConnectivityKit.Channel.transmit: Sends an APDU command to a secure element and returns the response bytes. Use it to talk to a smart card or secure element, such as reading card data.
ConnectivityKit.Client.callMethod: Calls a method on a connected server. Use it to send a request to a nearby device and get its response.
ConnectivityKit.Client.close: Closes the client connection. Use it to end a session with a server when you are done.
ConnectivityKit.Client.connect: Connects to the server. Use it to start a session with a server before exchanging data.
ConnectivityKit.Client.disconnect: Disconnects from the server or stops an ongoing connection. Use it to end a session with a server.
ConnectivityKit.Client.getServices: Finds all services offered by a connected server. Use it to see what a nearby device can do before using those services.
ConnectivityKit.Client.offConnectionStat: Stops listening for changes in the connection state of a client. Use it to stop being told when a device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.Client.offEventNotify: Unsubscribes from event notifications. Use it to stop receiving updates about events from a connected device.
ConnectivityKit.Client.offMtuChange: Stops listening for changes to the maximum data packet size. Use it to stop being told when the transfer size changes.
ConnectivityKit.Client.offPropertyChange: Stops listening for changes to a property value. Use it to stop being told when a device's property value changes.
ConnectivityKit.Client.onConnectionState: Listens for changes in the connection state of a client. Use it to know when a nearby device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.Client.onEventNotify: Subscribes to event notifications from a connected device. Use it to receive updates when something happens on the other device.
ConnectivityKit.Client.onMtuChange: Listens for changes to the maximum data packet size. Use it to know when the transfer size for a connection changes.
ConnectivityKit.Client.onPropertyChange: Listens for changes to a property value on a connected device. Use it to react when a device's data changes, such as a sensor reading updating.
ConnectivityKit.Client.readDescriptor: Reads a descriptor value from a server. Use it to fetch stored details about a connected device's data.
ConnectivityKit.Client.readProperty: Reads a property value from a server device. Use it to fetch data from a connected device, such as a sensor reading or device status.
ConnectivityKit.Client.requestMtuSize: Negotiates the maximum transmission unit size with a server device. Use it to set how much data can be sent at once when transferring data to a device.
ConnectivityKit.Client.setPropertyIndica: Turns indication on or off for a property so you are alerted when its value changes. Use it to get notified about changes to a device's data.
ConnectivityKit.Client.setPropertyNotifi: Turns notifications on or off for a property when its value changes. Use it to start or stop receiving updates when a device's data changes.
ConnectivityKit.Client.writeDescriptor: Writes a descriptor value to a server. Use it to store configuration details on a connected device.
ConnectivityKit.Client.writeProperty: Writes a property value to a server device. Use it to send data or settings to a connected device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.close: Disables a BLE peripheral device and clears its registered callbacks and handles. Use it to disconnect and release a Bluetooth device when you are done with it.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.connect: Connects to a nearby Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to start talking to a smart watch, fitness band, or other wireless gadget.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.disconn: Ends the connection to a Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to stop talking to a smart watch, fitness band, or other wireless gadget.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.getConn: Tells you whether a Bluetooth Low Energy device is currently connected. Use it to check if your smart watch or fitness band is still linked.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.getDevi: Gets the name of a Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to show which nearby gadget, such as a smart watch, you are connected to.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.getRssi: Gets the signal strength of a Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to see how close or far a wireless gadget is.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.getServ: Lists the services offered by a Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to find out what a smart watch or fitness band can do.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.off: Stops listening for a chosen Bluetooth client event, such as a change in connection, MTU, or services. Use it to stop being notified when a paired Bluetooth device changes.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.offBLEC: Stops listening for changes to a Bluetooth characteristic value. Use it to stop being notified when a connected Bluetooth device sends new data.
Stops listening for changes in the Bluetooth connection state. Use it to stop being notified when a Bluetooth device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.offBLEM: Stops listening for changes to the Bluetooth data packet size. Use it to stop being notified when the transfer size for a Bluetooth connection changes.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.offBleP: Stops listening for Bluetooth physical layer updates. Use it to stop being notified when the radio settings of a Bluetooth connection change.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.offServ: Stops listening for changes to the Bluetooth services offered by a device. Use it to stop being notified when a connected Bluetooth device changes its available services.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.on: Subscribes to a Bluetooth GATT service changed event, which means the connected device's data layout was refreshed and its service list must be fetched again. Use it to keep a connected Bluetooth accessory's information up to date.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.onBLECh: Watches for changes to a Bluetooth Low Energy characteristic value. Use it to get updates from a sensor or device, such as a heart rate monitor.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.onBLECo: Watches for changes in the Bluetooth Low Energy connection state. Use it to know when a device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.onBLEMt: Watches for changes in the maximum transmission unit size for Bluetooth Low Energy. Use it to adjust data packet sizes when sending large amounts of data.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.onBlePh: Watches for changes in the Bluetooth Low Energy physical layer settings. Use it to monitor connection speed and reliability.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.onServi: Watches for changes to the Bluetooth Low Energy service list. Use it to refresh the list of services when the device updates them.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.readCha: Reads a value from a Bluetooth Low Energy device's characteristic. Use it to get data like battery level or sensor readings.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.readDes: Reads a descriptor from a connected Bluetooth Low Energy device. Use it to fetch extra details about a Bluetooth device's data, such as a sensor reading's description.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.readPhy: Reads the physical layer setting used for a Bluetooth Low Energy connection. Use it to check the connection speed or radio mode of a paired Bluetooth device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.setBLEM: Sets the maximum data packet size for a Bluetooth Low Energy connection and returns the size that took effect. Use it to send larger chunks of data to a Bluetooth device.
Sets the maximum data packet size for a Bluetooth Low Energy connection. Use it to send larger chunks of data to a Bluetooth device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.setChar: Turns indication on or off for a Bluetooth characteristic so changes are reported back. Use it to get updates from a Bluetooth device, such as a heart-rate reading.
Turns notification on or off for a Bluetooth characteristic so changes are reported back. Use it to get updates from a Bluetooth device, such as a heart-rate reading.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.setNoti: Turns notifications on or off for a Bluetooth characteristic so you are told when its value changes. Use it to get live updates from a device, such as a heart-rate reading or sensor value.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.setPhy: Sets the preferred physical layer used for a Bluetooth connection. Use it to try to tune the connection speed or range with a paired device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.updateC: Updates the connection settings of the current Bluetooth link to save power or send data faster. Use it to balance battery life and speed for a connected device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.writeCh: Writes a value to a characteristic on a Bluetooth device. Use it to send settings or commands to a device, such as changing its name or turning an output on.
Writes a characteristic value to a Bluetooth Low Energy device and returns the result. Use it to send data or commands to a nearby device.
ConnectivityKit.GattClientDevice.writeDe: Writes a value to a descriptor on a Bluetooth device. Use it to change extra configuration details of a connected device.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.addService: Adds a service, with its characteristics, that your own device offers to Bluetooth clients. Use it to make your device act as a Bluetooth accessory others can connect to and read from.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.close: Closes the GATT server and stops its callbacks. Use it to shut down Bluetooth low-energy services your app was offering to nearby devices.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.connect: Connects to a nearby Bluetooth low-energy central device. Use it to link up with a phone or other device that wants to use your app's Bluetooth services.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.disconnect: Disconnects from a Bluetooth low-energy central device or stops an ongoing connection. Use it to end a Bluetooth link with a paired device.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.getConnectedS: Tells you whether a specific device is currently connected. Use it to check if a Bluetooth device is still linked before sending data.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.getService: Gets one of your app's Bluetooth services by its identifier. Use it to look up a specific service you registered so you can work with it.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.getServices: Lists the Bluetooth services your app has registered. Use it to see all the services your app is offering to nearby devices.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.notifyCharact: Sends a notification that a local characteristic has changed to a connected Bluetooth device. Use it to push updated data to a paired device, such as a heart-rate reading or sensor value.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.off: Stops listening for a chosen server event, such as a connection state change or a characteristic being read or written. Use it to stop reacting to Bluetooth device events you no longer need.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.offBLEMtuChan: Stops listening for changes to the maximum data packet size on a Bluetooth connection. Use it to stop reacting when the connection's packet size changes.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.offBlePhyUpda: Stops listening for changes to the Bluetooth connection's physical layer settings. Use it to stop reacting when the connection's radio settings change.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.offCharacteri: Stops listening for requests to read a characteristic from a connected Bluetooth device. Use it to stop reacting when a device reads your data.
Stops listening for requests to write a characteristic from a connected Bluetooth device. Use it to stop reacting when a device sends data to you.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.offConnection: Stops listening for changes in the connection state of a Bluetooth device. Use it to stop being notified when a device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.offDescriptor: Stops listening for requests to read a descriptor. Use it to stop being notified when a connected device reads a descriptor.
Stops listening for requests to write a descriptor. Use it to stop being notified when a connected device writes a descriptor.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.on: Subscribes to server events such as connection state changes and MTU changes. Use it to be notified when a device connects, disconnects, or the data packet size changes.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onBLEMtuChang: Subscribes to changes in the maximum data packet size for a Bluetooth connection. Use it to be notified when the transfer size changes during a connection.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onBlePhyUpdat: Subscribes to changes in the Bluetooth physical layer settings. Use it to be notified when the connection's radio settings are updated.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onCharacteris: Listens for a connected device reading a characteristic from your Bluetooth server. Use it to respond when another device requests data you are sharing over Bluetooth.
Listens for a connected device writing to a characteristic on your Bluetooth server. Use it to receive data or commands sent by another device over Bluetooth.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onConnectionS: Listens for changes in whether a device is connected to your Bluetooth server. Use it to know when another device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onDescriptorR: Listens for a connected device reading a descriptor from your Bluetooth server. Use it to respond when another device requests descriptor information you are sharing.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.onDescriptorW: Listens for a connected device writing to a descriptor on your Bluetooth server. Use it to receive descriptor updates sent by another device.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.readPhy: Reads the physical layer settings of a Bluetooth connection to a device. Use it to check the connection speed or radio mode for a paired device.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.removeAllServ: Removes all GATT services this device offers over Bluetooth. Use it to clear the services your device advertises before setting up new ones.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.removeService: Removes a service this device offers over Bluetooth. Use it to stop sharing that service with nearby devices.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.sendResponse: Sends a reply to a read or write request from a connected Bluetooth device. Use it to answer another device's request for data.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.setPhy: Sets the preferred Bluetooth radio setting for a connection to a device. Use it to try to adjust the connection speed or range with a paired device.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.startAdvertis: Starts broadcasting this device over Bluetooth so nearby devices can find it. Use it to make your device discoverable.
ConnectivityKit.GattServer.stopAdvertisi: Stops broadcasting this device over Bluetooth. Use it to make your device no longer discoverable.
ConnectivityKit.HandsFreeAudioGatewayPro: Connects to a device for hands-free calling over Bluetooth. Use it to link up with a car kit or headset for phone calls.
Disconnects a Bluetooth hands-free audio connection to a device. Use it to end a hands-free call link with a paired phone or car kit.
Stops listening for changes in the hands-free profile connection state. Use it to stop being notified when a hands-free device connects or disconnects.
Listens for changes in the hands-free profile connection state. Use it to be notified when a hands-free device connects or disconnects.
ConnectivityKit.HandsFreeHfProfile.conne: Starts a hands-free phone connection to a remote device. Use it to connect to a headset or car kit for phone calls.
ConnectivityKit.HandsFreeHfProfile.disco: Ends the hands-free phone connection with a paired device. Use it to hang up or stop using a car kit or headset for phone calls.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.off: Stops receiving APDU data for host card emulation. Use it to stop handling tap-to-pay or card emulation commands.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.offHceCmd: Stops receiving APDU data for host card emulation. Use it to stop handling tap-to-pay or card emulation commands.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.on: Registers to receive APDU data for host card emulation. Use it to let a phone act as a card, such as for tap-to-pay or a transit pass.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.onHceCmd: Starts receiving APDU data for host card emulation. Use it to handle tap-to-pay or card emulation commands.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.sendResponse: Sends a response back to a nearby card reader during a tap. Use it to answer a reader when your app is acting as a card being swiped.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.start: Starts card emulation and registers the app's card identifiers so it can be preferred while in the foreground. Use it to let a phone act as a card for tapping at a reader.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.startHCE: Turns on card emulation and registers the app's card identifiers. Use it to make the phone act as a card that can be tapped on a reader.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.stop: Stops card emulation and clears the app as the preferred card while in the foreground. Use it to end the phone acting as a card for tapping.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.stopHCE: Turns off card emulation. Use it to stop the phone acting as a card that can be tapped on a reader.
ConnectivityKit.HceService.transmit: Sends a response back to a nearby card reader. Use it to answer a reader when your app is acting as a card being tapped.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.connect: Starts a HID connection to a remote Bluetooth host device by its address. Use it to pair a keyboard, mouse, or game controller with a host.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.disconn: Ends the HID connection with the remote device. Use it to unpair or stop using a connected keyboard, mouse, or game controller.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.offGetR: Stops listening for GET_REPORT messages from the connected device. Use it to stop handling report requests from a keyboard, mouse, or game controller.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.offInte: Stops listening for interrupt data sent by the remote device. Use it to stop receiving input reports from a keyboard, mouse, or game controller.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.offSetP: Stops listening for SET_PROTOCOL messages from the connected device. Use it to stop handling protocol changes requested by a keyboard, mouse, or game controller.
ConnectivityKit.HidDeviceProfile.offSetR: Stops listening for SET_REPORT messages from the connected device. Use it to stop handling output reports sent to a keyboard, mouse, or game controller.

DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.installD: Creates a separate sandbox for an app so it can open protected files without exposing them to the rest of the app. Use it before opening a protected document so the file stays inside the authorized scope.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.isDLPFea: Checks whether the system supports encrypted file protection. Use it to see if encrypted file protection is available before trying to open or protect a file.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.isDLPFil: Checks whether a file is an encrypted protected file. Use it to decide whether to open a file in a protected sandbox.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.isInSand: Checks whether the app is running in a protected sandbox. Use it to know if the app is in a restricted environment before doing sandbox-only actions.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.off: Stops listening for protected file open or sandbox uninstall events. Use it to stop being notified when a protected file is opened or a sandbox app is uninstalled.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.on: Starts listening for protected file open or sandbox uninstall events. Use it to be notified when a protected file is opened or a sandbox app is uninstalled.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.openDLPF: Opens an encrypted protected file and gives back an object for managing its permissions. Use it when an authorized app needs to read or work with a protected document.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.processP: Handles plugin commands for transparent encryption and decryption. Use it to send commands to an enterprise security plugin while encrypting or decrypting files.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.queryDlp: Reads the header of a protected file and returns its plaintext policy as JSON. Use it to check what permissions and settings a protected file carries.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.queryOpe: Finds the enterprise-protected files that have already been opened. Use it to check which protected files are open or to keep track of them.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.setContr: Sets which apps are controlled by enterprise data protection. Use it to choose the apps whose data must be protected.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.setEnter: Sets the protection policy for enterprise apps. Use it by an administrator to apply data protection rules to company apps.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.setReten: Keeps the sandbox for a protected file alive after the file is closed. Use it when the same protected file is opened again and again, so it opens faster.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.setSandb: Sets configuration details for a sandbox app. Use it to pass custom settings that the sandbox app should run with.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.startDLP: Opens the data protection manager on the current page so file permissions can be set. Use it to let a person change a protected file's permissions and get the result back.
DataProtectionKit.dlpPermission.uninstal: Removes a previously created sandbox and frees its resources. Use it to clean up after an app no longer needs to open protected files.
DataProtectionKit.dlpSetDlpFeature.setDl: Turns the data-loss-prevention feature on or off, which controls whether an encryption option appears when right-clicking supported files. Use it to enable or disable file encryption under an enterprise policy.
DataProtectionKit.identifySensitiveConte: Scans a file and finds sensitive content such as labels and keywords based on rules you set. Use it to check whether a document contains private or sensitive information.
DeviceCertificateKit.CertCRLCollection.s: Finds the certificate revocation lists in a collection that match the criteria you give. Use it to pick out the revocation lists you need when checking whether certificates have been revoked.
Finds the certificates in a collection that match the criteria you give. Use it to pick out the certificates you need from a stored set.
Checks whether a chain of certificates is valid and trustworthy. Use it to confirm a certificate chain can be trusted before relying on it.
Checks whether a single certificate is valid by building and verifying its chain of trust. Use it to confirm a certificate is trustworthy before trusting it.
DeviceCertificateKit.CertExtension.check: Tells you whether a certificate is a CA certificate that can sign other certificates. Use it to check if a certificate is allowed to act as a certificate authority.
DeviceCertificateKit.CertExtension.getEn: Gets the serialized data of a certificate's extensions. Use it to read or save the raw extension bytes of a certificate.
Gets the value of one certificate extension entry by its OID. Use it to look up a specific extension's details in a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.CertExtension.getOi: Gets the OIDs of a certificate's extensions. Use it to list which extensions a certificate contains.
DeviceCertificateKit.CertExtension.hasUn: Checks whether a certificate has a critical extension that is not supported. Use it to decide whether a certificate can be trusted or accepted.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.addCer: Adds a certificate to a CMS signed-data message, such as the issuer certificate of a signing certificate. Use it to include certificates when building signed data.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.addRec: Adds recipient information to a CMS enveloped-data message; at least one recipient is required. Use it to set who can decrypt an encrypted message.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.addSig: Adds signer information to a CMS message of the signed data type. Use it to attach a certificate and private key so the message can be signed.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.doFina: Produces the final CMS message, such as signed data or enveloped data. Use it to finish creating a signed or encrypted message.
Produces the final CMS message, such as signed data or enveloped data, and returns it right away. Use it to finish creating a signed or encrypted message.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.getEnc: Gets the encrypted content data of an enveloped CMS message. Use it to retrieve the encrypted payload when detached enveloped data is generated.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsGenerator.setRec: Sets the encryption algorithm used for an enveloped CMS message. Use it to choose how the message content is encrypted.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsParser.decryptEn: Decrypts a CMS message of the enveloped data type. Use it to read the original content of an encrypted message.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsParser.getCerts: Gets the signer certificates or all certificates from a signed CMS message. Use it to check who signed a message or to collect the certificates it carries.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsParser.getConten: Gets the content data out of a signed CMS message. Use it to read the actual payload that was signed.
Tells you the content type of a CMS message. Use it to check what kind of CMS message you are holding before handling it.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsParser.setRawDat: Loads a CMS message into the parser in the given format. Use it to prepare a CMS message so you can read its content, certificates, or verify its signature.
DeviceCertificateKit.CmsParser.verifySig: Verifies the signature of a signed CMS message using the given configuration. Use it to confirm a signed message is authentic and unaltered.
DeviceCertificateKit.X500DistinguishedNa: Gets the DER-encoded data of an X.500 distinguished name. Use it to pass a name's raw bytes to other certificate or signing operations.
Gets the distinguished name as a text string, such as the common name or organization unit. Use it to read who a certificate or list belongs to.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getEncoded: Gets the serialized certificate revocation list data. Use it to save or send the list of revoked certificates.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getExtensio: Gets the certificate revocation list extension data in DER format. Use it to read extra details attached to a revocation list.
Gets the certificate revocation list extension object. Use it to inspect the extra details attached to a revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getIssuerNa: Gets the name of the authority that issued the certificate revocation list. Use it to find out who published the list of revoked certificates.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getIssuerX5: Gets the distinguished name of the authority that issued the certificate revocation list. Use it to identify who published the list of revoked certificates.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getLastUpda: Gets the date a certificate revocation list was last updated. Use it to check how current a list of revoked certificates is.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getNextUpda: Gets the date a certificate revocation list will next be updated. Use it to see when a fresh list of revoked certificates is due.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getRevokedC: Gets the revoked certificate entry matching a given serial number from a certificate revocation list. Use it to check whether a specific certificate has been revoked.
Gets the revoked certificate entry for a given certificate from a certificate revocation list. Use it to check whether that certificate has been revoked.
Gets all revoked certificate entries from a certificate revocation list. Use it to review every certificate that has been revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getSignatur: Gets the signature data of a certificate revocation list. Use it to verify that the list of revoked certificates is authentic.
Gets the name of the algorithm used to sign a certificate revocation list. Use it to check which signing method was used on a revoked-certificate list.
Gets the OID of the algorithm used to sign a certificate revocation list. Use it to identify the exact signing algorithm by its standard identifier.
Gets the parameters of the algorithm used to sign a certificate revocation list. Use it when you need the extra algorithm settings alongside the signing method.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getTBSInfo: Gets the DER-encoded body of a certificate revocation list, the part that is signed. Use it to inspect or verify the raw contents of a revoked-certificate list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getType: Gets the type of a certificate revocation list. Use it to tell what kind of revocation list you are holding.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.getVersion: Gets the version number of a certificate revocation list. Use it to check which CRL format version a revoked-certificate list uses.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.hashCode: Gets the hash value of the certificate revocation list data. Use it to compare or identify a revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.isRevoked: Checks whether a certificate has been revoked. Use it to confirm a certificate is still valid before trusting it.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.match: Checks whether this certificate revocation list matches given criteria. Use it to find the revocation list that applies to a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.toString: Turns the certificate revocation list into a text string. Use it to display or save the revocation list in readable form.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRL.verify: Verifies the signature of a certificate revocation list using a public key. Use it to confirm a revocation list is genuine and unaltered.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.getCer: Gets the issuer name of a revoked certificate from a revocation list entry. Use it to see who issued a revoked certificate.
Gets the distinguished name of the issuer of a revoked certificate in a certificate revocation list. Use it to find out which authority issued a revoked certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.getEnc: Gets the serialized data of a revoked certificate entry in a certificate revocation list. Use it when you need the raw encoded form of a revoked entry for storage or transfer.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.getExt: Gets the extensions of a revoked certificate entry in DER format. Use it to read extra details attached to a revoked entry.
Gets the extension object of a revoked certificate entry. Use it to inspect the extensions attached to a revoked entry.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.getRev: Gets the date on which a certificate was revoked. Use it to find out when a certificate was revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.getSer: Gets the serial number of a revoked certificate. Use it to identify which certificate was revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.hasExt: Checks whether a revoked certificate entry has extensions. Use it to find out if a revoked entry carries extra details.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.hashCo: Gets the hash value of a revoked certificate entry's data in DER format. Use it to identify or compare revoked certificate entries.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CRLEntry.toStri: Turns a revoked certificate entry's data into a text string. Use it to display or log the entry in readable form.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.checkValid: Checks whether an X.509 certificate is valid on a given date. Use it to confirm a certificate has not expired or is not yet active.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getBasicCo: Gets the basic constraints of an X.509 certificate. Use it to find out whether the certificate is a CA certificate and its path length limit.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getCRLDist: Gets the CRL distribution point addresses of an X.509 certificate. Use it to find where to download the certificate revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getCertSer: Gets the serial number of an X.509 certificate. Use it to identify or look up a specific certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getEncoded: Gets the serialized data of an X.509 certificate. Use it to save or send the certificate in its encoded form.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getExtKeyU: Gets the extended key usage of an X.509 certificate. Use it to check what purposes the certificate is allowed for.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getExtensi: Gets the extension object of an X.509 certificate. Use it to read the extra details attached to a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getIssuerA: Gets the issuer alternative names of an X.509 certificate. Use it to find other names for the certificate issuer.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getIssuerN: Gets the issuer name of an X.509 certificate in a chosen encoding. Use it to see who issued the certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getIssuerX: Gets the X.500 distinguished name of the certificate issuer. Use it to read the issuer's full distinguished name.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getItem: Reads a chosen field out of an X.509 certificate and returns it in DER format. Use it to pull a specific piece of certificate data when checking a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getKeyUsag: Tells you what a certificate's key is allowed to be used for. Use it to check whether a certificate may sign, encrypt, or serve other purposes.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getNotAfte: Gives the date and time when a certificate expires. Use it to check whether a certificate is still valid or has run out.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getNotBefo: Gives the date and time when a certificate becomes valid. Use it to check whether a certificate is already in effect.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getPublicK: Gets the public key held in an X.509 certificate, for verifying with that certificate. Use it to check a signature against the certificate's key.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getSerialN: Gets the serial number of an X.509 certificate. Use it to identify or tell apart individual certificates.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getSignatu: Gets the signature data of an X.509 certificate. Use it to check or verify the signature that secures a certificate.
Gets the name of the algorithm used to sign an X.509 certificate. Use it to check how a certificate was signed when verifying its trustworthiness.
Gets the object identifier of the algorithm used to sign an X.509 certificate. Use it to look up the exact signing algorithm when checking a certificate.
Gets the parameters of the algorithm used to sign an X.509 certificate. Use it to inspect the signing details when validating a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getSubject: Gets the subject alternative names of an X.509 certificate, such as other names it is valid for. Use it to check which hostnames or addresses a certificate covers.
Gets the subject name of an X.509 certificate. Use it to see who or what the certificate was issued to.
Gets the X.500 distinguished name of an X.509 certificate's subject. Use it to read the full structured identity of who the certificate belongs to.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.getVersion: Gets the version number of an X.509 certificate. Use it to check which certificate version you are working with.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.hashCode: Gets the hash value of the certificate data in DER format. Use it to compare or identify a certificate by its hash.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.match: Checks whether a certificate matches given parameters. Use it to find or confirm the right certificate among several.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.toString: Turns the certificate into a text string in a chosen encoding. Use it to display or save the certificate as readable text.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Cert.verify: Verifies the certificate's signature using a public key. Use it to confirm a certificate is genuine and trustworthy.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CertChain.getCe: Gets the list of X.509 certificates in a certificate chain. Use it to read each certificate in the chain.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CertChain.hashC: Gets the hash value of the certificate chain data in DER format. Use it to check or compare a certificate chain's fingerprint.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CertChain.toStr: Turns the certificate chain object's data into a text string. Use it to display or log the certificate chain in readable form.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CertChain.valid: Checks whether a certificate chain is valid using the given validation parameters. Use it to confirm a certificate chain can be trusted.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getEncoded: Gets the serialized data of an X.509 certificate revocation list. Use it to save or send the revocation list in its encoded form.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getIssuerNa: Gets the issuer name of an X.509 certificate revocation list. Use it to find out which authority issued the revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getLastUpda: Gets the date the X.509 certificate revocation list was last updated. Use it to check how current a revocation list is.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getNextUpda: Gets the next update date of a certificate revocation list. Use it to check when a revocation list expires and needs refreshing.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getRevokedC: Gets the revoked certificate entry matching a given certificate serial number. Use it to look up whether a specific certificate has been revoked.
Gets the revoked certificate entry for a given certificate. Use it to check whether a particular certificate appears on a revocation list.
Gets all revoked certificate entries from a certificate revocation list. Use it to review every certificate that has been revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getSignatur: Gets the signature data of a certificate revocation list. Use it to verify that a revocation list is authentic and untampered.
Gets the name of the signing algorithm used for a certificate revocation list. Use it to see which algorithm signed a revocation list.
Gets the OID of the algorithm used to sign a certificate revocation list. Use it to check which signing algorithm a revocation list uses.
Gets the parameters of the algorithm used to sign a certificate revocation list. Use it to inspect the signing algorithm settings of a revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getTbsInfo: Gets the DER-encoded certificate list information from a certificate revocation list. Use it to read the raw signed contents of a revocation list.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getType: Gets the type of a certificate revocation list. Use it to tell what kind of revocation list you are holding.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.getVersion: Gets the version of a certificate revocation list. Use it to check which version a revocation list follows.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.isRevoked: Checks whether a certificate has been revoked according to a certificate revocation list. Use it to confirm a certificate is still valid before trusting it.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509Crl.verify: Checks that a certificate revocation list's signature is genuine using a public key. Use it to confirm a revocation list really came from the authority that issued it.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CrlEntry.getCer: Gets the name of the authority that issued a revoked certificate. Use it to see which issuer a revoked certificate belongs to.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CrlEntry.getEnc: Gets the serialized data of a revoked certificate entry. Use it to save or pass on the raw entry data.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CrlEntry.getRev: Gets the date a certificate was revoked. Use it to check when a certificate stopped being valid.
DeviceCertificateKit.X509CrlEntry.getSer: Gets the serial number of a revoked certificate. Use it to identify which certificate was revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.buildX509CertC: Builds a chain of X.509 certificates from a set of certificates and given parameters. Use it to assemble a trusted certificate chain for verifying a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createCertCRLC: Builds a collection object holding X.509 certificates and certificate revocation lists. Use it to group certificates and revocation lists together for checking whether a certificate is still trusted.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createCertChai: Creates a validator that checks a certificate chain using the PKIX algorithm. Use it to verify that a chain of certificates is valid and trusted.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createCertExte: Creates a certificate extension object from serialized extension data. Use it to read and work with the extra fields attached to a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createCmsGener: Creates a generator for building CMS messages of a chosen type. Use it to produce signed or encrypted CMS message data.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createCmsParse: Creates a parser for CMS messages. Use it to read and inspect the contents of a CMS message.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createPkcs12: Packs certificate data into a P12 file in DER format. Use it to bundle a certificate and key into a password-protected file for storage or transfer.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createPkcs12Sy: Packs certificate data into a P12 file in DER format. Use it to bundle a certificate and key into one password-protected file for storage or transfer.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createTrustAnc: Builds a list of trusted certificate anchors from the CA certificates inside a password-protected P12 keystore file. Use it to set up which certificates your app will trust when checking secure connections.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createX500Dist: Creates a distinguished name object from a slash-separated name string such as CN, O, OU, C, ST, and L. Use it to describe the owner or issuer identity when building or checking a certificate.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createX509CRL: Creates a certificate revocation list object from serialized CRL data. Use it to check whether a certificate has been revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createX509Cert: Creates an X.509 certificate object from certificate data. Use it to load a certificate so you can inspect or work with it.
Creates a certificate chain object from an array of X.509 certificates. Use it to group a certificate with its issuers so the chain can be verified.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.createX509Crl: Creates a certificate revocation list object from serialized CRL data. Use it to check whether a certificate has been revoked.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.generateCsr: Creates a certificate signing request from a private key and configuration. Use it to request a certificate from a certificate authority.
DeviceCertificateKit.cert.parsePkcs12: Reads a P12 file and returns the certificates and keys inside it. Use it to open a password-protected certificate bundle.
Stops an ongoing signing or signature verification operation. Use it to cancel a signature check you no longer need.
Completes a signing or signature verification operation after the earlier steps. Use it to produce a signature or confirm that a signature is valid.
Retrieves all private credentials stored for the app. Use it to list the private certificates available for signing or authentication.
Gets all private certificates belonging to one app, identified by its UID. Used by certificate management apps to list an app's private certificates.
Gets the public certificates of all users. Used by certificate management apps to list every user's public certificates.
Gets all system certificates. Used by certificate management apps to list the system's certificates.
Gets the user's trusted root certificates. Use it to see which certificate authorities the user trusts.
Gets the list of apps authorized to use a user's public certificate. Used by certificate management apps to see which apps may use that certificate.
Returns the storage path for a certificate. Use it to find where a certificate is kept on the device.
Gets the details of one private credential, identified by its key URI. Use it to look up a stored private certificate when you need its information.
Gets the credentials installed for the application. Use it to list the app's installed certificates.
Gets the details of one public credential, identified by its key URI. Use it to look up a user's public certificate information.
Gets the details of a system app's certificate. Used by certificate management apps to view a system app certificate's details.
Gets details of a CA certificate trusted by the system. Used by certificate management apps to view a trusted CA certificate's details.
Gets the list of CA certificates the system trusts. Use it to see which certificate authorities are trusted on the device.
Gets the details of a USB Key credential. Use it to read a certificate stored on a USB security key.
Gets the list of credentials on a USB Key device. Use it to see which certificates a USB security key holds.
Gets the details of a user root CA certificate. Use it to look up a trusted root certificate the user installed.
Allows an app to use a user's public credential. Use it to let another app access a user's certificate.
Imports a certificate onto a USB Key using its credential URI and certificate data. Use it to add a certificate to a USB security key.

Starts a signing or signature verification operation with a credential, returning a handle for the later update and finish steps. Use it as the first step when signing or verifying with a certificate.
Installs a private credential from a keystore file with its password and an alias. Use it to set up a private key and certificate for secure use.
Installs a user's public credential from a keystore file. Use it to add a user's certificate and key pair to the device.
Installs a system application credential from a keystore file. Use it to add a system app's certificate and key pair to the device.
Installs a user CA certificate. Use it to add a trusted certificate so the device trusts that authority.
Installs a user CA certificate and returns the installation result. Use it to add a trusted certificate so the device trusts that authority.
Checks whether this application is authorized by a specified user credential. Use it to confirm the app may use that credential before relying on it.
Removes an app's permission to use a user's public credential. Use it to revoke another app's access to a user's certificate.
Turns a user's CA certificate on or off. Use it to enable or disable a certificate so it is trusted or not.
Removes all system application credentials and public user credentials. Used by the certificate management app to clear every stored app certificate at once.
Removes all CA certificates the user has trusted. Used by the certificate management app to clear all user-trusted certificates at once.
Removes a private credential using its unique identifier. Use it to delete a private certificate you no longer need.
Removes one public credential belonging to the user, identified by its unique key. Used by the certificate management app to delete a specific public certificate.
Removes the credential of a system application, identified by its unique key. Used by the certificate management app to delete a specific system app certificate.
Removes a user CA certificate using its unique identifier. Use it to delete a trusted certificate you no longer want.
Feeds data into an ongoing signing or signature verification operation. Use it to supply the content you want to sign or check.
DeviceCertificateKit.certificateManagerD: Opens a page where you authorize an app to use certificate credentials. Use it to let an app sign, verify, or view certificate details.
Opens a dialog showing a certificate's details, such as its validity period, issuer, and user. Use it to view information about a certificate.
Opens the certificate management dialog showing a chosen page. Use it to view, install, or uninstall certificates.
Opens the install certificate dialog so a certificate can be installed. Use it to add a certificate to the device and get its identifier for later use.
Opens the PIN entry dialog for a USB key credential so the user can authorize it. Use it to unlock the USB key credential for signing and encryption.
Opens the uninstall certificate dialog to remove a certificate. Use it to delete an installed CA certificate from the device.
Checks whether the device supports opening the CA certificate management dialogs. Use it to know if certificate install, uninstall, and detail dialogs can be shown.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.close: Destroys the connection object and releases its resources. Use it to disconnect from a peer device when interaction is finished.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.connect: Connects to the server on a peer device. Use it to start interacting with another device, up to ten connections at a time.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.disconn: Ends the link to a nearby device. Use it to stop a device-to-device session when you are done sharing data.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.getPeer: Gets the ID of the nearby device you are connected to. Use it to find out which device you are linked with.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.off: Stops listening for a connection ending. Use it when you no longer need to be told that a device link has dropped.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.offConn: Stops listening for connection results. Use it when you no longer need to be told whether a device link succeeded.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.offData: Stops listening for incoming data. Use it when you no longer need to receive data sent from a nearby device.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.offDisc: Stops listening for a dropped connection. Use it when you no longer need to be told that a device link has ended.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.on: Registers a listener for connection events such as connect result, disconnection, or received data. Use it to react when a peer device connects, drops, or sends data.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.onConne: Registers a listener that reports the result of connecting to a peer device. Use it to know whether a device connection succeeded or failed.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.onDataR: Registers a listener that receives data sent from a connected peer device. Use it to handle incoming data from another device.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.onDisco: Registers a listener that reports when a peer device connection is terminated or fails. Use it to detect when a device drops off and react to the disconnection.
DistributedServiceKit.Connection.sendDat: Sends data to a connected peer device after the connection is established. Use it to pass data between connected devices.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.auth: Authenticates another device using its device information and authentication parameters. Used to verify and trust a nearby device before connecting to it.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.bind: Binds a device using authentication parameters such as PIN authentication. Use it to pair with and connect to another device.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.dele: Deletes credential information given the credential details to remove. Used to clear a stored device credential so it can no longer be used.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getA: Gets all trusted devices and local devices. Use it to see which devices you can connect to or share with.
Gets all trusted devices and local devices right away. Use it to list the devices you can connect to or share with.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getD: Gets the icon for a device. Use it to show a picture of a nearby or trusted device in a device list.
Gets details about one device from its network ID. Use it to look up a specific trusted or local device.
Gets a device's name from its network ID. Use it to show which device you are connected to.
Gets the network IDs of devices matching your filter. Use it to find which devices are available to connect to.
Lists the devices signed in to the same account. Use it to see your other devices and pick one to work with.
Gets a device's type from its network ID. Use it to tell what kind of device you are connected to.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getI: Looks up device identification details from a list of device IDs. Use it to identify which devices are which.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getL: Gets the ID of your own device. Use it to identify this device when connecting or sharing.
Gets information about the device you are using. Use it to show or check details of your own device.
Gets information about the device you are using right now. Use it to find out details about your own device.
Gets the name of your own device. Use it to show this device's name when connecting or sharing.
Gets the network ID of the device you are using. Use it to identify your own device when connecting or sharing with nearby devices.
Gets the type of the device you are using. Use it to tell what kind of device you are on, such as a phone or tablet.
Gets the display name of your own device, limited to a set length. Use it to show or share the name of the device you are on.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getO: Tells you what operating system another device on the network runs. Use it to check whether a nearby device is compatible before connecting.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.getT: Gets the list of devices you have already trusted and paired with. Use it to see which of your devices you can connect to.
Gets the list of trusted devices and can quickly bring offline ones back online. Use it to refresh which of your paired devices are currently reachable.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.impo: Imports credential information used to trust a device. Use it to set up trust so you can connect to another device.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.off: Stops listening for the device service shutting down. Use it to stop being notified when the device connection service dies.
DistributedServiceKit.DeviceManager.offD: Stops listening for changes to a device's name. Use it to stop being notified when a nearby device is renamed.

LocalizationKit.System.getUsingNumerical: Gets the numerical date pattern currently used by the system locale. Use it to show dates in the format the device's region expects.
