LocalizationKit.System.setSystemMeasurem: Sets the measurement system used by the system locale. Use it to switch the device between metric and imperial units.
LocalizationKit.System.setSystemNumberPa: Sets the number pattern used by the system locale. Use it to change how numbers are formatted on the device.
LocalizationKit.System.setSystemNumberin: Sets the numbering system used by the system locale. Use it to change the digits used to display numbers on the device.
LocalizationKit.System.setSystemNumerica: Sets the numerical date pattern used by the system locale. Use it to change how dates are shown across the system.
LocalizationKit.System.setSystemRegion: Sets the system region. Use it to change the country or region the device uses for regional settings.
LocalizationKit.System.setTemperatureTyp: Sets the temperature unit of the system. Use it to switch weather and temperature readings between units like Celsius and Fahrenheit.
LocalizationKit.System.setUsingLocalDigi: Turns use of local digits on or off. Use it to show numbers in the digits of the local language.
LocalizationKit.SystemLocaleManager.getL: Gets a sorted list of languages. Use it to build a language picker in settings or a startup guide.
LocalizationKit.SystemLocaleManager.getR: Gets a sorted list of country or region IDs. Use it to build a country or region picker in settings or a startup guide.
LocalizationKit.SystemLocaleManager.getT: Gets a sorted list of time zone city items. Use it to let someone pick their city or time zone when setting up a device.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getAppDefaultTi: Gets the time zone the app uses, either one set earlier or the system's. Use it to show times in the right zone, such as where am I in the world.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getAvailableIDs: Gets the list of time zone IDs the system supports. Use it to let someone pick their time zone from a list.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getAvailableZon: Gets the list of time zone city IDs the system supports. Use it to let someone pick their city for time zone settings.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getCityDisplayN: Gets a time zone city's name shown in a chosen language. Use it to label city choices in a time zone picker.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getDisplayName: Gets the name of a time zone in a chosen language. Use it to show a readable time zone name to someone.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getID: Gets the identifier of a time zone. Use it to tell which time zone you are working with.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getOffset: Gets how far a time zone is from standard time at a given moment. Use it to work out the local clock time for a place.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getRawOffset: Gets the base difference between a time zone and standard time, without seasonal changes. Use it to compare time zones.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getTimezoneFrom: Creates a time zone for a named city. Use it to find the time zone of a city someone names.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.getTimezonesByL: Creates time zones for a place given its longitude and latitude. Use it to find where you are in time zone terms.
LocalizationKit.TimeZone.setAppDefaultTi: Sets the default time zone for the current app, used for the app's runtime. Use it to make date and time formatting follow a chosen time zone, such as "Asia/Shanghai".
LocalizationKit.Transliterator.getAvaila: Lists the IDs supported for text transliteration. Use it to see which transliteration options are available.
LocalizationKit.Transliterator.getInstan: Creates a transliterator object from a given ID. Use it to set up text transliteration, such as converting text between scripts.
LocalizationKit.Transliterator.transform: Converts input text from its source format to a target format. Use it to transliterate text, such as changing names or words into another writing system.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.detectEncoding: Detects the encoding of an input byte stream and returns the encoding name and confidence. Use it to find out how text bytes are encoded, such as when reading a file of unknown encoding.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.getType: Gets the character type of the input character. Use it to check what kind of character something is, such as a letter, digit, or unassigned code point.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isDigit: Checks whether the input character is a digit. Use it to tell if a character is a number, such as when validating typed input.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isIdeograph: Checks whether a character is an ideographic character, such as those used in Chinese or Japanese writing. Use it to tell if text is made of ideographs.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isLetter: Checks whether a character is a letter. Use it to tell letters apart from digits, spaces, or symbols when validating text.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isLowerCase: Checks whether a character is a lowercase letter. Use it to tell lowercase letters apart from uppercase ones in text.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isRTL: Checks whether a character belongs to a right-to-left language such as Arabic or Hebrew. Use it to detect text that reads right to left.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isSpaceChar: Checks whether a character is a space. Use it to find or skip spaces when processing text.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isUpperCase: Checks whether a character is an uppercase letter. Use it to tell uppercase letters apart from lowercase ones in text.
LocalizationKit.Unicode.isWhitespace: Checks whether a character is a whitespace. Use it to tell spaces and tabs apart from other characters when reading or cleaning up text.
LocalizationKit.Util.unitConvert: Converts a measurement value from one unit to another and formats it for a chosen locale and style. Use it to show distances, weights, or temperatures in the units a person expects.
LocalizationKit.fontManager.dataMigratio: Starts a font data migration task during a device upgrade and reports progress and results. Use it to move existing fonts over when a phone or tablet is upgraded.
LocalizationKit.fontManager.installFont: Installs a font file from a path into the system font library so apps can use it by name. Use it to add a new font to the device.
LocalizationKit.fontManager.uninstallFon: Removes an installed font from the system font library by its font name. Use it to delete a font that is no longer wanted.
LocalizationKit.i18n.addPreferredLanguag: Adds a language to the preferred language list at a chosen position. Use it to put a language higher or lower in the order of languages a person wants.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getCalendar: Gets a calendar object for a chosen locale and calendar type. Use it to work with dates such as holidays or the day of the week in a particular region.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getChineseCalendar: Gets a Chinese calendar object for a chosen locale. Use it to look up Chinese lunar dates such as festivals and traditional holidays.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getDisplayCountry: Gets the name of a country or region written in a chosen language. Use it to show a country's name in the reader's own language.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getDisplayLanguage: Gets the localized name of a language for a given locale. Use it to show a language's name in the user's own language, such as in a language picker.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getFirstPreferredLa: Gets the first language in the user's preferred language list. Use it to find the user's top language choice for displaying content.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getInstance: Creates an object for working with text indexing in a given locale. Use it to build or search an index of words in text.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getLineInstance: Gets an object that finds line break points in text for a locale. Use it to wrap text correctly when displaying paragraphs.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getPreferredLanguag: Gets the list of languages the user prefers. Use it to choose which language to show content in.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getSimpleDateTimeFo: Creates a date and time formatter from a custom pattern. Use it to display dates and times in a specific format you choose.
Creates a date and time formatter from a skeleton pattern. Use it to show dates and times in a chosen style, such as a calendar entry or clock display.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getSimpleNumberForm: Creates a number formatter from a skeleton pattern. Use it to display numbers in a chosen style, such as prices or measurements.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getSystemLanguage: Gets the system language ID. Use it to find out which language the device is set to, for example to show text in the user's language.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getSystemLocale: Gets the system locale ID. Use it to find the device's locale setting, for example to format dates and numbers correctly.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getSystemRegion: Gets the system region ID. Use it to find the device's region setting, for example to show the right country format.
LocalizationKit.i18n.getTimeZone: Gets a time zone object for a given time zone ID. Use it to show the correct local time, for example in a clock or calendar.
LocalizationKit.i18n.is24HourClock: Checks whether the device is set to use the 24-hour clock. Use it to decide how to show times, such as in a clock or alarm display.
LocalizationKit.i18n.isRTL: Checks whether a language is written right to left. Use it to decide whether to mirror the layout for right-to-left languages.
LocalizationKit.i18n.removePreferredLang: Removes a language from a chosen position in the preferred language list. Use it to manage which languages the user prefers.
LocalizationKit.i18n.set24HourClock: Turns the 24-hour clock on or off. Use it to switch how times are shown, such as between 13:00 and 1:00 PM.
LocalizationKit.resourceManager.getResou: Gets the resource manager for a named application. Use it to load that app's text, images, and other resources.
LocalizationKit.resourceManager.getSysRe: Gets a resource manager for the system's preset resources. Use it to load built-in system text and images.
LocalizationKit.resourceManager.getSyste: Gets a system resource manager for reading built-in system resources. Use it to load preset system text, images, or other resources in your app.
LocationKit.FenceExtensionAbility.onDest: Runs just before a geofence extension is destroyed. Use it to clean up when a geofence alert feature shuts down.
LocationKit.FenceExtensionAbility.onFenc: Runs when a geofence status changes, telling you the transition and extra details. Use it to react when someone enters or leaves a chosen area.
LocationKit.FenceExtensionContext.startA: Starts a service extension ability using the given want information. Use it to launch a background service, such as one that handles geofence events.
LocationKit.Geolocation.getLocation: Obtains the device's geographic location. Use it to find where you are.
LocationKit.Geolocation.getLocationType: Obtains the location types the system supports. Use it to check which positioning methods are available on the device.
LocationKit.Geolocation.getSupportedCoor: Obtains the coordinate system types the system supports. Use it to see which coordinate formats you can get locations in.
LocationKit.Geolocation.subscribe: Starts listening for the device's geographical location, with the latest call replacing earlier ones. Use it to keep track of where you are.
LocationKit.Geolocation.unsubscribe: Stops listening for the device's geographical location. Use it to stop tracking where you are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.addBeacon: Adds a beacon fence and reports its ID. Use it to be alerted when the device enters or leaves an area around a beacon.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.addFusion: Adds a fusion fence for location-based monitoring. Use it to set up an alert when someone enters or leaves an area.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.addGnssGe: Adds a geofence and reports its ID. Use it to be alerted when the device enters or leaves a chosen area.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.disableLo: Turns off the device's location switch. Use it to stop location tracking, for example to save battery or when the user wants to stop being located.
Turns off the location switch for a specified user. Use it to stop location tracking for one user account on a shared device.
Turns off simulated location data. Use it to stop testing with fake locations and return to real positioning.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.disableRe: Turns off simulated reverse geocoding results. Use it to stop testing with fake addresses and return to real address lookup.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.enableLoc: Turns on the device's location switch. Use it to start finding where you are, for example for maps or navigation.
Turns on the location switch for a specified user. Use it to start finding where a particular user account is on a shared device.
Turns on simulated location data instead of real GPS. Use it to test location features like where am I without moving.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.enableRev: Turns on simulated reverse geocoding, giving fake addresses for coordinates. Use it to test address lookup from a location without real data.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.findMatch: Checks whether nearby WLAN scan results match a list of WLAN BSSIDs and returns the matches above a signal threshold. Use it to find specific Wi-Fi devices around you.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.flushCach: Returns all stored GNSS locations to the app and clears the buffer. Use it to collect the locations recorded while the device was tracking position.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getActive: Gets all currently active geofences, with each fence's ID and details. Use it to see which location-based reminders or boundaries are active.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getAddres: Turns a latitude and longitude into address information. Use it to find out what place you are at, like a street address.
Turns a place name or address into latitude and longitude. Use it to find where a place is on a map.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getCached: Gets how many cached satellite location points are waiting to be reported. Use it to check stored location data before retrieving it.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getCountr: Gets the country code for where the device currently is. Use it to know which country you are in.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getCurren: Gets information about the district where the device currently is. Use it to find out which local area you are in.
Gets the device's current location. Use it to find where you are.
Gets the BSSID of the Wi-Fi hotspot you are connected to. Use it to identify the current Wi-Fi network for locating where you are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getDistan: Works out the distance between two locations. Use it to see how far apart two places are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getGeofen: Lists the coordinate system types that geofences support. Use it to check which coordinate formats work when setting up a geofence alert for a place.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getLastLo: Gets the most recently known location. Use it to quickly find where you are without waiting for a fresh position.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getLocati: Gets nearby WiFi and Bluetooth scan information used to work out a location. Use it to help determine where am I when GPS is weak.
Tells you the current status of the location icon. Use it to check whether location is being shown as active on the device.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getPoiInf: Gets information about the point of interest at your current spot. Use it to find out what place or business you are near.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.getPostPr: Gets the recorded track for a sport mode such as skiing after tracking has started. Use it to review the route you travelled during that activity.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isBeaconF: Checks whether the device supports beacon fencing. Use it to see if you can set up alerts when near a beacon.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isCachedG: Checks whether the device supports cached satellite positioning. Use it to see if location can be found faster or without a live signal.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isFusionF: Checks whether fusion fence service is available on the device. Use it to see if geofencing features can be used.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isGeocode: Checks whether the geocoding service is available. Use it to see if you can turn coordinates into an address or an address into coordinates.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isGnssFen: Checks whether the device supports satellite-based geofencing. Use it to see if you can get alerts when entering or leaving an area.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isGnssSer: Checks whether the device supports satellite positioning. Use it to see if you can find where you are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isLocatio: Checks whether the location switch is turned on. Use it to see if location services are currently available.
Checks whether location is switched on for a given user. Use it to find out if location services are enabled before asking where am I.
Checks whether the user has agreed to the location privacy terms. Use it to see if location features are allowed before asking for the user's location.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isPoiServ: Checks whether the point-of-interest service is available on the device. Use it to find out if you can look up nearby places.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.isWlanBss: Checks whether nearby Wi-Fi scan results match a given list of network identifiers, above a signal strength threshold. Use it to tell if you are near specific Wi-Fi networks.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.off: Stops listening for location service events such as NMEA messages. Use it to stop receiving location updates you no longer need.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offBlueto: Stops Bluetooth scanning and stops listening for Bluetooth scan result changes. Use it to end Bluetooth-based location scanning.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offCached: Stops receiving updates of cached satellite location results. Use it to stop getting stored location updates.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offCountr: Stops listening for changes to the country code. Use it to stop being told when the country you are in changes.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offGnssFe: Removes a geofence and stops reporting when you enter or leave it. Use it to stop alerts for arriving at or leaving a place.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offLocati: Stops WiFi and Bluetooth scanning and cancels updates about nearby scan data. Use it to stop watching nearby networks and devices when you no longer need them for finding where you are.
Stops receiving updates when the device's location changes. Use it to stop tracking where you are when you no longer need location updates.
Stops receiving updates when the location switch is turned on or off. Use it to stop watching whether location services are enabled.
Stops receiving continuous location error updates. Use it to stop being notified when location tracking fails.
Cancels updates about changes to the location icon status. Use it to stop being told when the location indicator on screen changes.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offNmeaMe: Stops receiving NMEA messages from the location service. Use it to stop listening to raw satellite positioning data.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.offSatell: Stops receiving updates when satellite status changes. Use it to stop watching satellite signal information for positioning.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.on: Subscribes to NMEA messages from the location service. Use it to receive raw satellite positioning data while finding where you are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onBluetoo: Listens for Bluetooth scanning results used by location services. Use it to keep track of nearby Bluetooth signals that help determine where you are.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onCachedG: Subscribes to updates of cached satellite location points. Use it to receive stored location fixes, such as for tracking where you have been.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onCountry: Listens for changes to the country code. Use it to know when the country you are in changes, for example while travelling.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onGnssFen: Adds a geofence and listens for its status changes, starting a chosen ability when the fence event triggers. Use it to get notified when you enter or leave a place.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onLocatin: Starts watching for changes in WiFi and Bluetooth scan data and uses it to find your location. Use it to locate yourself using nearby networks and devices.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onLocatio: Subscribes to location changes. Use it to keep receiving where you are as you move, such as for navigation or tracking.
Listens for changes to the location switch. Use it to know when location services are turned on or off.
Watches for changes in location errors and reports them. Use it to detect when getting your location fails.
Starts watching for changes to the location icon status. Use it to be told when the location indicator on screen changes.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onNmeaMes: Watches for incoming NMEA messages from the location system. Use it to read raw satellite navigation data.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.onSatelli: Watches for changes in satellite status. Use it to see how many satellites are being tracked for your location.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.removeBea: Removes a beacon fence. Use it to stop watching for when you enter or leave a place marked by a beacon.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.removeFus: Removes a fusion fence by its identifier. Use it to stop being alerted when you leave or enter a place you had set up a fence around.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.removeGns: Removes a geofence by its ID. Use it to stop watching for when you enter or leave a chosen area.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.sendComma: Sends an extended command to the location system. Use it to control location features that need extra instructions.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.setLocati: Sets whether the location privacy agreement has been confirmed. Use it to record that a user accepted the location privacy terms before location features are used.
Sets whether the app's location behavior is not controlled by the location switch. Use it to let an app keep locating even when the device location switch is off.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.setMocked: Sets the locations and reporting intervals used for simulated location. Use it to fake a position, for example when testing location-based features.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.setRevers: Sets the locations and place names used for simulated reverse geocoding. Use it to fake the place name returned for a location, for example when testing where-am-I features.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.startBlue: Starts scanning for Bluetooth devices and returns those matching the IDs you specify. Use it to find nearby Bluetooth devices by their known identifiers.
LocationKit.geoLocationManager.stopBluet: Stops the Bluetooth scanning and searching that was already running. Use it to end a Bluetooth device search.
LocationKit.geolocation.flushCachedGnssL: Returns all stored GNSS locations to your app and clears the buffer. Use it to collect saved location points and free the cache.
LocationKit.geolocation.getAddressesFrom: Turns a location into address details. Use it to find out what address you are at, like a street or city name.
Turns an address into latitude and longitude. Use it to find where a place is on a map.
LocationKit.geolocation.getCachedGnssLoc: Tells you how many GNSS locations are stored in the cache. Use it to check how many saved location points are waiting.
LocationKit.geolocation.getCurrentLocati: Gets the device's current location. Use it to find where you are.
LocationKit.geolocation.getLastLocation: Gets the most recent location the system has stored. Use it to find where you are right away without waiting for a fresh fix.
LocationKit.geolocation.isGeoServiceAvai: Checks whether the geocoding service is available. Use it to see if you can turn coordinates into addresses or look up places.
LocationKit.geolocation.isLocationEnable: Checks whether the location switch is turned on. Use it to see if location services are enabled before asking where you are.
LocationKit.geolocation.off: Stops listening for location changes and removes a geofence. Use it to stop being told when you move or when you enter or leave an area.
LocationKit.geolocation.on: Starts listening for location events such as raw satellite messages and geofence changes. Use it to be told when you move or when you enter or leave an area.
LocationKit.geolocation.requestEnableLoc: Asks the user to turn on location services. Use it when you need to find where you are but location is switched off.
LocationKit.geolocation.sendCommand: Sends an extended command to the location subsystem. Use it to control location services, such as starting or stopping location requests.

Reports when an app is updated on a managed enterprise device. Use it to notify the enterprise administrator that an app was updated.
Reports when the device administrator app is disabled. Use it to notify the enterprise administrator that the device is no longer under management.

MDMKit.accountManager.activateOsAccount: Switches the device to another system account. Use it to move between user accounts on a managed phone or tablet.
MDMKit.accountManager.addOsAccount: Adds a device account in the background, as an administrator, normal, or guest account. Use it to create a user account on a managed device.
MDMKit.accountManager.addOsAccountAsync: Creates a new device account in the background without user interaction. Use it to set up accounts in bulk or remotely for managed devices.
MDMKit.accountManager.createNormalOsAcco: Creates a normal system account, up to two in total. Use it to set up an extra user account on a managed device.
MDMKit.accountManager.disallowAddLocalAc: Sets whether creating local accounts on the device is forbidden. Use it to stop users from adding new local accounts on a managed device.
MDMKit.accountManager.disallowAddOsAccou: Stops a user from adding accounts on the device. Use it to block someone from creating new local accounts.
MDMKit.accountManager.disallowOsAccountA: Blocks users from adding new accounts, for one user or all users. Use it to stop employees creating local accounts on a work device.
MDMKit.accountManager.getDomainAccountPo: Gets the domain account policy, either global or for one domain account. Use it to check the current policy settings for work accounts.
MDMKit.accountManager.isAddOsAccountByUs: Checks whether a user is blocked from adding accounts. Use it to see if account creation is currently forbidden for that user.
MDMKit.accountManager.isOsAccountAdditio: Checks whether adding accounts is blocked for a user. Use it to confirm that account creation is still forbidden on a managed device.
MDMKit.accountManager.removeOsAccount: Removes a system account by its ID, except the default account. Use it to delete an extra user account from a managed phone or tablet.
MDMKit.accountManager.setDomainAccountPo: Sets the domain account policy, either for all domain accounts or one. Use it to apply rules to work accounts on a managed device.
MDMKit.adminManager.authorizeAdmin: Grants administrator rights to a chosen application. Use it to let an app manage the device as an administrator.
MDMKit.adminManager.disableAdmin: Turns off a device administrator app for a chosen user, so it no longer manages the device. Use it to revoke an app's device management rights.
MDMKit.adminManager.disableDeviceAdmin: Lets a super device administrator app switch off another device administrator app, removing its device management rights. Use it to revoke management permissions from an admin app.
MDMKit.adminManager.disableSuperAdmin: Turns off a super device administrator application. Use it to remove super administrator control from an app.
MDMKit.adminManager.enableAdmin: Turns on a device administrator application so it can manage the device. Use it to set up an app as a device administrator.
MDMKit.adminManager.enableDeviceAdmin: Lets a super device administrator app switch on another device administrator app and give it device management rights. Use it to grant an app device management permissions.
MDMKit.adminManager.enableSelfDeviceAdmi: Lets an MDM app turn on its own device administrator rights using a credential, for super or normal admin roles. Use it to activate the app's own device management permissions.
MDMKit.adminManager.getAdmins: Lists all device administrator applications for the current user. Use it to see which apps are managing the device.
MDMKit.adminManager.getDelegatedBundleNa: Lists which apps are allowed to use a given delegation policy. Use it to see which apps can access a policy.
MDMKit.adminManager.getDelegatedPolicies: Lists the policies a delegated app is allowed to access. Use it to check what a delegated app may manage.
MDMKit.adminManager.getEnterpriseInfo: Gets the enterprise information of a device administrator application. Use it to look up which company or organisation manages a device.
MDMKit.adminManager.getEnterpriseManaged: Gets the enterprise message tips. Use it to show the enterprise's own notice or tip text to the user.

MDMKit.securityManager.setDisallowedPerm: Disables a permission for all apps of a user, so they are denied when requesting or using it. Use to block high-risk permissions such as camera or microphone to prevent privacy leaks.
MDMKit.securityManager.setExternalSource: Sets the management policy for extensions from external sources, controlling whether they can run. Use to stop employees installing unauthorized browser extensions or to force enterprise-approved ones.
MDMKit.securityManager.setPasswordPolicy: Sets the screen lock password policy for the device, prompting users to reset passwords that do not meet requirements. Use to require strong passwords and periodic changes for enterprise security.

MDMKit.securityManager.setScreenLockDisa: Turns swipe-to-unlock on or off for the current user, so the screen either requires a swipe or goes straight to the home screen. Use it to simplify access on managed devices or to keep a basic lock-screen step.
MDMKit.securityManager.setScreenWatermar: Sets a watermark image that appears on the screen for all users. Use it to display an ownership or confidentiality mark across the device.
MDMKit.securityManager.setWatermarkImage: Sets a watermark image for a chosen app of a chosen user. Use it to mark a specific app's screen with an identifying image.
MDMKit.securityManager.uninstallEnterpri: Removes the enterprise app re-signing certificate, so apps signed with it stop running after the next restart. Use it when replacing or retiring an enterprise signing certificate.
MDMKit.securityManager.uninstallUserCert: Removes a user certificate from the device. Use it to replace an expired certificate or revoke an employee's access to enterprise resources.

MDMKit.systemManager.addKeyEventPolicies: Adds a policy so the management app is notified when a matching key event, such as a power or volume key press, occurs. Use it to watch for button presses like volume or power keys.

MDMKit.systemManager.getAutoUnlockAfterR: Checks whether the device unlocks automatically after a reboot. Use it to confirm whether the automatic unlock setting is on.
MDMKit.systemManager.getDisallowedNearLi: Gets the list of NearLink protocols that are blocked for a user. Use it to check which wireless connection types are restricted.
MDMKit.systemManager.getInstallLocalEnte: Checks whether installing enterprise apps locally is allowed on the device. Use it to confirm whether local enterprise app installation is turned on.

MDMKit.systemManager.getKeyEventPolicies: Obtains the current key event handling policy. Use it to check whether a key policy has been applied or to see the current configuration before changing it.
MDMKit.systemManager.getNTPServer: Obtains the NTP server address configured on the device. Use it to check whether time synchronization is set up correctly or to see the current server before changing it.
MDMKit.systemManager.getOtaUpdatePolicy: Checks the current OTA update policy of the device. Use it to verify whether an update policy was delivered correctly or to see the current policy before adjusting it.
MDMKit.systemManager.getUpdateAuthData: Obtains authentication data for verifying a system update package. Use it in intranet updates to check that an update package is valid and not malicious.
MDMKit.systemManager.getUpdateResult: Obtains the result of a system update for a given version. Use it to check whether an update succeeded and to handle update failures.
MDMKit.systemManager.isActivationLockDis: Checks whether the device activation lock is disabled. Use it to confirm the security setting before transferring or recycling a device.
MDMKit.systemManager.isOtaUpdateNonceEna: Checks whether nonce verification is enabled for OTA updates. Use it to confirm the security configuration of system updates on a device.
MDMKit.systemManager.notifyUpdatePackage: Tells the system about update packages for an intranet update. Use it to prepare a device for a system update before setting the update policy.
MDMKit.systemManager.removeDisallowedNea: Removes the list of disallowed NearLink protocols for a user, letting them use those protocols again. Use it to restore NearLink communication for a specific user.
MDMKit.systemManager.removeKeyEventPolic: Removes a key event handling policy so the system restores the default behavior for those keys. Use it to bring back normal key responses on a device.
MDMKit.systemManager.setActivationLockDi: Enables or disables the device activation lock; disabling it also turns off Find Device. Use it to manage whether a device can be activation-locked.
MDMKit.systemManager.setAutoUnlockAfterR: Sets whether the device unlocks automatically after a reboot, on devices without a screen lock password. Use it for unattended devices that must restart without manual unlocking.
MDMKit.systemManager.setInstallLocalEnte: Turns on or off whether users can install enterprise apps locally by double-tapping their installation packages. Use it to allow or block local installation of company apps on enterprise PCs and 2-in-1 devices.

MDMKit.systemManager.setNTPServer: Sets the time server used to synchronize the system clock. Use it to keep enterprise devices on the same accurate time, so logs and certificates stay valid.
MDMKit.systemManager.setOtaUpdateNonceEn: Turns the nonce check for system updates on or off. Use it to make the device verify update validity and block replay attacks during updates.
MDMKit.systemManager.setOtaUpdatePolicy: Sets the policy that controls how the system performs over-the-air updates. Use it to choose the update behavior for enterprise devices, including intranet updates.
MDMKit.systemManager.startCollectLog: Starts collecting fault logs already stored on the device's hard disk. Use it to gather device fault logs for troubleshooting.
MDMKit.telephonyManager.activeSim: Activates the SIM card in a chosen slot so it can be used for communication. Use it to activate a newly inserted SIM card without the user doing it manually.

MDMKit.telephonyManager.getOutgoingCallP: Gets the list of phone numbers set as the outgoing call trustlist or blocklist. Use it to review which numbers can be dialed or are blocked from being dialed.

MDMKit.telephonyManager.removeOutgoingCa: Removes numbers from the outgoing call trustlist or blocklist. Use it to lift call restrictions and let employees make calls again.
MDMKit.telephonyManager.setDefaultData: Sets the SIM card in a chosen slot as the default data SIM. Use it to pick which SIM provides internet access on a dual-SIM device.
MDMKit.telephonyManager.setSimDisabled: Disables the SIM card in a chosen slot so it cannot make calls, send messages, or use data. Use it to cut off phone service when a device is lost or an employee leaves.
MDMKit.telephonyManager.setSimEnabled: Turns on the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to switch a phone line back on for calls and mobile data.

MDMKit.usbManager.addDisallowedPermissiv: Blocks chosen types of USB devices, taking effect right away on plugged-in devices. Use it to stop a USB headset or other device from working immediately.
MDMKit.usbManager.addDisallowedUsbDevice: Blocks chosen types of USB devices. Use it to stop USB storage drives or other device types from being used and prevent data leaks.
MDMKit.usbManager.disableUsb: Turns USB on or off on the device. Use it to block or allow USB connections on a managed device.
MDMKit.usbManager.getAllowedUsbDevices: Lists the USB devices that are currently allowed. Use it to check which USB devices are permitted before changing the policy.
MDMKit.usbManager.getDisallowedPermissiv: Lists the USB device types that have been blocked. Use it to check which USB devices are currently not allowed.
MDMKit.usbManager.getDisallowedUsbDevice: Gets the list of USB device types that are currently blocked. Use it to review or display which USB devices are restricted on a managed device.
MDMKit.usbManager.getUsbStorageDeviceAcc: Gets the access policy for USB storage devices. Use it to check whether USB storage devices are allowed or blocked on a managed device.
MDMKit.usbManager.isUsbDisabled: Checks whether USB is currently disabled. Use it to see if USB access is blocked on the device.
MDMKit.usbManager.removeAllowedUsbDevice: Removes USB devices from the allowed list so they are no longer trusted. Use it to revoke access for specific USB devices in enterprise security management.
MDMKit.usbManager.removeDisallowedPermis: Removes USB device types from the disallowed list so they can be used normally again. Use it to lift restrictions on previously blocked USB device types.
MDMKit.usbManager.removeDisallowedUsbDev: Removes USB device types from the disallowed list. Use it to lift restrictions on blocked USB device types in enterprise security management.
MDMKit.usbManager.setUsbPolicy: Sets whether USB storage can be read and written or only read. Use it to restrict copying files to or from USB drives.
MDMKit.usbManager.setUsbStorageDeviceAcc: Sets the access policy for USB storage devices. Use it to allow or block USB storage devices on a managed device.
MDMKit.wifiManager.addAllowedWifiList: Adds Wi-Fi networks that the device is allowed to connect to, blocking all others. Use it to keep work devices on approved office Wi-Fi only.
MDMKit.wifiManager.addDisallowedWifiList: Adds Wi-Fi networks the device is forbidden to connect to. Use it to stop devices joining unsafe public Wi-Fi like cafe or airport hotspots.

MDMKit.wifiManager.getDisallowedWifiList: Lists the Wi-Fi networks the device is forbidden to connect to. Use it to check which blocked Wi-Fi networks are currently in force.
MDMKit.wifiManager.isWifiActive: Checks whether Wi-Fi is turned on. Use it to see if the device's Wi-Fi is enabled.
MDMKit.wifiManager.isWifiActiveSync: Tells whether Wi-Fi is currently switched on for the device. Use it to check if Wi-Fi is on before changing network settings.
MDMKit.wifiManager.isWifiDisabled: Checks whether Wi-Fi is turned off on the device. Use it to see if Wi-Fi is disabled before changing network settings.
MDMKit.wifiManager.removeAllowedWifiList: Removes Wi-Fi networks from the allowed list, so the device may connect to others again. Use it to lift old Wi-Fi restrictions after an office network change.
MDMKit.wifiManager.removeDisallowedWifiL: Removes Wi-Fi networks from the disallowed list so the device can connect to them again. Use it to lift restrictions on a specific Wi-Fi network or allow employees onto newly approved office networks.
MDMKit.wifiManager.setWifiDisabled: Turns Wi-Fi off or on for the device. Use it to disable Wi-Fi to enforce a no-wireless policy.
MDMKit.wifiManager.setWifiProfile: Sets up Wi-Fi so the device connects to a chosen network. Use it to join the device to a specific Wi-Fi network.
MDMKit.wifiManager.setWifiProfileSync: Configures the device to connect to a specified Wi-Fi network using its SSID, key, and security type. Use it to set up which Wi-Fi network the device joins.
MDMKit.wifiManager.turnOffWifi: Turns Wi-Fi off on the device. Use it to disable Wi-Fi, for example to enforce an enterprise policy that keeps devices off wireless networks.
MDMKit.wifiManager.turnOnWifi: Turns Wi-Fi on, optionally forcing it on so it cannot be switched off manually. Use it to remotely enable Wi-Fi on employee devices or when enforcing a policy.

MechanicKit.mechanicManager.isSupportAct: Checks whether a mechanical device supports a given action type. Use it to confirm a mechanical part can perform the action you want before trying it.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.move: Moves a mechanical device using the given parameters. Use it to drive a connected mechanical device to a position.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.moveBySpeed: Moves a mechanical device at a set speed for a set time. Use it to drive a connected mechanical device at a chosen speed.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.off: Stops listening for device attachment state changes. Use it when you no longer need to know when a device is attached or removed.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.offAttachSta: Stops listening for device attachment state changes. Use it to stop being notified when a device is attached or removed.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.offRotationA: Stops listening for changes in the state of a rotation axis. Use it to stop being notified when a rotation axis changes.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.offTrackingS: Stops listening for tracking events. Use it when you no longer need updates on tracking.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.on: Registers a listener for rotation axis state changes. Use it to keep track of a mechanical device's moving axis.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.onAttachStat: Subscribes to events when a connected mechanical device is attached or detached. Use it to know when a mechanical device is connected or removed.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.onRotationAx: Listens for changes in the state of a rotation axis. Use it to be notified when a rotation axis changes.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.onTrackingSt: Watches for tracking events from a connected mechanical device. Use it to react when the device starts or stops tracking something.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.rotate: Rotates a mechanical device to relative angles over a set time. Use it to turn a connected mechanical device by an angle.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.rotateBySpee: Rotates a mechanical device at a set speed for a set time. Use it to spin a connected mechanical device at a chosen speed.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.rotateToEule: Rotates a mechanical device to exact angles over a set time. Use it to aim or turn a connected device to a chosen position.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.searchTarget: Searches for a specified target using given search parameters. Use it to find and locate a target with a connected device.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.setCameraTra: Turns camera tracking on or off for a connected mechanical device. Use it to start or stop the device following a subject with its camera.

MechanicKit.mechanicManager.setUserOpera: Sets a user operation for a device by its address. Use it to send a chosen operation to a connected device.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.stopMoving: Stops a mechanical device from moving. Use it to halt a connected device that is currently in motion.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.subscribe: Subscribes to specified events from mechanical devices. Use it to be notified when a connected device reports an event.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.turnBySpeed: Rotates a connected mechanical device in place at a given angular speed for a set time. Use it to spin a motorized device, such as turning a rotating stand or turntable.
MechanicKit.mechanicManager.unSubscribe: Stops receiving the specified events from a connected mechanical device. Use it to stop listening for device updates you no longer need.

MediaKit.AVAdsController.skipCurrentAdsM: Skips the ad content that is currently playing. Use it to jump past an ad and get back to the main content.

MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.getTaskProg: Tells how far along a download is, as a number from 0 to 1. Use it to show a download progress bar.

MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.onStatusCha: Watches for changes in the status of offline download tasks. Use it to keep track of whether a download is running, paused, or finished.

MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.release: Releases the resources used by the download manager. Use it when you are done downloading to free up memory.
MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.removeDownl: Removes a download task from the offline download manager. Use it to delete a download you no longer need.
MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.resumeDownl: Resumes the offline download of a specified task. Use it to continue a download that was paused.
MediaKit.AVDownloaderManager.setRequestT: Sets the network timeout for HTTP requests during downloads. Use it to control how long to wait before a download fails.

MediaKit.AVMetadataExtractor.setUrlSourc: Sets a network media file as the source for reading its metadata and thumbnails. Use it to look up details or grab a preview image from an online video or song.

MediaKit.AVPlayer.forceLoadVideo: Sets whether the video should be forcibly loaded during playback. Use it to make a video load even when it normally would not.

MediaKit.AVPlayer.getCurrentPresentation: Gives the current playback time in microseconds while playing, paused, or finished. Use it to show how far into a song or video you are.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getCurrentTrack: Gives the index of the selected track for a given media type. Use it to find which audio or video track is currently playing.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getLoadedTimeRanges: Gets the time ranges of the media that have finished loading, given as start and end positions in milliseconds. Use it to show how much of a song or video is buffered before playing.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getMediaKeySystemInfos: Gets the media key system details, such as UUID and PSSH, for the media being played. Use it to set up protected playback of a song or video.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getMediaSources: Returns the list of media sources in the playlist. Use it to see which songs or videos are queued up for playback.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getPlaybackInfo: Gets information about the current playback. Use it to check details of the song or video that is playing.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getPlaybackPosition: Gets the current playback position in milliseconds. Use it to show how far into a song or video playback has reached.

MediaKit.AVPlayer.getPlaybackStatisticMe: Gets statistics about the current playback, such as how much has been played. Use it to show playback stats while a song or video is playing, paused, or finished.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getSeekableTimeRanges: Gets the time ranges you can jump to in the current media, given as start and end positions in milliseconds. Use it to know where you can skip to while playing a song or video.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getSelectedTracks: Gets the indexes of the audio or video tracks currently selected. Use it to see which audio or video track is playing.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getTrackDescription: Gets information about the audio and video tracks in the media. Use it to list the available audio or video tracks while playing a song or video.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.getTrackSelectionFilte: Gets the track selection filter currently set for the player. Use it to check which tracks the player is set to pick while playing media.
MediaKit.AVPlayer.isSeekContinuousSuppor: Checks whether the media can be seeked continuously. Use it to find out if smooth skipping through a song or video is possible.

MediaKit.AVPlayer.offAmplitudeUpdate: Stops listening for changes in the maximum audio amplitude. Use it to stop being notified about how loud the sound gets while playing audio.

MediaLibraryKit.Album.getFaceId: Gets the face identifier shown on the cover of a portrait or group photo album. Use it to find which person's face represents an album.
MediaLibraryKit.Album.getFusionAssetsInf: Gets information about the combined assets in an album. Use it to see details of merged photos or videos in an album.
MediaLibraryKit.Album.getSelectedAssets: Gets the portrait album photos or videos that match your filter, up to a set limit. Use it to pick out selected pictures from a portrait album.
MediaLibraryKit.Album.recoverAssets: Restores photos or videos from the trash back into the album. Use it to bring back pictures or clips you deleted by mistake.
MediaLibraryKit.Album.removeAssets: Takes pictures and videos out of one of your albums. Use it to tidy an album by deleting chosen photos or clips from it.
MediaLibraryKit.Album.setCoverUri: Sets the cover image of a user album using a file URI. Use it to choose which photo appears as the album cover.
MediaLibraryKit.AnalysisAlbum.getOrderPo: Gets the position order of given photos within an analysis album. Use it to find where each photo sits in the album's sequence.
MediaLibraryKit.AnalysisAlbum.getRelatio: Gets the relationship of a person shown in a portrait album. Use it to find how that person is related, such as family or friend.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.cancelA: Cancels all cloud enhancement tasks. Use it to stop every pending AI photo enhancement job at once.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.cancelC: Cancels cloud enhancement tasks for the given photos. Use it to stop AI enhancement for selected photos.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.getClou: Gets a cloud enhancement instance for the current ability context. Use it to start managing AI-powered cloud photo enhancement tasks.
Gets the AI-enhanced version of a photo after cloud enhancement. Use it to view or save the improved copy of a picture.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.priorit: Moves a photo's cloud enhancement task to the front of the queue. Use it to get a chosen photo enhanced sooner.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.queryCl: Checks the status of a photo's cloud enhancement task. Use it to see whether a photo's enhancement is still pending or finished.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.submitC: Starts cloud enhancement tasks for photos, optionally adding a watermark to the results. Use it to enhance pictures with AI in the cloud.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudEnhancement.syncClo: Refreshes the status of cloud enhancement tasks. Use it to update the progress shown for photos being enhanced in the cloud.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.c: Stops an in-progress download of media stored in the cloud. Use it to cancel downloading cloud photos or videos.
Cancels a batch download for the specified cloud media assets. Use it to stop downloading chosen photos or videos from the cloud.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.g: Obtains a CloudMediaAssetManager instance. Use it to start managing downloads of cloud media assets.
Obtains the status of a task that downloads cloud media assets. Use it to check how a cloud media download is going.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.o: Unregisters a callback that monitors changes in the progress of a batch download for cloud media assets. Use it to stop watching download progress.

Pauses the download of chosen cloud photos and videos. Use it to stop downloading pictures or videos for now.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.q: Shows the details of a batch download of cloud photos and videos. Use it to check how a download of pictures or videos is going.

MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.r: Continues a paused download of chosen cloud photos and videos. Use it to carry on downloading pictures or videos that were stopped.
Deletes the local copy and details of cloud photos and videos. Use it to free up space by removing downloaded pictures or videos from the device.
MediaLibraryKit.CloudMediaAssetManager.s: Begins or continues downloading cloud photos and videos. Use it to download pictures or videos stored in the cloud.
Starts downloading a batch of cloud-stored photos and videos at original quality. Use it to save chosen cloud pictures or videos onto the device.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.close: Releases a set of found files so it can no longer be used. Use it to free up a search result once you are done looking through your photos and videos.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.contains: Tells you whether a particular photo or video is part of a set of found files. Use it to check if a certain picture or clip turned up in your search.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getAllObject: Gives you every photo and video in a set of found files. Use it to grab all the pictures and clips from a search at once.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getCount: Counts how many files are in a set of found photos and videos. Use it to see how many pictures or clips your search turned up.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getFirstObje: Gives you the first photo or video in a set of found files. Use it to grab the top picture or clip from a search.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getIndex: Finds the position of a given file in a set of results, returning -1 if it is not there. Use it to tell where a photo or video sits in a list.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getLastObjec: Gets the last file in a set of results. Use it to jump to the final photo or video in a list.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getNextObjec: Gets the next file in a set of results. Use it to step through photos or videos one by one.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getObjectByP: Gets the file at a given position in a set of results, counting from zero. Use it to open a specific photo or video by its place in a list.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getObjectsBy: Gets several files at once from a set of results by their positions. Use it to load a chosen group of photos or videos together.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.getRangeObje: Gets a chosen number of file assets starting from a given position in a result set. Use it to page through search or album results a few files at a time.
MediaLibraryKit.FetchResult.isAfterLast: Checks whether the cursor has reached the last row of a set of results. Use it to know when you have gone through all photos or videos.
MediaLibraryKit.HighlightAlbum.deleteHig: Deletes highlight albums, the automatically made collections of memorable photos and videos. Use it to remove a memories album you no longer want.
MediaLibraryKit.HighlightAlbum.getHighli: Gets specific information about a highlight album, such as details of the memories collection. Use it to show or check details of an automatically created memories album.
Gets the cached data for a chosen asset in a highlight album. Use it to load a photo or video from a memories album for display.
MediaLibraryKit.HighlightAlbum.setHighli: Sets user behaviour data for a highlight album. Use it to record how someone interacts with a memories album.
MediaLibraryKit.HighlightAlbum.setSubTit: Sets the subtitle text for a Highlights album of memorable photos or videos. Use it to give a Highlights album a short descriptive caption.
MediaLibraryKit.KnowledgeContent.getRela: Finds entities related to a search topic, such as smart labels. Use it to look up things connected to a topic you are searching for.
MediaLibraryKit.KnowledgeContent.getSear: Gets suggested search words for the given suggestion types. Use it to offer recommended search terms as someone types a query.

Sets the relationship label for a person in a portrait album, such as mother, friend, or colleague. Use it to label who someone is in your people albums.

Permanently deletes images or videos in batches, up to 500 at a time. Use it to erase photos or videos from the device for good.
Permanently deletes images or videos in batches by their URIs, up to 500 at a time. Use it to erase photos or videos from the device for good.
Deletes local images or videos to the trash in batches, up to 500 at a time. Use it to move photos or videos to the trash so they can be recovered.

Saves edited data for a media asset. Use it to keep changes made to a photo or video.

Saves the version of a moving photo, which decides what special effects it supports. Use it when saving a motion picture so the right effects work.
Sets the rotation angle of an image to 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. Use it to fix a photo that appears sideways.
Sets which watermark type a photo supports. Use it to choose the watermark applied to a photo.
Sets the title of a media asset. Use it to give a photo or video a name.

Sets the video enhancement type for a video asset. Use it to apply an enhancement to a video in the gallery.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetDataHandler.on: Called when a requested media asset is ready, providing the image or video data. Use it to receive a photo or video after requesting it.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetManager.cancel: Cancels a media asset request whose callback has not yet been triggered. Use it to stop waiting for a photo or video you no longer need.

MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetManager.quickR: Quickly requests an image and returns it through a handler when ready. Use it to show a picture fast, such as a thumbnail or preview.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetManager.reques: Requests an image and returns it through a handler when ready. Use it to load and display a picture from the media library.

Requests a moving photo object that can provide its asset data. Use it to get and work with a moving photo from the media library.
Requests a video and saves it to a chosen sandbox folder, reporting success through a handler. Use it to download a video into your app's files.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetProgressHandle: Reports how far along a video's processing has got, as a percentage from 0 to 100. Use it to show a progress bar while a video is being prepared.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaAssetsChangeRequest: Marks a file as a favorite or removes it from favorites. Use it to favorite or unfavorite photos and videos in the gallery.

Sets the user comment text on a media asset. Use it to add or change a note or caption on a photo or video.
MediaLibraryKit.MediaHighlightAlbumChang: Sets a chosen attribute value in a highlights album, such as whether it has been viewed or favorited. Use it to mark a highlight album as seen or as a favorite.

MediaLibraryKit.MovingPhoto.requestConte: Fetches the image and video parts of a moving photo and saves them to the given locations. Use it to export or save a moving photo's picture and clip.
MediaLibraryKit.MovingPhotoViewAttribute: Turns automatic playing of a moving photo on or off; when on, it starts playing once loaded. Use it to make a moving photo play by itself.

Runs when moving photo playback fails. Use it to handle a photo or video that cannot play.
Runs when the moving photo video finishes playing. Use it to react when playback reaches the end.
Runs when moving photo video playback is paused. Use it to react when the video stops partway through.

Runs when a moving photo stops playing. Use it to react when playback of the moving photo ends.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.acquir: Starts a backup of the media library database and returns backup details, working only on beta devices. Use it to collect database backup information for troubleshooting on a beta device.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.applyC: Applies requested changes to photos or albums. Use it to save edits or updates made to a photo or album.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.batchG: Gets the values of chosen properties for many photos or videos at once. Use it to read details like size or date for a group of files in one go.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.canPer: Tells you whether deep storage space optimization can be started. Use it to check before freeing up space taken by photos and videos.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.cancel: Stops a running intelligent analysis tool. Use it to cancel an analysis task you no longer need.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.checkP: Checks whether photos exist and whether you can read them. Use it to find out which photos you are allowed to open.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.cloneA: Copies files from a file path into an album. Use it to add photos or videos from file storage into an album.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.cloneT: Copies photos or videos into an album. Use it to add existing media files to an album.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.conver: Converts photo or video items into a compatible form. Use it when an app needs photos or videos in a format it can handle.
Turns a file manager path into a photo or video item. Use it to open or work with a picture or video by its file path.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.create: Creates a new photo album with the given name. Use it to make a new album to organize pictures and videos.

Shows a dialog to delete chosen photos or videos, moving them to the trash. Use it to let someone remove pictures or videos from their gallery.
Creates a new image or video file of a given type and extension. Use it to save a picture or video into the gallery.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.delete: Deletes user albums. Use it to remove photo albums you no longer want.
Deletes media files, moving them to the trash. Use it to remove photos or videos from the gallery.

Gets albums of a chosen type and subtype from the photo library. Use it to list someone's photo albums so they can browse or open them.
Gets album information for a list of album IDs. Use it to look up details of several photo albums at once.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getAss: Checks whether an app needs compatibility conversion when it gets a file, based on the app's bundle name. Use it to find out if a photo or video must be converted before an app can open it.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getBur: Gets the burst photos that belong to one burst group. Use it to show all shots taken in a single burst so the user can pick the best one.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getClo: Gives the current addresses of cloned albums from the old addresses on a previous device. Use it to find where your albums ended up after moving to a new phone.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getDat: Reports how far along the analysis of your photos and videos is, as a JSON string. Use it to check the progress of scanning your gallery.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getDee: Gives the size in bytes of the deep storage space that can be freed. Use it to see how much space deep cleaning your photos and videos could free up.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getHid: Gets the hidden photo albums for a chosen display mode. Use it to find albums you have hidden from the main gallery.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getInd: Reports how far the photo and video indexing has gotten, as counts of analyzed and total items. Use it to check progress while the gallery builds its search index.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getPho: Gets the sorting order used for system, user, and source albums, in phone or PC style. Use it to see how albums are arranged in the gallery.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getRec: Gets details about the most recent photo or video. Use it to show a recent picture or clip in a recent-photos view.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getSha: Gets the photo assets that have been shared with you. Use it to view or work with photos others have shared.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.getSup: Gets the image or video file name extensions the media library supports. Use it to check which photo or video file types can be saved or opened.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.isComp: Checks whether a temporary JPEG copy should be made for an app. Use it to decide if an app needs a JPEG copy of a photo.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.isMedi: Checks whether the specified media data, such as an asset's added date, is ready. Use it to confirm a photo's details are available before showing them.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.modify: Changes the default cover order of albums. Use it to control which photo appears as an album's cover.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.moveAs: Moves files from the file manager into an album. Use it to add photos or videos from folders into an album.
Moves photos or videos from the media library into a file manager directory. Use it to export media out of the gallery into a folder.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.off: Stops listening for changes to photos and videos, including hidden or trashed ones. Use it to stop being notified when photos are added, changed, or moved to the trash.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.offAna: Stops listening for changes to smart analysis albums, either one listener or all of them. Use it to stop being notified when smart albums change.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.offMed: Stops listening for changes in whether the photo library is available. Use it to stop being notified when the photo library becomes available or unavailable.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.offhid: Stops listening for changes to hidden albums. Use it to stop being notified when hidden albums change.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.onAnal: Listens for changes to the smart analysis album and reports them. Use it to be notified when the smart analysis album changes.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.onHidd: Watches for changes to hidden albums and reports them when they happen. Use it to keep an app's list of hidden albums up to date.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.onMedi: Watches whether the photo library is available and reports when that changes. Use it to know when the photo library can be used again, for example after it becomes unavailable.
MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.onPhot: Watches for changes to photo albums and reports them. Use it to refresh an album list when albums are added, renamed, or removed.

MediaLibraryKit.PhotoAccessHelper.regist: Watches a photo, album, or all photos for changes and reports them back. Use it to keep a gallery view up to date when pictures are added, edited, or removed.

NetworkKit.TCPSocket.on: Listens for connection or close events on a TCP connection. Use it to react when the connection opens or closes.

NetworkKit.TCPSocketConnection.on: Listens for error events on a TCP socket connection. Use it to be notified when a network connection has a problem.
NetworkKit.TCPSocketConnection.send: Sends data over a TCP server connection to a client. Use it to send a message to the connected client.

NetworkKit.TCPSocketServer.getSocketFd: Gets the file descriptor of the server socket. Use it when you need the underlying socket handle for low-level operations.

NetworkKit.TCPSocketServer.on: Listens for connect events on a TCP server connection. Use it to react when a client connects to your server.
NetworkKit.TCPSocketServer.setExtraOptio: Sets extra attributes on a TCP server connection. Use it to tune how the server socket behaves.

NetworkKit.TLSSocket.close: Closes a secure socket connection. Use it to end a secure connection when you are done.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.connect: Sets up a secure connection to a given IP address and port over TCP. Use it to open a secure link to a server.

NetworkKit.TLSSocket.getLocalAddress: Gets the local address of a secure connection. Use it to find out which address and port your side of the connection is using.

NetworkKit.TLSSocket.getSocketFd: Gets the file descriptor of a secure socket connection. Use it when you need the underlying socket handle for a secure connection.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.getState: Gets the status of a secure socket connection. Use it to check whether a secure connection is open, closed, or otherwise.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.off: Stops listening for error events on a secure socket connection. Use it to stop being notified when a secure connection has an error.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.on: Listens for error events on a secure socket connection. Use it to be notified when a secure connection has an error.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.send: Sends data over a secure socket connection. Use it to send text or binary data through a secure connection.
NetworkKit.TLSSocket.setExtraOptions: Sets extra attributes of a secure socket connection. Use it to adjust options on a secure connection.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.close: Closes a secure client connection. Use it to end a secure session when you are done talking to a server.

NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.getLocalA: Gets the local address of a secure server connection. Use it to find out which local address a secure connection is using.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.getRemote: Gets the address of the other end of a secure server connection. Use it to find out which peer a secure connection is talking to.

NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.getSocket: Gets the file descriptor of a secure socket connection. Use it to identify or manage the underlying connection in low-level networking tasks.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.off: Stops listening for error events on a secure socket connection. Use it to remove an error handler you no longer need.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.on: Listens for error events on a secure socket connection. Use it to be notified when something goes wrong with the connection.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketConnection.send: Sends text or binary data over a secure socket connection to the client. Use it to transmit messages or files to a connected client.

NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.getProtocol: Tells which secure connection protocol version was agreed for the current connection. Use it to check how a connection is secured.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.getSocketFd: Gets the file descriptor of the secure server socket. Use it to identify or manage the underlying socket.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.getState: Gets the current status of a secure server connection. Use it to check whether the connection is open, closed, or connecting.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.listen: Binds an address and port and waits for secure client connections, accepting them as they arrive. Use it to start a secure server that clients can connect to.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.off: Stops listening for error events on a secure server connection. Use it to stop being notified when connection errors happen.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.on: Listens for connect events on a secure server connection. Use it to react when a client connects to your server.
NetworkKit.TLSSocketServer.setExtraOptio: Sets extra attributes for a secure server connection. Use it to tune how the server socket behaves.

NetworkKit.UDPSocket.on: Starts listening for error or close events on a UDP connection. Use it to be notified when the connection fails or closes.

NetworkKit.UDPSocket.setExtraOptions: Sets extra attributes for a UDP connection. Use it to adjust how the connection behaves before sending or receiving data.

NetworkKit.WebSocket.onOpen: Listens for a WebSocket connection opening. Use it to know when a live connection is ready to send and receive.

NetworkKit.WebSocket.send: Sends data over a WebSocket connection. Use it to send messages or binary data to the other side.
NetworkKit.WebSocketServer.close: Closes a given WebSocket connection. Use it to end a specific client's connection.

NetworkKit.WebSocketServer.off: Stops listening for WebSocket server error events. Use it to stop handling server errors.

NetworkKit.WebSocketServer.stop: Stops the WebSocket server from listening. Use it to shut down your server and stop accepting client connections.
