NetworkKit.policy.restoreAllPolicies: Resets the network management policy for a specified SIM card. Use it to undo custom network rules for that SIM.
NetworkKit.policy.setBackgroundAllowed: Controls whether apps are allowed to use mobile data while running in the background. Use it to stop background apps from using data.
NetworkKit.policy.setDeviceIdleTrustlist: Sets which apps may still access the internet while the device is hibernating. Use it to keep chosen apps online during sleep mode.
NetworkKit.policy.setNetQuotaPolicies: Sets data quota limits for metered networks. Use it to cap how much data can be used before limits apply.
NetworkKit.policy.setNetworkAccessPolicy: Sets whether a chosen app is allowed to access the network. Use it to block or allow internet access for a specific app.
NetworkKit.policy.setPolicyByUid: Sets the network policy for a specific app. Use it to control how an app is allowed to use the network.
NetworkKit.policy.setPowerSaveTrustlist: Sets which apps may still use the Internet while power saving mode is on. Use it to keep chosen apps online when the battery is low.
NetworkKit.policy.showAppNetPolicySettin: Opens the app's network settings screen so the network connection method can be configured. Use it to let someone change how the app connects to the network.
NetworkKit.policy.updateRemindPolicy: Updates the policy for when a data quota reaches its upper limit. Use it to change the reminder shown when mobile data runs out.
NetworkKit.sharing.getSharableRegexes: Gets the patterns that describe which network interfaces can be shared. Use it to find out what connections can be shared with others.
NetworkKit.sharing.getSharingIfaces: Gets the names of network interfaces in a given sharing state. Use it to see which connections are currently being shared.
NetworkKit.sharing.getSharingState: Gets the network sharing state for a type of connection. Use it to check whether sharing is on, off, or busy.
NetworkKit.sharing.getStatsRxBytes: Tells how many bytes have been downloaded through the shared network connection. Use it to check how much data the hotspot has received.
NetworkKit.sharing.getStatsTotalBytes: Tells the total number of bytes sent and received through the shared network connection. Use it to see the overall data used by the hotspot.
NetworkKit.sharing.getStatsTxBytes: Tells how many bytes have been uploaded through the shared network connection. Use it to check how much data the hotspot has sent.
NetworkKit.sharing.isSharing: Tells whether network sharing is currently turned on. Use it to check if the hotspot is active.
NetworkKit.sharing.isSharingSupported: Tells whether this device can share its network connection. Use it to check if a hotspot can be turned on.
NetworkKit.sharing.off: Stops listening for changes to the network sharing state. Use it to stop being notified when the hotspot turns on or off.
NetworkKit.sharing.on: Registers a callback that fires when network sharing turns on or off. Use it to keep your app informed about whether the device is sharing its connection.
NetworkKit.sharing.startSharing: Starts sharing the device's network connection for a chosen interface type. Use it to turn on tethering so other devices can get online.
NetworkKit.sharing.stopSharing: Stops sharing the device's network connection for a chosen interface type. Use it to turn off tethering when you no longer want other devices using your connection.
NetworkKit.socket.constructLocalSocketIn: Creates a local socket object for communication between processes on the same device. Use it to set up local inter-process data exchange.
NetworkKit.socket.constructLocalSocketSe: Creates a local socket server object that listens for local connections. Use it to accept connections from local clients on the same device.
NetworkKit.socket.constructMulticastSock: Creates a multicast socket object for sending and receiving data to a group of devices at once. Use it for group messaging or streaming to multiple receivers.
NetworkKit.socket.constructTCPSocketInst: Creates a TCP socket object for reliable network connections. Use it to connect to a server and exchange data over the internet.
NetworkKit.socket.constructTCPSocketServ: Creates a TCP socket server object that accepts incoming network connections. Use it to host a service that clients can connect to.
NetworkKit.socket.constructTLSSocketInst: Creates a secure TLS socket object for encrypted network connections. Use it to send and receive data safely over the internet.
NetworkKit.socket.constructTLSSocketServ: Creates a secure TLS socket server. Use it to accept encrypted connections from clients.
NetworkKit.socket.constructUDPSocketInst: Creates a UDP socket. Use it to send and receive datagrams over the network.
NetworkKit.statistics.getAllRxBytes: Reports the total data received through all network interfaces. Use it to check how much data has been downloaded.
NetworkKit.statistics.getAllTxBytes: Reports the total data sent through all network interfaces. Use it to check how much data has been uploaded.
NetworkKit.statistics.getCellularRxBytes: Reports the data received over the cellular network. Use it to check mobile data usage for downloads.
NetworkKit.statistics.getCellularTxBytes: Reports the data sent over the cellular network. Use it to check mobile data usage for uploads.
NetworkKit.statistics.getIfaceRxBytes: Tells you how many bytes of data a chosen network interface has received. Use it to check download traffic on a network card.
NetworkKit.statistics.getIfaceTxBytes: Tells you how many bytes of data a chosen network interface has sent. Use it to check upload traffic on a network card.
NetworkKit.statistics.getMonthTrafficSta: Gets this month's cellular data usage for a given SIM card. Use it to show how much mobile data has been used this month.
NetworkKit.statistics.getSelfTrafficStat: Shows how much data your app used on a chosen network over a chosen time period. Use it to see your app's data usage.
NetworkKit.statistics.getSockfdRxBytes: Tells you how many bytes a chosen socket has received. Use it to check download traffic on one connection.
NetworkKit.statistics.getSockfdTxBytes: Tells you how many bytes a chosen socket has sent. Use it to check upload traffic on one connection.
NetworkKit.statistics.getTrafficStatsByI: Gets traffic usage details for a network interface over a chosen time period. Use it to see how much data a particular connection has used.
NetworkKit.statistics.getTrafficStatsByN: Gets per-app traffic usage for a specified network over a chosen time period. Use it to see which apps used data on that network.
NetworkKit.statistics.getTrafficStatsByU: Gets how much data an app used over a chosen time period. Use it to check an app's data usage.
Gets the history of an app's data usage on a chosen network over a time period. Use it to see how much data an app used on a specific network.
NetworkKit.statistics.getUidRxBytes: Tells you how many bytes a chosen app has received. Use it to check an app's download traffic.
NetworkKit.statistics.getUidTxBytes: Finds out how much data an app has sent over the network. Use it to check an app's upload usage.
NetworkKit.statistics.off: Stops receiving updates about network traffic changes. Use it to stop being told when data usage changes.
NetworkKit.statistics.offNetStatsChange: Stops receiving updates about network traffic changes. Use it to stop being told when data usage changes.
NetworkKit.statistics.on: Starts sending updates when network traffic changes. Use it to be told when data usage changes.
NetworkKit.statistics.onNetStatsChange: Starts sending updates when network traffic changes. Use it to be told when data usage changes.
NetworkKit.statistics.setCalibrationTraf: Sets the remaining and total traffic data for a SIM card so the reported usage matches reality. Use it to correct a phone's data counter after a plan change or reset.
NetworkKit.statistics.updateIfacesStats: Updates the traffic statistics recorded for a network interface over a given time range. Use it to refresh the data usage numbers shown for a connection.
NetworkKit.statistics.updateStatsData: Refreshes the stored network traffic statistics. Use it to bring a device's data usage figures up to date.
NetworkKit.vpn.addSysVpnConfig: Adds a system VPN network configuration. Use it to set up a VPN connection profile on the device.
NetworkKit.vpn.createVpnConnection: Creates a VPN connection using the app's context. Use it to start a VPN session for secure browsing or private network access.
NetworkKit.vpn.deleteSysVpnConfig: Deletes a system VPN network configuration by its ID. Use it to remove a saved VPN profile from the device.
NetworkKit.vpn.getConnectedSysVpnConfig: Gets the configuration of the VPN network that is currently connected. Use it to check the settings of the VPN you are connected to.
NetworkKit.vpn.getConnectedVpnAppInfo: Gets information about the apps connected through VPN. Use it to see which apps are using the VPN connection.
NetworkKit.vpn.getSysVpnConfig: Gets the configuration of a system VPN network by its ID. Use it to look up the settings of a specific VPN.
NetworkKit.vpn.getSysVpnConfigList: Gets the configuration of all system VPN networks. Use it to list every VPN set up on the device.
NetworkKit.vpn.off: Stops listening for changes in the VPN connection state. Use it to stop being notified when the VPN connects or disconnects.
NetworkKit.vpn.on: Starts listening for changes in the VPN connection state. Use it to be notified when the VPN connects or disconnects.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.createVpnConnect: Sets up a VPN connection for an app. Use it to build a secure private network link.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.createVpnObserve: Creates an observer for VPN events. Use it to watch VPN status changes.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.isAlwaysOnVpnEna: Checks whether always-on VPN mode is turned on for an app. Use it to see if a VPN stays connected automatically.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.setAlwaysOnVpnEn: Turns always-on VPN mode on or off for an app. Use it to keep a VPN connected automatically.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.startVpnExtensio: Starts a VPN extension service. Use it to turn on a VPN connection.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.stopVpnExtension: Stops a VPN extension service. Use it to turn off a VPN connection.
NetworkKit.vpnExtension.updateVpnAuthori: Updates the authorization information for a VPN dialog. Use it to refresh whether a VPN is allowed.
NetworkKit.webSocket.createWebSocket: Creates a web socket connection. Use it to open a live two-way link with a server.
NetworkKit.webSocket.createWebSocketServ: Creates a web socket server. Use it to let apps or devices connect and exchange live messages over a network.
NotificationKit.Notification.show: Displays a notification. Use it to alert the user with a message on their device.
NotificationKit.NotificationSubscriberEx: Called when notifications are canceled. Use it to react when a user dismisses or clears notifications.
Called when the notification subscription extension is destroyed. Use it to clean up when notification listening stops.
Called when a notification is received. Use it to handle incoming notifications in a subscriber extension.
NotificationKit.notificationExtensionSub: Gets all apps that can subscribe to notifications. Use it to list which apps may read your notifications.
Obtains the subscription information about the notification extension of this application. Use it to check which notification subscriptions are active.
Gets the apps allowed to access device notifications for the current app. Use it to see which apps the user has granted notification access to.
Checks whether an app is allowed to access notifications on this device. Use it to see if an app can read your notifications.
Checks whether the Allow access to notifications on this device switch is turned on. Use it to find out if the user has allowed notification access on this device.
Opens the notification extension subscription settings screen in a semi-modal dialog. Use it to let the user turn on notification access and grant it to chosen apps.

Opens the notification extension subscription settings screen in a semi-modal dialog and returns the user's authorization result when it closes. Use it to let the user turn on notification access and see what they chose.
Turns notification access on or off for an app on this device. Use it to allow or block an app from reading your notifications.
Turns the 'Allow access to notifications on this device' switch on or off for a chosen app. Use it to let or stop an app showing its notifications on this device.
Subscribes to the notification extension, after getting the Bluetooth device's unique address. Use it to receive notifications forwarded from a paired Bluetooth device.
Unsubscribes from the notification extension. Use it to stop receiving notifications forwarded from a Bluetooth device.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.addD: Adds a Do Not Disturb profile for a chosen user. Use it to set up quiet hours so notifications stay silent.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.addS: Creates a notification slot that sets how alerts for a type of notification behave, such as sound, vibration, or banner. Use it to control how your app's notifications alert the user before publishing them.
Adds a set of notification slots. Use it to create the channels an app uses to post its notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.canc: Cancels a published notification by its ID and label, removing it from the notification center and status bar. Use it to dismiss a specific notification the user no longer needs.
Removes all notifications of your app from the notification center and status bar so the user no longer sees them. Use it when the app exits or the user clears all notifications.
Cancels a notification that was posted through the reminder agent. Use it to clear a reminder notification that is no longer needed.
Removes all notifications belonging to one named notification group of your app from the notification center. Use it to clear a batch of related notifications at once, grouped by service.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.disa: Blocks listed apps from posting notifications by adding their bundle names to a control list. Use it to stop chosen apps from sending you notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.disp: Sets whether the notification badge (the dot with a count) shows for a chosen app. Use it to turn the app icon's notification dot on or off.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getA: Finds the live notification that matches given filter criteria. Use it to look up a specific ongoing notification, such as a live view, by its details.
Tells you how many active notifications your app currently has in the notification center. Use it to show an unread notification count.
Gives the list of your app's active notifications with details like ID, tag, content, and creation time. Use it to look up or list the notifications your app has posted.
Gets every notification that is currently active. Use it to list all notifications showing on the device right now.
Lists the apps allowed to publish notifications for a user. Use it to see which apps can send you notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getB: Checks whether app badges are shown for several apps at once. Use it to find out if an app's icon shows a notification badge.
Tells you the badge number shown on your app's desktop icon. Use it to read the current unread count displayed on the app icon.
Gets the priority setting of an app's notifications. Use it to check how important an app's notifications are ranked.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getD: Gets the current notification reminder type of the device. Use it to check how the device alerts you for notifications, such as by sound or vibration.
Gets the device types that have cross-device notifications turned on. Use it to see which of your other devices can receive your notifications.
Gets the Do Not Disturb time set for a user. Use it to check when notifications are silenced for that user.
Looks up the Do Not Disturb profile with the given ID. Use it to check the Do Not Disturb settings a profile defines.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getN: Gets information about the wantAgent field of a notification, identified by its notification ID. Use it to look up details of a notification you sent, such as where it leads when tapped.

Gets the app's notification settings, including switches for lock screen notifications, banners, desktop badges, vibration, and ringtone. Use it to check whether notifications can show on the lock screen, pop up as banners, or make a sound.
Gets notification counts for a list of apps all at once. Use it to see how many notifications each app has sent.
Gets whether a named notification switch is on or off for a user. Use it to check if transaction or logistics notification alerts are enabled.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getP: Checks, for several apps at once, whether priority notifications are turned on. Use it to see which apps are allowed to send priority notifications.
Gets the notification priority settings for several apps at once. Use it to check which apps are set to show notifications with high priority.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getR: Gets the reminder details for several apps at once. Use it to see the reminders set for those apps.
Gets the custom ringtone an app uses for its notifications. Use it to find out which sound plays when that app sends a notification.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.getS: Gets the detailed configuration of one notification slot type, such as its reminder method, level, and lock screen display. Use it to check how a category like social messages or service reminders is set to alert you.
Gets a notification slot of a chosen type for an app. Use it to check how notifications of that type are set to behave.
Gets the notification slot flags for an app, such as sound alert and lock screen settings. Use it to check whether an app's notifications make a sound or show on the lock screen.
Gets how many notification slots an app has. Use it to count the notification categories set up for that app.
Gets all notification slots created by the app, including each slot's type, reminder method, and level. Use it to review every notification category's settings at once.
Gets the notification slots set up for a given application. Use it to see which kinds of notifications an app can post.
Tells whether notifications are synced to devices where the app is not installed. Use it to check if alerts follow the user to other devices.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isBa: Checks whether the notification badge (the dot or count on the app icon) is turned on for an app. Use it to see if unread counts will show on the icon.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isDi: Checks whether the device supports cross-device notifications. Use it to find out if notifications can be shared to another device such as a wearable or tablet.
Tells whether an app sends its notifications across the user's other devices. Use it to check if alerts appear on more than one device.
Tells whether notifications of a given kind can be sent to a certain type of device, such as a wearable or tablet. Use it to check if alerts reach another device.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isGe: Checks whether geofencing is enabled. Use it to find out if location-based reminders, such as alerts when arriving somewhere, are turned on.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isNo: Checks whether the current app is allowed to send notifications. Use it before posting an alert to avoid a failed notification.
Checks right away whether the app is allowed to send notifications. Use it to see if notifications are turned on before sending one.
Checks whether a notification slot type is turned on for a given app. Use it to find out if a certain kind of alert, such as messages or reminders, can reach the user.
Checks in one go whether a notification slot type is turned on for several apps. Use it to see which apps allow a certain kind of alert.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isPr: Checks whether priority notifications are turned on. Use it to find out if important alerts are allowed to stand out.
Checks whether priority notifications are turned on for a given app. Use it to see if that app may send important alerts.
Checks whether the intelligent priority notification service is turned on. Use it to find out if alerts can be ranked by importance automatically.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isSi: Checks whether silent reminders are turned on for a given app. Use it to find out if that app may remind the user quietly without sound.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isSm: Checks whether smart reminders for cross-device collaboration are turned on for a given device type. Use it to see if reminders can be sent between your devices.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.isSu: Checks whether the device supports Do Not Disturb mode. Use it to find out if silent mode for notifications is available.
Checks whether a given notification template is supported. Use it to confirm a template can be used before sending a notification with it.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.off: Stops listening for notification check events. Use it to stop screening incoming notifications once you no longer need to.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.offB: Stops the callback that reports how many notification badges an app has. Use it to stop tracking the app's unread badge count.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.offC: Stops the callback that checks notifications before they are shown. Use it to stop screening incoming notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.on: Listens for notification events and decides whether each notification should be shown, for example to limit how often marketing notifications appear. Use it to control which notifications get published.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.onBa: Registers a callback that reports how many badge notifications an app has. Use it to show or update the unread count on an app icon.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.onCh: Subscribes a callback that decides whether an incoming notification should be shown. Use it to filter which notifications are allowed through.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.open: Opens the app's notification settings page so the user can turn notifications on or change how they alert. Use it to guide someone to enable notifications after they declined.
Opens the app's notification settings page and reports back what the user set when they close it. Use it to guide someone to enable notifications and then check whether they did.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.publ: Shows a notification in the notification center and status bar. Use it to alert the user about a message or event, and publishing again with the same ID and tag updates the existing notification.
Publishes a notification on behalf of another app through the reminder agent. Use it to post a notification for an app whose notifications are taken over.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.remo: Removes all of the app's notification slots and their settings. Use it to clear every notification category setup at once.
Deletes a Do Not Disturb profile for a user. Use it to remove a quiet-hours setting so notifications are no longer silenced.
Removes all notifications in a named notification group of an app. Use it to clear a group of notifications at once.
Removes one notification slot of a chosen type and its settings. Use it to delete a notification category so it can be set up again.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.requ: Asks the user to turn on notifications for your app by showing a dialog box. Use it before sending a notification so the user can allow alerts.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setA: Sets extra notification configuration, such as which apps may use custom ringtones. Use it to allow an app's own ringtone for its notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setB: Sets whether notification badges are shown for several apps at once. Use it to turn the little red dot on or off for chosen apps.
Sets the number shown on the app icon badge, such as unread messages or to-do items. Set it to zero or less to clear the badge.
Sets the number shown on another app's notification badge. Use it to show a count, like unread messages, on an app's icon.
Sets the priority configuration for an app. Use it to control how prominently that app's notifications are treated.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setD: Turns distributed notifications on or off for this device. Use it to let notifications from your phone appear on other devices.
Turns distributed notifications on or off for one chosen app. Use it to let a specific app's notifications appear on other devices.
Sets whether several apps share notifications across devices, for a given device type. Use it to let chosen apps' notifications appear on other devices like a tablet.
Turns cross-device notifications on or off for a chosen device type, such as a headset or tablet. Use it to let notifications appear on another device you own.
Turns cross-device collaboration on or off for one chosen app. Use it to decide whether a specific app's notifications can show on your other devices.
Chooses whether notifications of one slot type can be sent to a chosen device type. Use it to control which kinds of alerts reach your other devices.
Sets the do-not-disturb time period for a user. Use it to silence notifications during chosen hours, such as at night.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setG: Turns geofencing on or off. Use it to enable or disable location-based alerts tied to places you arrive at or leave.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setN: Turns notifications on or off for a chosen app. Use it to stop or allow an app from sending you alerts.
Turns a notification slot type on or off for a chosen app. Use it to control which kinds of alerts an app may show.
Turns a named notification switch on or off for a user, such as the aggregated switch for transaction or logistics notifications. Use it to control those notification groups.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setP: Turns priority notifications on or off. Use it to allow important alerts to stand out.
Sets whether priority notifications are enabled for a chosen app, including smart recognition of important ones. Use it to control an app's priority alerts.
Sets whether priority notifications are enabled for several apps at once. Use it to turn priority alerts on or off for many apps together.
Turns the intelligent priority notification service on or off. Use it to let important alerts be recognised automatically.
Sets which apps' notifications should be treated as high priority, in batches. Use it to make important app alerts stand out.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setR: Sets reminders for several apps at once. Use it to schedule reminder alerts for chosen apps.
Sets a custom ringtone for an app's notifications. Use it to give an app its own alert sound.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setS: Turns an app's silent reminder on or off. Use it to make an app remind you quietly without sound.
Sets the notification slot used by a specified app. Use it to control how that app's alerts behave, such as sound or vibration.
Sets alert options for an app's notifications, such as sound, vibration, banner, or screen wake. Use it to choose how an app's alerts get your attention.
Turns a smart reminder for cross-device collaboration on or off for a chosen device type. Use it to let notifications be reminded across your other devices.
Sets whether notifications are synced to devices where the app is not installed. Use it to keep getting your phone's notifications on another device.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.setT: Sets the status of a connected device, such as whether it is in use or in Do Not Disturb. Use it to control how notifications are shown on that device.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.snoo: Snoozes a notification so it is reminded again after a set time, then deletes it. Use it to be reminded of a notification later.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.subs: Subscribes to system live view notifications. Use it to receive live view updates such as ongoing activity notifications.
NotificationKit.notificationManager.trig: Triggers a system live view notification with a chosen button. Use it to start a live view notification for an app.
NotificationKit.notificationSubscribe.di: Triggers a notification for cross-device actions like tap-to-redirect or quick reply. Use it to let someone act on a notification from another device.
NotificationKit.notificationSubscribe.re: Removes a single notification using its unique ID and a reason. Use it to clear a notification the user has already dealt with.
Removes all notifications for a specified application and user. Use it to clear every notification from an app at once.
NotificationKit.notificationSubscribe.su: Subscribes to notifications with the given subscription information. Use it to start receiving notifications so you can show or handle them.
Subscribes to notifications, delivering new messages through the subscriber's callback. Use it to receive incoming notifications as they arrive.
Subscribes to the application's own notifications. Use it to receive notifications posted by your own app.
NotificationKit.notificationSubscribe.un: Stops receiving notifications for a subscriber you previously set up. Use it to turn off notification delivery when you no longer want them.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.AppEventPackageHo: Sets how many event records are fetched at a time from a subscription. Use it to control the batch size when reading subscribed events.
Sets the data size limit, in bytes, for each batch of subscribed events fetched. Use it to control how much event data is read at once.
Gets the next batch of subscribed event data, or nothing when all events have been read. Use it to read through collected events one batch at a time.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.FaultLogExtension: Runs initialization when the system service finishes connecting to the fault log extension. Use it to set up before delayed fault notifications are handled.
Releases resources and clears the running status when the system service finishes disconnecting. Use it to clean up when a fault notification connection ends.
Handles fault events when the system service asks the app to process faults. Use it to receive and act on fault notifications.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.FaultLogger.query: Gets up to 10 cached fault records for the current application by fault type. Use it to look up crash or fault logs for your app.
Gets up to 10 cached fault records for the current application by fault type. Use it to look up your app's own crash or fault logs.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.bytrace.finishTra: Marks the end of a timeslice trace task. Use it to stop timing a piece of work you started tracing.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.bytrace.startTrac: Marks the start of a timeslice trace task, with an optional expected duration. Use it to begin timing a piece of work for performance tracing.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.bytrace.traceByVa: Records a named numeric value for performance tracing. Use it to count how many times a traced task ran while measuring app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.addPro: Registers a data processor that receives chosen events. Use it to set up which events get collected and handled for logging.
Registers a data processor using a saved configuration file. Use it to set up event collection from a named configuration.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.addWat: Adds a watcher that subscribes to events through its callback. Use it to be notified when chosen events happen in the app.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.clearD: Deletes the app's locally stored logging data. Use it to free up space or wipe collected event logs.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.config: Sets the configuration policy for system events. Use it to control how system events are collected during the app's lifecycle.
Sets up app event logging, such as the logging switch and storage quota. Use it to control how much event data is logged and kept.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.getUse: Reads back a user ID value that was stored earlier under a key. Use it to look up which user an event or log entry belongs to.
Reads back a user property value that was stored earlier under a key. Use it to look up saved details about a user, such as their name or level.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.remove: Stops and removes a data processor that was previously added for reported events. Use it to turn off sending event data to a destination you no longer need.
Removes an event watcher so it no longer receives event reports. Use it to stop listening for events you no longer care about.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.setEve: Sets configuration options for a named event, such as crash or main thread jank events. Use it to control how those events are recorded or logged.
Attaches custom parameters to an event, linking them by event domain and name. Use it to add your own details to crash, freeze, or resource leak reports.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.setUse: Sets a user ID used to associate events with a user when a processor is configured. Use it to tag logged events with the person they belong to.
Sets a user property used to associate events with a user when a processor is configured. Use it to attach extra details about a user to logged events.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiAppEvent.write: Writes a custom application event that can later be subscribed to. Use it to record your own events for logging and analysis.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.getCu: Queries the current HiRetrieval configuration. Use it to check the settings in effect for the retrieval feature.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.getLa: Queries the time of the last participation, in milliseconds, or zero if never. Use it to find out when the user last took part.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.init: Initializes the HiRetrieval functionality. Use it to set up the retrieval feature before using it.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.isPar: Checks whether the app is taking part in the HiRetrieval project. Use it to find out if this app is participating.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.parti: Joins the HiRetrieval project using the given settings. Use it to start taking part in HiRetrieval with your configuration.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.quit: Leaves the HiRetrieval project and clears the current configuration. Use it to stop participating in HiRetrieval.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiRetrieval.run: Starts the HiRetrieval functionality so it begins working. Use it to trigger HiRetrieval to start working.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.addWat: Adds a watcher that listens for system events. Use it to start receiving system event notifications for monitoring or debugging.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.export: Exports system events in batches and saves them as a file in the app's cache directory. Use it to collect system event logs for later review or analysis.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.query: Queries system events using given arguments and rules. Use it to look up recorded system events for troubleshooting or diagnostics.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.remove: Removes a watcher that was listening for system events. Use it to stop receiving system event notifications when monitoring is no longer needed.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.subscr: Subscribes to occasional or low-frequency real-time system events and saves them as a file in the app's cache directory. Use it to capture system events for monitoring or debugging.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.unsubs: Stops receiving system event notifications that were previously subscribed to. Use it to stop listening for system events when they are no longer needed.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiSysEvent.write: Writes system event information to the event file. Use it to record a system event for later analysis.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.begi: Starts call chain trace for a named service and returns a trace ID. Use it to trace calls through a service process.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.clea: Clears the trace ID stored for the current thread. Use it to stop tracing the current thread's call chain.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.crea: Creates a new trace span and returns its trace ID. Use it to mark the start of a traced step in a call chain.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.enab: Turns on a chosen trace flag for a trace ID. Use it to switch on a specific tracing option for a call chain.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.end: Stops call chain tracing for the given trace ID. Use it to finish tracing a call chain when the work is done.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.getI: Gets the trace ID stored for the current thread. Use it to read the current call chain's trace ID.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.isFl: Checks whether a trace flag is turned on for a trace ID. Use it to see if a tracing option is active.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.isVa: Checks whether a trace ID is valid. Use it to confirm a trace ID can be used before tracing.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.setI: Sets a trace ID for the current thread so its activity can be followed through a call chain. Use it to tag work with an ID when tracing how a request flows through your app.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceChain.trac: Adds a trace point that starts or ends performance tracing for a call chain, depending on the type chosen. Use it to mark where a traced operation begins and ends so its timing can be measured.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.fini: Stops an asynchronous trace that was started earlier, using the same level, name, and task ID. Use it to end timing of a background task you started tracking.
Stops a synchronous trace at the given output level, matching the level used when it started. Use it to end timing of a piece of work you were measuring.
Stops an asynchronous trace, using the same name and task ID as when it started. Use it to end timing of a task you began tracking.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.isTr: Checks whether application trace capture is currently enabled. Use it to decide whether to bother recording performance traces.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.regi: Registers a callback that tells you when application trace capture is turned on or off. Use it to react when performance tracing starts or stops.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.star: Starts tracking a background task that runs at the same time as others, giving each one an ID so they can be told apart. Use it to measure how long overlapping jobs take when checking app performance.
Starts tracking a task that runs step by step in order. Use it to measure how long a single piece of work takes when checking app performance.
Starts tracking a background task, giving it an ID so several tasks with the same name can be told apart. Use it to measure how long a job takes when checking app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.trac: Records how the value of a whole number changes over time. Use it to watch a counter or similar number while checking app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hiTraceMeter.unre: Stops the callback that tells you whether trace capture is turned on. Use it to clean up when you no longer need to know if tracing is active.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.addChec: Adds one or more rules so the app is checked for unexpected operations and reports them in the logs. Use it during development to catch mistakes that are easy to miss.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.addRule: Adds one or more rules so that unexpected operations are detected or reported. Use it to turn on checks for issues that are easy to miss while building an app.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.contain: Checks whether a given rule is already in the set of added rules. Use it to confirm a check is active before relying on it.
Checks whether a given rule is already in the set of added rules. Use it to confirm a check is active before relying on it.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.getRule: Gets the collection of thread, process, and alarm rules that have been added. Use it to see which checks are currently turned on.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.removeC: Removes one or more rules so they stop taking effect. Use it to turn off checks you no longer need.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hichecker.removeR: Removes one or more rules so they stop taking effect. Use it to turn off checks you no longer need.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.disableGw: Turns off GWP-ASan and restores the default settings. Use it to stop the extra memory error checking you turned on earlier.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.dumpHeapD: Saves the app's memory heap to a snapshot file with the name you give. Use it to capture a memory snapshot for checking how much memory the app is using.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.dumpJsHea: Saves the app's heap data to a snapshot file with the name you give. Use it to capture a memory snapshot for checking how much memory the app is using.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.dumpJsRaw: Saves a raw heap snapshot of the current thread and gives back the file path. Use it to capture a memory snapshot for checking how much memory the app is using.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.enableGwp: Turns on GWP-ASan for your app. Use it to switch on extra memory error checking while your app runs.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getAppMem: Gets the memory limit of the app process. Use it to find out how much memory your app is allowed to use.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getAppNat: Reads the memory usage of the app's process. Use it to check how much memory the app is using.
Reads the memory usage of the app's process. Use it to check how much memory the app is using.
Reads the app process memory usage using a five-minute cache, faster than reading it fresh. Use it to check memory usage often without slowing things down.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getAppThr: Gets the CPU usage of the app's threads. Use it to see which threads are working hard and slowing the app down.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getAppVMM: Gets the virtual machine's memory information. Use it to check how much memory the app's runtime is using.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getAppVMO: Gets the virtual machine memory size used by app objects, in KB. Use it to see how much memory the app's objects take up.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getCpuUsa: Reports how much CPU a process is using, as a fraction such as 0.5 for 50%. Use it to check how hard a running app is working.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getGraphi: Reports the total GPU memory an app is using, in kilobytes. Use it to see how much graphics memory the app takes up.
Reports a summary of the app's GPU memory use, in kilobytes. Use it to check graphics memory usage over a chosen interval.
Reports the total GPU memory an app is using, in kilobytes, right away. Use it to check graphics memory use without waiting.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getGwpAsa: Reports how many days of GWP-ASan grayscale remain for the app. Use it to check how long this memory-checking period still lasts.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getNative: Reports how many bytes of memory a process has allocated from the native heap. Use it to see how much native memory the app is holding.
Reports how many bytes of free space the memory allocator holds for the process. Use it to check available heap memory when tracking down memory problems.
Reports the total bytes of memory the allocator holds for the process. Use it to see how much heap memory the app is using.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getPrivat: Reports the private dirty memory size of the process in kilobytes. Use it to check memory the app alone is using when investigating memory growth.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getPss: Reports the physical memory actually used by the app process, in kilobytes. Use it to see how much real memory the app is taking up.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getRssInf: Reports the physical memory information of the app process. Use it to check the app's resident memory usage.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getServic: Gets information about a system service and writes it to a file. Use it to inspect or debug system service state.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getShared: Reports the shared dirty memory size of the process in kilobytes. Use it to check memory shared with other processes when investigating memory usage.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getSystem: Tells you how busy the whole system's processor is, as a fraction such as 0.5 for 50%. Use it to check whether the device is under heavy load.
Reads and returns how much memory the system is using and has free. Use it to see whether the device is running low on memory.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getVMRunt: Returns one chosen garbage-collection statistic, such as how many collections ran or how much memory was freed. Use it to check how much memory cleanup the app is doing.
Returns the system's garbage-collection statistics. Use it to see how often and how long memory cleanup runs in the app.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.getVss: Reports the total virtual memory size the app process has reserved, in kilobytes. Use it to check how much memory the app is holding.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.isDebugSt: Tells you whether the app process is currently being debugged. Use it to detect when a debugger is attached.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.requestTr: Collects a trace of what the program is doing and returns the path of the trace file. Use it to record activity for later performance analysis.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.setAppRes: Sets the maximum allowed file descriptors, threads, JavaScript heap memory, or native memory for the application. Use it to cap resource use and catch memory or handle leaks.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.setJsRawH: Sets how much detail is kept when trimming the raw heap snapshot of the current process. Use it to control heap snapshot size for memory analysis.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.setProcDu: Chooses whether a heap snapshot is dumped for the whole process or just one thread when shared memory runs out. Use it to control what memory dump you get when the app runs out of memory.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.startAppT: Starts recording a trace of app activity within chosen scopes and returns the trace file path. Use it to capture performance traces while the app runs.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.startJsCp: Starts sampling how the JavaScript code uses the CPU, saving results to a named file. Use it to profile which code is slow or heavy.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.startProf: Starts recording how the program uses the processor, saving the sample data to a file you name. Use it to profile your app's performance and find slow parts.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.stopAppTr: Stops collecting a trace of what the application is doing. Use it to end a trace you started earlier when investigating app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.stopJsCpu: Stops recording how the program uses the processor. Use it to end a profiling session you started earlier when checking app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hidebug.stopProfi: Stops recording how the program uses the processor. Use it to end a profiling session you started earlier when checking app performance.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.clean: Deletes all log records stored in the app's sandbox. Use it to clear old logs and free up space.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.debug: Prints a debug-level log message with a service domain, tag, and formatted text. Use it to record detailed diagnostic information while troubleshooting your app.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.error: Prints an ERROR-level log message with a service domain, tag, and formatted text. Use it to record serious problems while debugging or monitoring how an app is running.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.fatal: Prints a FATAL-level log message with a service domain, tag, and formatted text. Use it to record the most severe failures while debugging or monitoring how an app is running.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.flush: Flushes buffered log messages in the sandbox. Use it to make sure recent log entries are written out before reading or collecting them.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.getLogFile: Returns the paths of log files from a chosen recent time period, newest first. Use it to find and collect recent logs for troubleshooting.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.getOutputDi: Returns the folder path where log files are stored in the sandbox. Use it to locate the logs so you can read or collect them.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.getOutputTy: Returns the current output type used for logs. Use it to check where logs are being sent before reading or collecting them.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.info: Writes an informational log message with a service domain, tag, and formatted text. Use it to record what your app is doing so you can review its running status later.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.isLoggable: Checks whether a log message would actually be printed for a given service domain, tag, and level. Use it to skip building expensive log text when that log would not appear.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.setLogLevel: Sets the lowest log level your app will output, with a choice of preference strategy. Use it to quiet noisy logs or raise detail while debugging.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.setMinLogLe: Sets the lowest log level that will be output. Use it to control how much detail your app writes to its logs.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.setOutputTy: Sets where log output goes and returns the previous setting. Use it to switch your app's logs between destinations.
Sets where logs go for a chosen list of service domains, or for all others, and returns the previous setting. Use it to route logs from specific services to a different destination.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.hilog.warn: Prints warning-level logs with a service domain, tag, and formatted message. Use it to record warnings about your app's running status for troubleshooting.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.jsLeakWatcher.che: Gets the list of registered objects that were not reclaimed after garbage collection, marking them as leaked. Use it to find memory leaks in your app's objects.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.jsLeakWatcher.dum: Saves the list of leaked objects and a memory snapshot to files at the given path. Use it to inspect leaked objects and memory usage when hunting memory leaks.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.jsLeakWatcher.ena: Turns JS object leak detection on or off; it is off by default. Use it to start monitoring your app for leaked objects.
Enables ArkTS object leak detection in one call, optionally limiting which object types are monitored. Use it to watch for memory leaks in components, windows, or abilities.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.jsLeakWatcher.wat: Registers an object to be checked for leaks, with custom information about it. Use it to mark objects you want leak detection to track.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.logLibrary.copy: Copies log files of a chosen type into a folder in the app's cache directory. Use it to keep a copy of logs such as fault or beta logs for later use.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.logLibrary.list: Gets the list of log files of a chosen type. Use it to see which logs, such as fault or beta logs, are available.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.logLibrary.move: Moves log files of a chosen type into a folder in the app's cache directory. Use it to relocate logs such as fault or beta logs to a folder you choose.
PerformanceAnalysisKit.logLibrary.remove: Deletes log files of a chosen type. Use it to clear out logs such as fault or beta logs you no longer need.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.getModelR: Asks the security guard for a security model result based on a given rule. Use it to check the running status of a device against a security model.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.off: Stops receiving a security event you previously subscribed to. Use it to cancel security event monitoring when you no longer need updates.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.on: Subscribes to a security event so you are notified when it occurs. Use it to watch for security events and react to them.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.querySecu: Queries security event information from the security guard using given rules. Use it to look up recorded security events matching your criteria.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.reportSec: Reports security event information to the security guard. Use it to send a security event so it can be recorded and analyzed.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.startSecu: Starts a collector that gathers security event data according to a rule. Use it to begin collecting security event information for analysis.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.stopSecur: Stops collecting security event information. Use it to end monitoring of a device's running status for security analysis.
SecurityGuardKit.securityGuard.updatePol: Updates the policy file with new policy file information. Use it to change the security rules a device follows.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.getOnBodyState: Checks whether a wearable device is currently being worn. Use it to tell if the watch or band is on the body.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeAcceler: Starts reporting changes in the acceleration sensor's data. Use it to detect movement, tilt, or shake of the device.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeBaromet: Starts reporting changes in the barometer sensor's data. Use it to track air pressure changes, such as for altitude or weather.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeCompass: Starts reporting changes in the compass sensor's data. Use it to find which direction the device is facing.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeDeviceO: Starts reporting changes in the device orientation sensor's data. Use it to tell how the device is turned or held.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeGyrosco: Starts reporting changes in the gyroscope sensor's data. Use it to detect rotation or spinning of the device.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeHeartRa: Starts listening for changes in heart rate sensor data. Use it to track your heart rate during exercise or rest.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeLight: Starts listening for changes in ambient light sensor data. Use it to detect how bright the surroundings are, such as for auto screen brightness.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeOnBodyS: Starts listening for changes in whether a wearable device is being worn. Use it to tell when the watch is put on or taken off.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeProximi: Starts listening for changes in proximity sensor data. Use it to detect when something is close to the screen, such as during a phone call.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.subscribeStepCou: Starts listening for changes in step counter sensor data. Use it to count your steps as you walk or run.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeAccel: Stops listening for changes in acceleration sensor data. Use it to stop tracking movement or tilt once you no longer need it.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeBarom: Stops receiving updates from the barometer sensor. Use it to stop tracking air pressure or altitude changes.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeCompa: Stops receiving updates from the compass sensor. Use it to stop tracking which direction the device is facing.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeDevic: Stops receiving updates from the device orientation sensor. Use it to stop tracking how the device is tilted or rotated.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeGyros: Stops receiving updates from the gyroscope sensor. Use it to stop tracking the device's rotation.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeHeart: Stops receiving updates from the heart rate sensor. Use it to stop tracking the user's heart rate.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeLight: Stops receiving updates from the ambient light sensor. Use it to stop tracking surrounding light levels.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeOnBod: Stops receiving updates about whether a wearable device is being worn. Use it to stop tracking when the device is put on or taken off.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeProxi: Stops receiving updates from the proximity sensor. Use it to stop detecting when an object is near the device.
SensorServiceKit.Sensor.unsubscribeStepC: Stops receiving updates from the step counter sensor. Use it to stop counting steps.
SensorServiceKit.Vibrator.vibrate: Makes the device vibrate. Use it to buzz the phone for an alert, notification, or touch feedback.
Adds a long vibration event to a vibration pattern, with a start time and duration. Use it to build a pattern that makes the device vibrate for a longer stretch.
Adds a short vibration event to a vibration pattern at a given start time. Use it to build a pattern that makes the device give a brief buzz.
Creates a vibration pattern object from the short and long events added to it. Use it to finish building a vibration sequence for the device to play.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.createQuaternion: Turns a rotation vector into a quaternion. Use it to work out device orientation for motion tracking or augmented reality.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.createRotationMa: Works out a rotation matrix from a gravity vector and a geomagnetic vector. Use it to track how the device is oriented in space.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getAltitude: Works out the altitude of the device from sea-level and current atmospheric pressure. Use it to tell how high up you are.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getAngleModify: Works out the angle change between two rotation matrices. Use it to measure how far the device has turned.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getAngleVariatio: Works out the angle change between two rotation matrices. Use it to measure how far the device has turned.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getDeviceAltitud: Works out the altitude from atmospheric pressure. Use it to tell how high up the device is.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getDirection: Works out which way the device is pointing from a rotation matrix, giving the angles around the z, x and y axes in degrees. Use it to tell which way the phone is facing, as in a compass or map that turns with you.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getGeomagneticDi: Works out the magnetic dip, in radians, from an inclination matrix. Use it to find how steeply Earth's magnetic field dips at your position, as in compass or navigation apps.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getGeomagneticFi: Gives the geomagnetic field at a geographic location for a chosen time. Use it to find magnetic field strength and declination for a place, as in compass or navigation apps.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getGeomagneticIn: Gives the geomagnetic field at a geographic location at a certain time. Use it to find magnetic field strength and declination for a place and moment, as in compass or navigation apps.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getInclination: Works out the magnetic dip, in radians, from an inclination matrix. Use it to find how steeply Earth's magnetic field dips at your position, as in compass or navigation apps.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getOrientation: Works out which way the device is pointing from a rotation matrix, giving the angles around the z, x and y axes in degrees. Use it to tell which way the phone is facing, as in a compass or map that turns with you.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getQuaternion: Turns a rotation vector into a quaternion, a set of numbers describing an orientation in 3D. Use it to track how a device is turned or tilted, such as for motion tracking or a compass.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getRotationMatri: Turns a gravity vector and a geomagnetic vector into a rotation matrix describing device orientation. Use it to work out which way a device is facing, such as for a compass or augmented reality view.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSensorList: Lists all sensors built into the device. Use it to see which sensors are available, such as checking for a step counter or heart rate sensor.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSensorListByD: Lists all sensors on the device, optionally for a given device. Use it to see which sensors are available, such as checking for a step counter or heart rate sensor.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSensorListSyn: Lists all sensors built into the device right away. Use it to see which sensors are available, such as checking for a step counter or heart rate sensor.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSingleSensor: Gets information about one sensor of a chosen type. Use it to check details of a specific sensor, such as whether the device has a heart rate sensor.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSingleSensorB: Gets information about a sensor of a given type. Use it to check which sensors are available and their details before reading sensor data.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.getSingleSensorS: Gets information about one sensor of a chosen type, returned straight away. Use it to look up a sensor's details before reading its data.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.off: Stops receiving data from a sensor you were subscribed to. Use it to stop sensor updates when you no longer need them.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offAccelerometer: Stops receiving accelerometer data about movement and tilt. Use it to stop motion updates when you no longer need them.
Stops receiving raw, uncalibrated accelerometer data. Use it to stop uncalibrated motion updates when you no longer need them.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offAmbientLightC: Stops receiving ambient light sensor data. Use it to stop light-level updates, for example when leaving an auto-brightness screen.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offAmbientTemper: Stops receiving ambient temperature sensor data. Use it to stop temperature updates when you no longer need them.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offBarometerChan: Stops receiving barometer sensor data. Use it to stop tracking air pressure changes, such as for weather or altitude readings.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offColorChange: Stops receiving color sensor data. Use it to stop detecting the color of light or objects.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offFusionPressur: Stops receiving fusion pressure sensor data. Use it to stop tracking combined pressure readings for altitude or weather.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offGravityChange: Stops receiving gravity sensor data. Use it to stop tracking which way is down, such as for screen rotation or level tools.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offGyroscopeChan: Stops receiving gyroscope sensor data. Use it to stop tracking rotation and turning motion, such as for games or camera stabilization.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offGyroscopeUnca: Stops receiving uncalibrated gyroscope sensor data. Use it to stop tracking raw rotation motion without calibration corrections.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offHallChange: Stops receiving hall sensor data. Use it to stop detecting magnetic fields, such as for a flip cover or magnetic dock.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offHeartRateChan: Stops receiving heart rate sensor updates. Use it to stop tracking your heart rate when you no longer need it.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offHumidityChang: Stops receiving humidity sensor updates. Use it to stop checking how humid the air is.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offLinearAcceler: Stops receiving linear acceleration sensor updates. Use it to stop tracking movement without gravity.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offMagneticField: Stops receiving magnetic field sensor updates. Use it to stop reading the magnetic field around you.
Stops receiving uncalibrated magnetic field sensor updates. Use it to stop reading raw magnetic field values.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offOrientationCh: Stops receiving orientation sensor updates. Use it to stop tracking which way the device is facing.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offPedometerChan: Stops receiving step-count updates from the pedometer sensor. Use it to stop tracking how many steps someone has taken.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offPedometerDete: Stops receiving pedometer detection updates that report when a person is walking. Use it to stop detecting walking activity.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offProximityChan: Stops receiving updates from the proximity sensor. Use it to stop detecting when something is close to the screen, such as during a phone call.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offRotationVecto: Stops receiving rotation vector updates that describe the device's orientation in space. Use it to stop tracking which way the device is turned.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offSarChange: Stops receiving SAR sensor data. Use it to stop monitoring radio wave exposure near the device.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offSensorStatusC: Stops listening for changes in the status of the device's sensors. Use it to stop being told when a sensor turns on or off.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offSignificantMo: Stops receiving significant motion updates that report a notable movement of the device. Use it to stop detecting when the device is picked up or moved.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.offWearDetection: Stops receiving wear detection sensor data. Use it to stop checking whether a device is being worn.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.on: Subscribes to sensor status change events. Use it to be notified when a sensor's status changes.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onAccelerometerC: Subscribes to accelerometer sensor data. Use it to detect movement, tilt, or shake of the device.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onAccelerometerU: Subscribes to uncalibrated accelerometer sensor data. Use it to get raw motion readings without calibration applied.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onAmbientLightCh: Subscribes to ambient light sensor data. Use it to detect how bright the surroundings are.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onAmbientTempera: Subscribes to ambient temperature sensor data. Use it to read the surrounding temperature.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onBarometerChang: Subscribes to barometer sensor data so you receive pressure readings as they change. Use it to check air pressure or help estimate altitude and weather changes.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onColorChange: Starts receiving color sensor data. Use it to detect the color of light or objects.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onFusionPressure: Subscribes to fusion pressure sensor data so you receive combined pressure readings as they change. Use it to track air pressure for altitude or weather-related readings.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onGravityChange: Subscribes to gravity sensor data so you receive the direction and strength of gravity as it changes. Use it to detect device tilt or orientation.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onGyroscopeChang: Subscribes to gyroscope sensor data so you receive rotation readings as they change. Use it to detect how the device is turning or rotating.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onGyroscopeUncal: Subscribes to uncalibrated gyroscope sensor data so you receive raw rotation readings as they change. Use it when you need rotation data without calibration applied.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onHallChange: Subscribes to hall sensor data so you receive magnetic field readings as they change. Use it to detect nearby magnets or a magnetic cover opening and closing.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onHeartRateChang: Subscribes to heart rate sensor data so you receive updates as your heart rate changes. Use it to show your pulse while exercising or to track heart rate during a workout.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onHumidityChange: Subscribes to humidity sensor data so you receive updates as the surrounding moisture level changes. Use it to show the current humidity in a weather or indoor comfort display.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onLinearAccelero: Subscribes to linear acceleration sensor data so you receive updates as the device's movement speed changes. Use it to detect motion, such as counting steps or tracking how the device moves.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onMagneticFieldC: Subscribes to magnetic field sensor data so you receive updates as the surrounding magnetic field changes. Use it to build a compass or find magnetic objects nearby.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onMagneticFieldU: Subscribes to uncalibrated magnetic field sensor data so you receive raw magnetic readings as they change. Use it when you need the unprocessed magnetic field values, such as for custom compass calibration.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onOrientationCha: Subscribes to orientation sensor data so you receive updates as the device's orientation changes. Use it to tell which way the device is facing, such as for a compass or screen rotation.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onPedometerChang: Subscribes to pedometer sensor data, reporting step counts as they change. Use it to track how many steps someone has walked.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onPedometerDetec: Subscribes to pedometer detection sensor data, reporting when walking is detected. Use it to tell when someone has started walking.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onProximityChang: Subscribes to proximity sensor data, reporting nearby objects. Use it to detect when something is close to the screen, such as during a phone call.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onRotationVector: Subscribes to rotation vector sensor data, reporting the device's orientation in space. Use it to track how the device is turned or tilted.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onSarChange: Starts receiving SAR sensor data. Use it to monitor radio wave exposure near the device.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onSensorStatusCh: Starts listening for changes in sensor device status. Use it to know when a sensor turns on, off, or changes state.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onSignificantMot: Subscribes to significant motion sensor data, reporting when a notable movement occurs. Use it to detect when the device starts moving after being still.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.onWearDetectionC: Watches for changes in whether a wearable device is being worn. Use it to tell when the device is put on or taken off, for example to pause or resume playback.
SensorServiceKit.sensor.once: Reads the pedometer sensor once to get a single step count. Use it to check how many steps have been taken.
