TelephonyKit.radio.isNRSupported: Checks whether the device supports 5G New Radio for a card slot. Use it to tell if a phone can connect to 5G.
TelephonyKit.radio.isNrSupported: Checks whether the device supports 5G New Radio for a card slot. Use it to tell if a phone can connect to 5G.
TelephonyKit.radio.isRadioOn: Checks whether the radio service is turned on for a card slot. Use it to see if the phone radio is enabled before making calls or using mobile data.
TelephonyKit.radio.off: Stops listening for changes in the IMS registration state on a chosen SIM card and service. Use it to stop being notified about whether calling over the mobile network is registered.
TelephonyKit.radio.offImsRegStateChange: Stops listening for IMS registration state changes on a chosen SIM card and service. Use it to stop being notified about whether calling over the mobile network is registered.
TelephonyKit.radio.on: Starts listening for changes in the IMS registration state on a chosen SIM card and service. Use it to know when calling over the mobile network becomes registered or unregistered.
TelephonyKit.radio.onImsRegStateChange: Starts listening for IMS registration state changes on a chosen SIM card and service. Use it to know when calling over the mobile network becomes registered or unregistered.
TelephonyKit.radio.sendUpdateCellLocatio: Asks the network to refresh the device's location information for a chosen SIM card. Use it to get an up-to-date cell location, for example to help find where you are.
TelephonyKit.radio.setNROptionMode: Sets the NR option mode for a chosen SIM card. Use it to choose how the phone uses 5G networks on that SIM.
TelephonyKit.radio.setNetworkCapability: Turns a chosen network service capability on or off for a SIM card slot. Use it to enable or disable a cellular service for a specific SIM.
TelephonyKit.radio.setNetworkSelectionMo: Sets how the phone chooses its cellular network, such as automatic or manual selection. Use it to control which network the phone connects to.
TelephonyKit.radio.setPreferredNetwork: Sets the preferred network type for a chosen SIM card slot. Use it to pick which cellular network mode a SIM should use.
TelephonyKit.radio.setPrimarySlotId: Sets which SIM card slot is the main one. Use it to choose the primary SIM for the phone.
TelephonyKit.radio.startManualNetworkSca: Starts a manual scan for available cellular networks on a SIM slot and reports results as they come in. Use it to search for networks to connect to.
TelephonyKit.radio.stopManualNetworkScan: Stops an ongoing manual scan for cellular networks on a SIM slot. Use it to cancel a network search.
TelephonyKit.radio.turnOffRadio: Turns off the radio service for a SIM card slot. Use it to disable cellular network connectivity, such as when going offline or saving battery.
TelephonyKit.radio.turnOnRadio: Turns on the radio service for a SIM card slot. Use it to enable cellular network connectivity so the phone can make calls and use mobile data.
TelephonyKit.sim.activateSim: Activates the SIM card in the specified slot. Use it to enable a SIM card so it can be used for phone calls and mobile network services.
TelephonyKit.sim.addIccDiallingNumbers: Adds dialing number information to a SIM card. Use it to save a phone number to the SIM card's contacts.
TelephonyKit.sim.alterPin: Changes the PIN password of a SIM card. Use it to set a new PIN for the SIM card.
TelephonyKit.sim.alterPin2: Changes the PIN2 password of a SIM card. Use it to set a new PIN2 for the SIM card.
TelephonyKit.sim.deactivateSim: Turns off the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to disable a phone line so that SIM stops working.
TelephonyKit.sim.delIccDiallingNumbers: Deletes a dialing number stored on the SIM card. Use it to remove a saved phone number from the SIM.
TelephonyKit.sim.getActiveSimAccountInfo: Gets the list of active SIM card account information, including ICCID and phone number. Use it to see which SIM accounts are active on the device.
TelephonyKit.sim.getAllSimAccountInfoLis: Gets the account information for every SIM card. Use it to list the SIM accounts and their phone numbers.
TelephonyKit.sim.getCardType: Tells you the type of SIM card installed in a given card slot. Use it to check what kind of SIM is in a slot.
TelephonyKit.sim.getCardTypeSync: Tells you the type of SIM card inserted in a given card slot. Use it to check what kind of SIM is in a slot.
TelephonyKit.sim.getDefaultVoiceSimId: Gets the SIM ID of the default SIM used for voice service. Use it to find which SIM handles phone calls.
TelephonyKit.sim.getDefaultVoiceSlotId: Gets the card slot used by default for the voice service. Use it to find which slot handles phone calls.
TelephonyKit.sim.getDsdsMode: Gets the dual-SIM dual-standby mode value. Use it to check how the two SIM cards share standby.
TelephonyKit.sim.getIMSI: Gets the international mobile subscriber ID of the SIM in a slot. Use it to identify the subscriber of a phone line.
TelephonyKit.sim.getISOCountryCodeForSim: Gets the ISO country code of the SIM card in a given slot. Use it to find the country of the SIM's carrier.
Gets the ISO country code of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to find out which country a SIM card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getLockState: Gets the lock status of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to check whether a SIM is locked.
TelephonyKit.sim.getMaxSimCount: Tells you the maximum number of SIM cards the device can use at once, meaning how many card slots it has. Use it to see how many SIM cards the phone supports.
TelephonyKit.sim.getOpKey: Gets the operator key of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to identify which mobile network operator a SIM card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getOpKeySync: Gets the operator key of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to identify which mobile network operator a SIM card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getOpName: Gets the operator name of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to show which mobile network a SIM card is on.
TelephonyKit.sim.getOpNameSync: Gets the operator name of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to show which mobile network a SIM card is on.
TelephonyKit.sim.getOperatorConfigs: Gets the operator settings for the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to look up which mobile network operator a SIM belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getShowName: Gets the display name of the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to show which SIM is which when a phone has more than one card.
TelephonyKit.sim.getShowNumber: Gets the phone number of the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to show the user their own phone number.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimAccountInfo: Gets the account information of the SIM card in a given slot, such as its ICCID and phone number. Use it to read the SIM card details of a phone.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimAuthentication: Performs SIM card authentication using a chosen slot, authentication type, and authentication data. Use it to verify a SIM card for secure network access.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimGid1: Gets the Group Identifier Level 1 of the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to read the SIM's group identifier for operator or service checks.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimIccId: Gets the unique 20-digit ICCID of the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Use it to identify a specific SIM card.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimLabel: Gets the label of the SIM card in a given slot. Use it to show which SIM card is in a slot.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimLabelSync: Gets the label of the SIM card in a given slot right away. Use it to show which SIM card is in a slot.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimOperatorNumeric: Gets the home network number stored on the SIM card in a given slot, or an empty string if no card is inserted. Use it to find out which mobile network a SIM card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimOperatorNumericSy: Gets the home network number stored on the SIM card in a given slot right away, or an empty string if no card is inserted. Use it to find out which mobile network a SIM card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimSpn: Gets the service provider name stored on the SIM card in a given slot, or an empty string if unavailable. Use it to show the name of the mobile operator for a SIM card.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimSpnSync: Reads the service provider name stored on the SIM card in a given slot. Use it to show which mobile network the card belongs to.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimState: Tells you the state of the SIM card in a given slot, such as ready, locked, or missing. Use it to check whether the phone can make calls or use mobile data.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimStateSync: Tells you the state of the SIM card in a given slot, such as ready, locked, or missing. Use it to check whether the phone can make calls or use mobile data.
TelephonyKit.sim.getSimTelephoneNumber: Reads the phone number stored on the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to show the user their own phone number.
TelephonyKit.sim.getVoiceMailIdentifier: Reads the name label of the voice mailbox stored on the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to show the voicemail name.
TelephonyKit.sim.getVoiceMailNumber: Reads the voice mailbox number stored on the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to dial or show the voicemail number.
TelephonyKit.sim.hasOperatorPrivileges: Checks whether your app has been granted operator permissions for the SIM card in a given slot. Use it to decide whether operator-specific features are allowed.
TelephonyKit.sim.hasSimCard: Checks whether a SIM card is inserted in a given slot. Use it to tell whether the phone can make calls or use mobile data.
TelephonyKit.sim.hasSimCardSync: Checks whether a SIM card is inserted in a given slot. Use it to tell whether the phone can make calls or use mobile data.
TelephonyKit.sim.isOperatorSimCard: Checks whether the SIM card in a chosen slot belongs to a given mobile operator. Use it to tell which carrier the user's SIM is on.
TelephonyKit.sim.isSimActive: Checks whether the SIM card in a given card slot is activated. Use it to find out if a SIM is ready for phone calls or messages.
TelephonyKit.sim.isSimActiveSync: Checks whether the SIM card in a given card slot is activated. Use it to find out if a SIM is ready for phone calls or messages.
TelephonyKit.sim.queryIccDiallingNumbers: Lists the dialling numbers saved on the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to show the contacts stored on the SIM.
TelephonyKit.sim.sendEnvelopeCmd: Sends an envelope command to the SIM card in a chosen slot. Use it to pass a command through to the SIM.
TelephonyKit.sim.sendTerminalResponseCmd: Sends a terminal response command to the SIM card in a chosen card slot. Used to reply to SIM card commands during card operations.
TelephonyKit.sim.setDefaultVoiceSlotId: Sets which card slot is used for the default voice service. Used to choose which SIM makes phone calls by default.
TelephonyKit.sim.setLockState: Sets the lock status of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Used to lock or unlock a SIM card.
TelephonyKit.sim.setShowName: Sets the display name of the SIM card in a chosen slot. Used to rename a SIM card as shown on the phone.
TelephonyKit.sim.setShowNumber: Sets the phone number stored for the SIM card in a chosen slot. Used to save the SIM card's own phone number.
TelephonyKit.sim.setSimLabelIndex: Sets the label index of a SIM card. Used to label a SIM card for identification.
TelephonyKit.sim.setVoiceMailInfo: Sets the name and number used for voice mail on a chosen SIM card slot. Use it to set up where your phone call voicemail is reached.
TelephonyKit.sim.unlockPin: Unlocks a SIM card in a chosen card slot using its PIN password. Use it to get phone service back after entering the wrong SIM PIN.
TelephonyKit.sim.unlockPin2: Unlocks a SIM card in a chosen card slot using its PIN2 password. Use it to unlock the second SIM PIN that guards certain SIM features.
TelephonyKit.sim.unlockPuk: Unlocks a SIM card in a chosen card slot with its PUK and sets a new PIN. Use it to recover phone service when the SIM is blocked after too many wrong PIN tries.
TelephonyKit.sim.unlockPuk2: Unlocks a SIM card in a chosen card slot with its PUK2 and sets a new PIN2. Use it to recover the second SIM PIN when it is blocked.
TelephonyKit.sim.unlockSimLock: Unlocks a SIM card in a chosen card slot using customized lock information. Use it to remove a carrier or network lock so the SIM works for phone service.
TelephonyKit.sim.updateIccDiallingNumber: Updates a dialling number stored on a SIM card. Use it to change a saved phone number on the card.
TelephonyKit.sms.addSimMessage: Adds a text message to the SIM card. Use it to save a message onto the card.
TelephonyKit.sms.createMessage: Creates an SMS message instance from raw received data and the SMS protocol type. Use it to read or process a text message the phone has received.
TelephonyKit.sms.decodeMms: Decodes the content of a multimedia message file. Use it to read a picture message from a file.
TelephonyKit.sms.delSimMessage: Deletes a text message from the SIM card. Use it to remove a saved message from the card.
TelephonyKit.sms.downloadMms: Downloads a multimedia message. Use it to fetch a picture message.
TelephonyKit.sms.encodeMms: Encodes multimedia message content. Use it to prepare a picture message for sending.
TelephonyKit.sms.getAllSimMessages: Reads every text message stored on a SIM card. Use it to list or back up the messages saved on a SIM.
TelephonyKit.sms.getDefaultSmsSimId: Gets the SIM ID used by default for sending SMS messages. Use it to know which SIM sends your text messages.
TelephonyKit.sms.getDefaultSmsSlotId: Gets the card slot of the default SIM used for sending SMS messages. Use it to know which SIM sends your text messages.
TelephonyKit.sms.getImsShortMessageForma: Tells which text message format is used over IMS, either 3GPP, 3GPP2, or unknown. Use it to check how text messages are formatted on the network.
TelephonyKit.sms.getSmsSegmentsInfo: Shows how a text message is split and encoded into segments before sending. Use it to see how many parts a long text message will take.
TelephonyKit.sms.getSmsShortCodeType: Gets the short code type of the number a text message is sent to. Use it to check what kind of short code a destination number is.
TelephonyKit.sms.getSmscAddr: Gets the message center address for a SIM card slot. Use it to find the number texts are sent through.
TelephonyKit.sms.hasSmsCapability: Tells whether the device can send and receive SMS messages. Use it to check if texting is possible on this device.
TelephonyKit.sms.isImsSmsSupported: Checks whether text messages over IMS are supported on a SIM card slot. Use it to see if texting works over IMS on that card.
TelephonyKit.sms.sendMessage: Sends a text or data SMS message, splitting it into parts if it is too long. Use it to send a text message from an app.
TelephonyKit.sms.sendMms: Sends a multimedia message. Use it to send a picture or other media message from your app.
TelephonyKit.sms.sendShortMessage: Sends a text or data SMS message, splitting it into parts if it is too long. Use it to send a text message from an app.
TelephonyKit.sms.setCBConfig: Turns cell broadcast messages on or off. Use it to enable or disable emergency and public alert messages on the phone.
TelephonyKit.sms.setCBConfigList: Turns cell broadcast on using a list of settings. Use it to enable public alert messages for chosen channels or areas.
TelephonyKit.sms.setDefaultSmsSlotId: Sets which SIM card is used by default for sending text messages. Use it to choose the SIM for sending an SMS.
TelephonyKit.sms.setSmscAddr: Sets the message center address for a chosen SIM card. Use it to configure where text messages are sent through.
TelephonyKit.sms.splitMessage: Splits a long text message into several parts. Use it to send a text message longer than one message allows.
TelephonyKit.sms.updateSimMessage: Updates a text message stored on a SIM card. Use it to change or correct a message saved on the SIM.
TelephonyKit.vcard.exportVCard: Exports contact data to a vcf file. Use it to save or back up contacts as a vcf file.
TelephonyKit.vcard.importVCard: Imports contacts from a specified vcf file. Use it to add contacts from a vcf file into a contact account.
TestKit.By.clickable: Specifies the clickable attribute of a target component for filtering and matching components. Use it to find components that can be clicked in a UI test.
TestKit.By.enabled: Specifies the enabled attribute of a target component for filtering and matching components. Use it to find components that are enabled in a UI test.
TestKit.By.focused: Matches UI components by whether they are focused. Use it to find the component that currently has focus, such as the text box a user is typing in.
TestKit.By.id: Matches UI components by their ID. Use it to find a specific component on screen when you know its ID.
TestKit.By.isAfter: Matches a component that sits after another given component. Use it to find a component positioned later in the layout than a known one.
TestKit.By.isBefore: Matches a component that sits before another given component. Use it to find a component positioned earlier in the layout than a known one.
TestKit.By.key: Matches UI components by their key attribute. Use it to find a specific component on screen when you know its key.
TestKit.By.scrollable: Matches UI components by whether they can be scrolled. Use it to find scrollable areas such as lists or pages you can swipe through.
TestKit.By.selected: Finds UI components by whether they are selected, matching selected or unselected ones. Use it to locate a chosen item, like a selected tab or checkbox, in a test.
TestKit.By.text: Finds UI components by their displayed text, with several matching patterns available. Use it to locate a button or label by the words shown on screen.
TestKit.Component.clearText: Clears the text inside an editable text component. Use it to empty a text box or input field before typing something new.
TestKit.Component.click: Clicks a UI component. Use it to press a button or tap an item on screen.
TestKit.Component.doubleClick: Double-clicks a UI component. Use it to open or activate an item that responds to a double tap.
TestKit.Component.dragTo: Drags one UI component onto another target component. Use it to move an item to a new place on screen.
TestKit.Component.getBounds: Gets the position and size of a component on screen. Use it to find where a button or other item is before tapping it.
TestKit.Component.getBoundsCenter: Gets the center point of a component on screen. Use it to find the exact spot to tap when clicking a button or item.
TestKit.Component.getDescription: Gets the description text of a component. Use it to read what a screen item is for when checking or identifying it.
TestKit.Component.getDisplayId: Gets the ID of the display showing the component. Use it to tell which screen a component is on when several displays are connected.
TestKit.Component.getHint: Gets the hint text shown for a component. Use it to read the guidance a field or button gives before you type or tap.
TestKit.Component.getId: Gets the ID of a component. Use it to identify a specific screen item when finding or tapping it.
TestKit.Component.getOriginalText: Gets the text shown by a component, even when its accessibility level hides it from normal text reading. Use it to read the label or content of a UI element during a test.
TestKit.Component.getText: Gets the text information of a component. Use it to read the label or content shown by a UI element during a test.
TestKit.Component.getType: Gets the type of a component. Use it to find out what kind of UI element something is during a test.
TestKit.Component.inputText: Clears an editable text field and types the given text into it. Use it to fill in a text box or search field during a test.
TestKit.Component.isCheckable: Tells whether a component can be checked, like a checkbox or toggle. Use it to find out if a UI element can be selected during a test.
TestKit.Component.isChecked: Tells whether a component is currently checked. Use it to see if a checkbox or toggle is selected during a test.
TestKit.Component.isClickable: Checks whether a component can be clicked. Use it to find out if a button or item on screen will respond to a tap.
TestKit.Component.isEnabled: Checks whether a component is enabled. Use it to tell if a button or control is active or greyed out before tapping it.
TestKit.Component.isFocused: Checks whether a component currently has focus. Use it to see which on-screen item is selected for typing or keyboard input.
TestKit.Component.isLongClickable: Checks whether a component can be long-pressed. Use it to find out if holding down an item opens a menu or extra options.
TestKit.Component.isScrollable: Checks whether a component can be scrolled. Use it to tell if a list or page can be swiped to see more content.
TestKit.Component.isSelected: Checks whether a component is selected. Use it to see if a checkbox, tab, or list item is currently chosen.
TestKit.Component.longClick: Presses and holds on a component on the screen. Use it to test or automate a long press, such as opening a context menu.
TestKit.Component.pinchIn: Pinches in on a component to zoom out, using a scale between 0 and 1. Use it to test or automate a zoom-out gesture on the screen.
TestKit.Component.pinchOut: Pinches out on a component to zoom in, using a scale greater than 1. Use it to test or automate a zoom-in gesture on the screen.
TestKit.Component.scrollSearch: Scrolls a scrollable component to find a target component matching given attributes. Use it to locate an item that is off-screen in a list.
TestKit.Component.scrollToBottom: Scrolls a scrollable component all the way to its bottom. Use it to reach the end of a long list or page.
TestKit.Component.scrollToTop: Scrolls a scrollable component all the way back to its top. Use it to return to the start of a long list or page.
TestKit.Driver.assertComponentExist: Checks whether a component with the given attributes is present on the current page. Use it to confirm a button, label, or other element is showing before acting on it.
TestKit.Driver.click: Clicks at a given screen position specified by x and y coordinates. Use it to tap a button or other spot on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.clickAt: Clicks at a target screen position given as a point. Use it to tap a specific spot on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.clickAtWithOptions: Clicks at a given screen position, with optional touch settings. Use it to tap a spot on the screen with a chosen touch behaviour.
TestKit.Driver.create: Creates and returns a driver object. Use it to get the entry object needed to search for components, tap, slide, or take screenshots.
TestKit.Driver.createUIEventObserver: Creates a listener for UI events. Use it to watch for user interface events happening on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.crownRotate: Rotates the crown by a number of ticks, clockwise for positive values and counterclockwise for negative ones. Use it to scroll or adjust a value with the watch crown.
TestKit.Driver.delayMs: Pauses for the given number of milliseconds. Use it to wait a moment before the next step in a test.
TestKit.Driver.doubleClick: Double-clicks at the given screen coordinates. Use it to open or zoom in on something by tapping twice.
TestKit.Driver.doubleClickAt: Double-clicks at a given point on the screen. Use it to open or zoom in on something by tapping twice.
TestKit.Driver.drag: Drags from one screen coordinate to another, optionally at a set speed. Use it to move items or scroll content across the screen.
TestKit.Driver.dragBetween: Drags from one point to another, with optional speed and press duration. Use it to move items or scroll content across the screen.
TestKit.Driver.dragBetweenWithOptions: Drags a finger across the screen from one point to another, with optional touch settings. Use it to swipe or scroll through content in a test.
TestKit.Driver.dumpLayout: Saves the current screen layout information as a JSON file in the app's sandbox directory. Use it to capture what is on screen for later inspection.
TestKit.Driver.findComponent: Searches for a single screen component matching given attributes. Use it to locate a button, text field, or other element before interacting with it.
TestKit.Driver.findComponents: Searches for all screen components matching given attributes and returns them as a list. Use it to find every matching element, such as all list items.
TestKit.Driver.findWindow: Searches for a window matching given filter attributes. Use it to locate a specific app window before working with it.
TestKit.Driver.fling: Simulates a quick fling gesture in a chosen direction and speed. Use it to flick through a list or page quickly in a test.
TestKit.Driver.getDisplayDensity: Gets how dense the pixels are on a display of the current device. Use it to find the screen density when positioning or scaling things on screen.
TestKit.Driver.getDisplayRotation: Gets how the display of the current device is rotated. Use it to find the screen orientation, such as whether the screen is sideways or upright.
TestKit.Driver.getDisplaySize: Gets the width and height of a display on the current device. Use it to find the screen size when placing or measuring things on screen.
TestKit.Driver.injectKnucklePointerActio: Simulates a multi-point knuckle scrolling gesture on the screen. Use it to test knuckle scrolling through content.
TestKit.Driver.injectMultiPointerAction: Simulates a multi-finger touch gesture on the device. Use it to test pinch, zoom, or other multi-finger gestures.
TestKit.Driver.injectPenPointerAction: Simulates a continuous single-finger pen stroke on the screen. Use it to test drawing or writing with a stylus.
TestKit.Driver.inputText: Types text at a chosen spot on the screen without erasing what is already there. Use it to fill in a text box or search field during an automated test.
TestKit.Driver.isComponentPresentWhenDra: Drags from one point to another and reports whether the target component is there. Use it to check that dragging makes something appear.
TestKit.Driver.isComponentPresentWhenLon: Presses and holds a point on the screen and reports whether the target component is there. Use it to check that a long press brings up something.
TestKit.Driver.isComponentPresentWhenSwi: Swipes from one point to another and reports whether the target component is there. Use it to check that swiping reveals something.
TestKit.Driver.knuckleKnock: Simulates knuckle knocks on the screen, once or twice. Use it to test knuckle-knock gestures like taking a screenshot.
TestKit.Driver.longClick: Long-presses the screen at the given x and y coordinates. Use it to simulate a long press on a spot in the UI during automated tests.
TestKit.Driver.longClickAt: Presses and holds a point on the screen for a set time. Use it to test long-press actions such as opening a menu.
TestKit.Driver.longClickAtWithOptions: Presses and holds on a chosen spot on the screen, with optional touch settings. Use it to long-press an item at a given position.
TestKit.Driver.mouseClick: Clicks a mouse button at chosen screen coordinates, optionally while holding a key such as Ctrl. Use it to click or Ctrl-click at a spot on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.mouseDoubleClick: Double-clicks a mouse button at chosen screen coordinates, optionally while holding a key such as Ctrl. Use it to double-click at a spot on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.mouseDrag: Drags the mouse from one point to another, with an optional speed. Use it to drag the mouse across the screen.
TestKit.Driver.mouseDragWithOptions: Holds the left mouse button and drags between two points, with optional touch and key settings. Use it to drag the mouse across the screen.
TestKit.Driver.mouseLongClick: Presses and holds a mouse button at chosen screen coordinates, optionally with a key held. Use it to long-press with the mouse at a spot on the screen.
TestKit.Driver.mouseMoveTo: Moves the mouse cursor to a chosen point on the screen. Use it to position the pointer before clicking or hovering over something.
TestKit.Driver.mouseMoveWithTrack: Moves the mouse pointer from one point to another, optionally at a set speed. Use it to drag the pointer across the screen like a real mouse movement.
TestKit.Driver.mouseScroll: Scrolls the mouse wheel at a chosen spot, optionally while holding a key such as Ctrl. Use it to scroll a page or zoom with the wheel.
TestKit.Driver.penClick: Simulates a single pen tap at a chosen point. Use it to tap on screen as if with a stylus.
TestKit.Driver.penDoubleClick: Simulates a double pen tap at a chosen point. Use it to double-tap on screen as if with a stylus.
TestKit.Driver.penLongClick: Simulates a long pen press at a chosen point, with optional pressure. Use it to press and hold on screen as if with a stylus.
TestKit.Driver.penSwipe: Simulates a pen swipe from one point to another on the screen. Use it to draw or drag with a stylus in tests.
TestKit.Driver.pressBack: Presses the Back button on the screen. Use it to go back to the previous screen.
TestKit.Driver.pressHome: Returns to the home screen. Use it to go back to the home screen.
TestKit.Driver.screenCap: Captures the screen and saves it as a PNG image to a path. Use it to take a screenshot.
TestKit.Driver.screenCapture: Captures an area of the screen and saves it as a PNG image to a path. Use it to take a screenshot of part of the screen.
TestKit.Driver.setDisplayRotation: Sets the display rotation of the current scene. Use it to rotate the screen.
TestKit.Driver.setDisplayRotationEnabled: Turns screen rotation on or off. Use it to lock the screen in place or allow it to rotate during a test.
TestKit.Driver.swipe: Swipes from one point on the screen to another. Use it to scroll a page or move a slider by dragging.
TestKit.Driver.swipeBetween: Swipes from one point to another on the same screen. Use it to scroll or drag across the screen.
TestKit.Driver.swipeBetweenWithOptions: Swipes between two points on the screen with extra touch settings. Use it to scroll or drag with control over the touch.
TestKit.Driver.touchPadMultiFingerSwipe: Simulates a three- or four-finger swipe on the touchpad. Use it to trigger multi-finger touchpad gestures.
TestKit.Driver.touchPadTwoFingersScroll: Simulates a two-finger scroll on the touchpad. Use it to scroll content with a touchpad gesture.
TestKit.Driver.triggerCombineKeys: Presses a keyboard shortcut made of two or three keys together, such as Ctrl+C. Use it to send copy, paste, or other combined key presses during a test.
TestKit.Driver.triggerKey: Presses a single key on the screen, such as a letter or the back key. Use it to send one key press during a test.
TestKit.Driver.triggerPenKey: Triggers a pen key action, such as clicking or double-clicking the handwriting or air-mouse key. Use it to simulate stylus button presses during a test.
TestKit.Driver.waitForComponent: Looks for a screen element matching given attributes within a set time. Use it to wait until a button or other element appears before acting on it.
TestKit.Driver.waitForIdle: Checks whether everything on the screen has stopped changing for a set time. Use it to wait until the screen is settled before taking the next step.
TestKit.Driver.wakeUpDisplay: Turns the screen back on. Use it to wake the display before interacting with it in a test.
TestKit.ON.afterComponent: Finds a component that sits after another given component, locating it by relative position. Use it to pick out a component that comes later in the layout.
TestKit.ON.beforeComponent: Finds a component that sits before another given component, locating it by relative position. Use it to pick out a component that comes earlier in the layout.
TestKit.ON.belongingDisplay: Finds a component by the display it belongs to, given that display's id. Use it to pick out a component shown on a particular screen.
TestKit.ON.checkable: Sets whether a component can be checked. Use it to find components that can be ticked or selected.
